en: Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Goddess, the bestower of accomplishments. Śrī Bhairava said:

"Now I shall declare the ritual manual (paddhati) conjoined with the worship of Śrīvidyā, composed of both prose and verse, secret, and established by all the Āgamas. [Having performed the morning duties...]"
If one worships the Goddess with devotion,
yet lacks purity, that worship is indeed fruitless, just as a ritual act performed by one devoid of ritual purity (*śauca*). Therefore, the illustrious practitioner (*sādhaka*),
having risen from his bed during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, [should perform] the washing of hands and feet...
Having rinsed his mouth with water beginning with the *nādi* [mantra] and performed the ritual sipping (*ācamana*), he sits upon his own seat; then,

[he visualizes the deity] seated upon a lion-throne within the lunar disc located in the pericarp of a thousand-petaled white lotus facing downward, situated at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) on the crown of his head.

One's own Guru is white in color, adorned with white ornaments, his mind delighted by the bliss of knowledge; his form is the embodiment of pure consciousness and bliss (*saccidānanda*), possessing three eyes and four arms, holding the gesture of knowledge (*jñānamudrā*), a book,
and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness in his hands, while a red lotus is held in the left hand upon his left shoulder.

Meditate upon the Lord of all gods, who resembles moonstone, who is the essence of all holy fords, the supreme Śiva-nature, peaceful and gracious; he is embraced with his right arm by his beloved wife who wears ornaments, and he himself is clothed in white garments, adorned with ornaments and unguents, and decorated with pearl necklaces and other jewels.

Having visualized oneself as being completely bathed by streams of nectar flowing from the pair of your lotus feet, and having mentally worshipped with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth,
and having prostrated, [recite]: *Oṃ, of this Śrī Guru-mantra, Sanatkumāra...*
*Śiḥ* is the *paṅkti* meter (*mu*); *Śrī-Amukānandanātha* is the deity (*hṛ*); *Aiṃ* is the seed-syllable (*gu*);
*Hrīṃ* is the power (*pā*); *Śrīṃ* is the bolt (*vā*); for the sake of my *dharma*, *artha*, *kāma*, and *mokṣa*, this is the application (*sa*) in the recitation (*japa*).
Having thus remembered with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*), one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Next is the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) on the hands.
He [recites]: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ* to the two thumbs, *namas* to the heart;
*hskhphreṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā* to the head; *hsrkṣmlvyūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock; *shkhphreṃ* to the two ring fingers, *huṃ* to the armor...

CĀYAHŪṂ ŚKṢMLVRYŪṂ VAUṢAṬ to the two little fingers; VAUṢAṬ to the three eyes; HSAUṂḤ SHAUṂḤ, I worship the sandals (śrīpādukā) of [Name] Ānandanātha, the venerable [Name] woman, NAMAH with the palms and backs of the hands; PHAṬ to the weapon (astra), PHAṬ.
The six-limbed *itikara* mantra: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ha sa kha phreṃ ha sa ra kṣa ma la va yūṃ sa ha kha phreṃ sa ha ra kṣa ma la va yūṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ*.
[I worship] the venerable sandals of Śrīmacchrīsvāmipratāpakaulānandanātha and the venerable sandals of Śrīdayāvatyambā.
Having reflected ten times, "I worship; obeisance," one should mentally perform a prostration like a staff.

[One should meditate on] the Lord of all gods, who possesses the luster of the full moon within a thousand-petaled lotus, whose lotus-hands grant boons and fearlessness, who is adorned with pure fragrant flowers and excellent garments, and whose face and eyes are serene.
One should meditate on the Guru, who is formless yet possesses the name "He who rides upon the Swan" (*Haṃsaga*), preceded by that very appellation; he is white, adorned with white unguents,
garlands, and garments, his face serene, bestowing the gestures of fearlessness and boons with his two hands, and embraced with great passion by his beloved, who holds a red lotus in her left hand.

Having meditated thus: "I bow to that supreme Śambhu, whose nature is the Guru, who resides upon my head, whose eyes are like red lotuses," and having worshipped the Guru with mental offerings (mānasopacāra), [one offers]:
*Laṃ*—scent consisting of the element of earth—to the form of the venerable Guru; *Haṃ*—flowers consisting of the element of space.

To the form of the venerable Guru, [I offer] this incense (dhūpa), whose nature is wind and space; to the form of the venerable Guru, [I offer] this lamp (dīpa), whose nature is fire; to the form of the venerable Guru, [I offer] these various food offerings (naivedya), whose nature is nectar;
to the form of the venerable Guru, [I offer] this fruit, root, and betel-leaf (tāmbūla), whose nature is all-pervading. To the form of the venerable Guru...

Having worshipped with these mental offerings, saying "rtaye samarpayāmi namaḥ," one should worship [the Guru] with: "Oṃ, I bow to my own Guru, who is peaceful, manifest in the form of Śiva, seated upon the Yoga-pīṭha, for the sake of attaining the goal of liberation and desire. I salute the Śrī Guru, supreme bliss, the embodiment of bliss. (1) I salute the Śrī Guru, supreme bliss, the embodiment of bliss.

Salutations to that Guru, who is the very embodiment of one’s chosen deity; by whose mere presence even the senses (grahas) become supreme consciousness-bliss (cidānanda). Salutations to him whose nectar-like speech destroys the poison known as worldly attachment (saṃsāra).
That state, which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which the moving and unmoving world is pervaded—[to that state, salutations].

Salutations to that venerable Guru by whom [the truth] has been revealed. (4) Salutations to that venerable Guru by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance was opened with the ointment-stick of knowledge.
(5) The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is Maheśvara himself; the Guru alone is the entire universe.

Salutation to that Śrī Guru. (6) Salutation to you, O Lord, the Blessed One, Śiva in the form of the Guru, who possesses ever-new forms yet has the single form of ultimate reality, who acts as the dense mass of consciousness that dispels the darkness of all ignorance, and who has assumed manifold bodies for the sake of perfectly accomplishing the descent of knowledge. (7) Salutation to you.

Salutations to the Seizer (Graha), who is the Supreme Self, whose form is fashioned by independent compassion; who appears in a gracious form for the sake of devoted and fortunate beings who are dependent on Him; who is discernment for the discerning, reflection for those possessed of reflection, light for the luminous, and the very embodiment of knowledge for the wise. (8–10) Pu.

"I shall always offer salutation from the front, from the sides, from behind, from above, and from below, with the form of a pure mind; O Lord, grant me Your seat. (11) "By Your grace, O God, I am one who has accomplished all that was to be done;
I am liberated from the great noose of Māyā and death; I am Śiva. (12) With these mantras...
Having mentally prostrated before the venerable Guru like a staff and having contemplated him as being well-pleased, one should receive his command.

Then, within the Mūlādhāra, upon the triangular seat situated inside the Śṛṅgāṭa-pīṭha at the center of the pericarp of the four-petalled lotus of golden hue, one should contemplate the Supreme Power, Kuṇḍalinī.

She who has the form of a serpent with her face turned upward, possessing three and a half coils; whose radiance is like a thousand rising suns, resembling ten million flashes of lightning; subtler than a strand of lotus fiber; whose body consists of the fifty letters and whose nature is the thirty-eight *kalās*; she who is the abode of the three abodes and the life-force of all living beings.

Having visualized the Goddess who is supreme over all gods and the mother of all mantras as being asleep, one should awaken her with consciousness through the innate *nāda* according to the path taught by the Guru. Then, upon the four petals— namely, *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* (4),
*ṃ śaṃ namaḥ* (4), *ṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ* (4), and *ṃ saṃ namaḥ*— and in the center with the root mantra (*mūla*).

Having first worshipped according to the right-hand tradition (*dakṣiṇācāra*), and having led [the consciousness] from one lotus to another by means of the mantra "Haṃsaḥ," one then leads it to the six-petaled lotus, which is the color of coral, at the base of the *liṅga* in the *svādhiṣṭhāna*.
There, one worships with: (4) *ṃ vaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ bhaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ maṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ yaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ raṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ laṃ na*.

Having worshipped [the syllable] *maḥ* in the center of the petals with the root-mantra (*mūla*), one should then lead her by means of the *maṇipūraka* to the ten-petaled lotus in the navel, which is blue in color. There, one worships: (4) *ṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ taṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ thaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ daṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ dhaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ naṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃ paṃ*.

Having worshipped with "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Phaṃ Namaḥ" on the petals and with the root mantra in the center, one should then lead her to the twelve-petaled lotus of the *anāhata* cakra in the chest, which is of a tawny (*piṅgala*) color, and there [worship] with: "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Kaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Khaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Gaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Ghaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Caṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ Chaṃ Namaḥ," "Namaḥ (4) Ṃ..."

Having worshipped on the petals with "jaṃ namaḥ" (4), "ṃ jhaṃ namaḥ" (4), "ṃ ñaṃ namaḥ" (4), "ṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ" (4), and "ṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ," and having worshipped in the center with the root mantra, one should then lead [the consciousness] to the sixteen-petaled lotus at the Viśuddhi-cakra in the throat, which is smoke-colored, and there [worship] with "ṃ aṃ namaḥ" (4),
"ṃ āṃ namaḥ" (4), "ṃ iṃ namaḥ" (4), "ṃ īṃ namaḥ" (4), and "ṃ uṃ namaḥ" (4).
(4) ṃūṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃṛṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃṝ namaḥ, (4) ṃḷṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃḹṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃeṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃaiṃ namaḥ,

(4) ṃoṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃauṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃaṃ namaḥ, (4) ṃaḥ namaḥ— having thus worshipped [these] on the petals and in the center with the root mantra, one should then [worship] her in the *ājñācakra* between the eyebrows, within the two-petaled lotus that is the color of lightning.
Having led [the consciousness] there, one should worship with "Oṃ haṃ namaḥ," "Oṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ" on the petals, and in the center with the root mantra. Then,

having caused it to reach the thousand-petaled lotus situated at the *brahmarandhra*, and having brought about its unification there with the Supreme Śiva, who consists of light in the form of the *bindu*, [one should contemplate] that which flows from the Supreme...
Having satisfied her with the deceased [nectar], and having contemplated absorption (*laya*) for a moment while intent on hearing the *nāda*,

he then brings that Kuṇḍalinī to the Ājñācakra— the two-petaled lotus colored like lightning— by means of the mantra "I am He" (*so'ham*). There, [he places] (4) *ṃ haṃ namaḥ* and (4) *ṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ* upon the petals.

Having worshipped [the deity] with the *mūla-mantra* between the eyebrows, one should then bring it down to the throat—the seat of purification—which is smoke-colored and possesses a sixteen-petaled lotus.

There, one should recite: (4) *ṃaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃāṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃiṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃīṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃuṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃūṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃṛṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃṝ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃḷṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃḹṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ṃeṃ*.

Having worshipped with *namaḥ* (4) *maṃ namaḥ*, (4) *oṃ namaḥ*, (4) *auṃ namaḥ*, (4) *aṃ namaḥ*, and (4) *aḥ namaḥ* upon the petals and with the root mantra in the center, one should then bring [the deity] to the twelve-petaled lotus of the *anāhata* cakra in the heart, which is of a golden-yellow color (*piṅgala-varṇa*), and there [worship] with (4) *kaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *khaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *gaṃ namaḥ*, (4) *ghaṃ*...

*Namaḥ* (4) *ṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ caṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ chaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ jaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ jhaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ ñaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped on the petals and in the center with the root mantra, one should then bring her to the ten-petaled lotus of blue color at the *maṇipūra* in the navel, and there [worship] with *ṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* (4) *ṃ ḍhaṃ na...*

*Maṃ namaḥ*, *ṃñaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃṭaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃthaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃdaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃdhaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃnaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃpaṃ namaḥ*, *ṃphaṃ namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped on the petals and in the center with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), one should then bring her to the six-petaled lotus at the base of the *liṅga* in the *svādhiṣṭhāna* cakra, which is the color of coral, and there [worship] with *ṃvaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃbhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃmaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃyaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃraṃ namaḥ*. *ṃlaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃvaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃśaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃsaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃāṃ namaḥ*. *ṃiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃīṃ namaḥ*. *ṃuṃ namaḥ*. *ṃūṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṛṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṝṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḷṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḹṃ namaḥ*. *ṃeṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃoṃ namaḥ*. *ṃauṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaḥ namaḥ*. *ṃkaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃgaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃghaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṅaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃcaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃchaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃjaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃjhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃñaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṭaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṭhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḍaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḍhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṇaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃtaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃthaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃdaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃdhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃnaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃpaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃphaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃbaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃbhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃmaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃyaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃraṃ namaḥ*. *ṃlaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃvaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃśaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃsaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃāṃ namaḥ*. *ṃiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃīṃ namaḥ*. *ṃuṃ namaḥ*. *ṃūṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṛṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṝṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḷṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḹṃ namaḥ*. *ṃeṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃoṃ namaḥ*. *ṃauṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaḥ namaḥ*. *ṃkaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃgaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃghaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṅaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃcaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃchaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃjaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃjhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃñaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṭaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṭhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḍaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḍhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṇaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃtaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃthaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃdaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃdhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃnaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃpaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃphaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃbaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃbhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃmaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃyaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃraṃ namaḥ*. *ṃlaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃvaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃśaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃsaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkṣaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃāṃ namaḥ*. *ṃiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃīṃ namaḥ*. *ṃuṃ namaḥ*. *ṃūṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṛṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṝṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḷṃ namaḥ*. *ṃḹṃ namaḥ*. *ṃeṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaiṃ namaḥ*. *ṃoṃ namaḥ*. *ṃauṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃaḥ namaḥ*. *ṃkaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃkhaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃgaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃghaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃṅaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃcaṃ namaḥ*. *ṃchaṃ
Having worshipped with "Bhaṃ namaḥ" (4), "Maṃ namaḥ" (4), "Yaṃ namaḥ" (4), "Raṃ namaḥ" (4), and "Laṃ namaḥ" on the petals, in the center, and at the base,
one should then bring her down to the four-petaled lotus of golden color in the *mūlādhāra* and establish her there.
Then, in that *mūlādhāra*, [one worships] with "Vaṃ namaḥ" (4), "Śaṃ namaḥ" (4), and "Ṣaṃ namaḥ" (4).

(4) One should worship her with the root-mantra at the shoulders. Thus, having meditated upon the supreme power Kuṇḍalinī according to the sequence of ascent and descent— shining forth at the first departure,
ending in nectar even at the time of return, and moving along the internal path in the form of bliss— one should worship her.
"I take refuge in Pārvatī; I am not this [body], nor is there another besides me; I am Brahman alone, not a partaker of sorrow.

I am of the nature of Being-Consciousness-Bliss. Thus one should contemplate one’s own Self. With the *hṛdaya-mantra*, one should meditate upon dissolution. One should visualize the circle of fire at the *mūlādhāra*, consisting of ten digits (*kalās*).

Having visualized the first *kūṭa* of the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), known as *Vāgbhava*, which is radiant like a flashing streak of lightning and possesses a crest of sound reaching as far as the *Anāhata* [cakra], and having meditated upon the solar disc consisting of twelve digits within the *Anāhata*, one should [visualize] the *Kāma* [kūṭa] of the root-mantra in its center.

Having meditated upon the second peak-syllable called *rājya*, which resembles the rising sun, possesses ten flames reaching to the limits of its command, and has rays extending upward; and having visualized within that command a lunar disc consisting of sixteen digits (*kalās*), one should [visualize] therein the power-peak (*śakti-kūṭa*) of the root-mantra.
Having meditated upon the third section, which has the luster of the moon and reaches as far as the upper sphere within the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*),
and then having meditated upon the Root Mantra (*mūlavidyā*) from the Mūlādhāra up to the *brahmarandhra*—
blazing with light like a thousand rising suns, undivided— one should [meditate] upon that...

Having meditated upon one’s own body as pervaded by that light, and having visualized the Supreme Goddess, who is transformed by that radiance, within the lotus of the heart, one should worship her with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*). Then, offering fragrance consisting of the element of earth (*laṃ*):
"I offer *namaḥ* to the sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī. [Then] *haṃ* [the element of] space...

Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, accept this flower consisting of the nature of *śa* (earth); Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, accept this incense consisting of the nature of *ya* (air); Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, accept this lamp consisting of the nature of *raṃ* (fire); Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, accept these various food offerings (*naivedya*) consisting of the nature of *vaṃ* (nectar); Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, accept this... consisting of the nature of *saṃ* (water).
I offer this fruit, betel-leaf, and so forth, which consist of the essence of the *Ṛgveda*, to the *Śrīpādukā* of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī;

*namaḥ*. One should perform three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) as follows: the practitioner, having assumed a prescribed posture such as the lotus-posture (*padmāsana*), should fix his mental activity upon the root-center (*mūlādhāra*) and recite either the root-mantra or the *praṇava*.

Reciting [the mantra] sixteen times while blocking the right nostril with the right thumb, one should fill in the air through the left. Then, reciting that same [mantra] sixty-four times while likewise blocking the left nostril with the right ring finger and little finger, one should [retain] the air with both.
Then, while reciting that same [mantra] thirty-two times, one should retain that very [air], likewise block the left nostril, and fill the breath through the right;
this is one *prāṇāyāma*.
This same process performed in reverse is the second. The third is like the first. Thus, in this manner, there is a triad of *prāṇāyāmas*.

Having contemplated one's own body as worthy for the propitiation of the deity, with all impurities entirely dispelled, one should perform the recollection of the *ṛṣi* and other elements as follows: first, regarding this mantra of Śrī Mahāgaṇapati—of this mantra of Śrī Mahāgaṇapati, the venerable Brahmā is the *ṛṣi* (śi), the *gāyatrī* is the meter (mu), and [Śrī Mahā... [is the deity].

Gaṇapati is the deity (hṛ); *gaṃ* is the seed-syllable (gu); *hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*, pā); *namaḥ* is the bolt (*kīlaka*, nā). For the sake of attaining the fruit of the four aims of life and for the sake of accomplishing the grace of Gaṇapati, this is the application (*viniyoga*, sa) in recitation. Thus ends the ritual placement of the seer and so forth (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): *oṃ gāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ* to the heart.

Yāya namaḥ to the two index fingers, svāhā to the head, svāhā; gūṃ to the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ; gaiṃ to the two ring fingers, huṃ to the armor, huṃ; gauṃ to the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ; gaḥ to the palms and backs of the hands, phaṭ. a.

[Recite] *strāyaphaṭ* for the six-limbed protection (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Then, one should meditate upon Śrī Mahāgaṇapati within the lotus of one’s own heart. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): *Oṃ*, [I meditate on the Lord] with the face of an elephant, inconceivable, with sharp tusks, three eyes, and a large belly; infinite, bearing a row of teeth, and holding in his four hands an axe, a water-pot, and a pair of lotuses.
I worship Śrī Gaṇeśa, who is seated upon the pair of Viṇḍu and Hari. Now, the Gāyatrī mantra:
*Tatpuruṣāya vidmahe, Vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi, tan no Dantiḥ pracodayāt*.
Having worshipped Him with mental offerings (*mānasopacāra*), the mantra is: *Hrīṃ Gaṃ Hrīṃ Gaṇapataye Namaḥ*.

Taking the rosary with the *tīma* mantra and performing the recitation (*japa*) according to one's capacity, one should offer the fruit of the recitation— which consists of radiant light— to the left hand of the deity with the words "guhyātiguhyam" (the secret of secrets), and bow down with the *yonimudrā*. Then,
having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the *Śrībhairava* mantra, [one should proceed] with this *Śrīkāme*...

For the mantra of Śvarabhairava: Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (śiras), Paṅkti is the meter (mukha), Śrī Kāmeśvara is the deity (hṛdaya), Śrīṃ is the seed-syllable (guhya), Hrīṃ is the power (pāda), Klīṃ is the bolt (nābhi); its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation (*japa*) for the sake of attaining the success of the Śrīvidyā mantra (sarva). Thus is the ritual placement of the seer and others (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

Aiṃ to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*, to the heart, *namaḥ*; Klīṃ to the two index fingers, *svāhā*, to the head, *svāhā*; Sauṃḥ to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*, to the tuft (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*; Aiṃ to the two ring fingers, *huṃ*, to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; Klīṃ to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*, to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; Sauṃḥ to the [two] hands.
With the palms and backs of the hands [reciting] *phaṭ astrāya phaṭ*, this is the six-limbed ritual for the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga*). One should meditate upon Śrī Parabhairava as follows:

Now, the meditation: "I worship Śiva, who possesses the luster of ten million suns, who bears the moon upon his crest, who has three eyes, and who holds a noose, a goad, a bow, and arrows. Having thus meditated, one should perform the *māna*...

Having worshipped with ritual services (*sopacāra*), one should then recite the *gāyatrī*: *oṃ kāmeśvarāya vidmahe śaktīśvarāya dhīmahi tanno ātmā pracodayāt* (3). Then the mantra: *aṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ kāmeśvarāya namaḥ*. Again, [one should perform] the breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and the assignment of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth for the six limbs (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga*).

Having performed the *gaṇyāsas* with the *yonimudrā*, reciting "guhyātiguhye," one should offer the fruit of the recitation (*japa*) to the hand of the deity and prostrate; [then state]: "Of this King of Mantras, the Śrī Mahātripurasundarī-mantra-rāja, the Seer (*ṛṣi*) is Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, and the Meter (*chandas*) is Paṅkti."

The *chaṃdas* is Śrī Mahātripurasundarī-devatā (hṛ); *aiṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, is the *bīja* (gu); *sauṃḥ*, the third *kūṭa*, is the *śakti* (pā); *klīṃ*, the second *kūṭa*, is the *kīlaka* (nā). The application (*viniyoga*) is for my attainment of the four aims (*caturvarga-siddhi*) during recitation (*japa*). Thus ends the ritual placement of the seer and others (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

*Aiṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Klīṃ*, the second *kūṭa*, to the two index fingers, *svāhā*; to the head, *svāhā*. *Sauṃḥ*, the third *kūṭa*, to the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*; to the tuft (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*. *Aiṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, to the two ring fingers, *huṃ*. *Ka*...
*Vacāya huṃ klīṃ*, the second *kūṭa*, with the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; *netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*;

*sauṃḥ*, the third *kūṭa*, with the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*; *astrāya phaṭ*. Thus is the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the hands. Then, one should meditate upon the Śrī Devī as non-different from oneself within the lotus of one's own heart.

Thus, having meditated upon her with the mental offerings—[worshipping] Kāmeśvarī, who is the embodiment of Śiva and Śakti, who holds in her beautiful arms the bow, arrow, goad, and noose made of kāśa grass, and who possesses eyes like the sun, moon, and fire, and a complexion as radiant as refined gold; and who bears a crescent moon upon her brow—I worship her in my heart. Having thus meditated, [one performs] the mental offerings...

Having worshipped with the *cāras*, one should perform the mantra-consecration (*mantra-saṃskāra*). Therein, one should recite three times for the purpose of unbolting (*utkīlana*): *sakalahrīṃ namaḥ hasakahalahrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ*. *Sañjīvana* (revitalization) is performed with: *hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hasa(-) kahalahrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ*. That is the root; [the seed-syllable] *thaṃ*.
*Daṃ dhaṃ naṃ*—thus [is] the *kauṭilya* mantra; *aiṃ sauṃḥ klīṃ rudraśāpaṃ mocaya (2) phaṭ svāhā*.
This is the *śāpaharī-vidyā*, recited ten times. *Aiṃ sauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kurukullāyai svāhā*. Thus [is] Kurukullā, recited ten times. *Aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ tripureśi bhagavati...*

Recite *tisrāhā* ten times at the crown of the head (*mūrdhan*) for the *kullaka*; *oṃ* ten times at the heart (*hṛd*) for the *setu*; *hrīṃ* ten times in the *viśuddha* [cakra] for the *mahāsetu*; *oṃ aṃ mūlaṃ aiṃ aṃ* (50); and *oṃ* ten times in the *maṇipūra* for the *nirvāṇa*. First: *namaḥ tripurāstrāya daha daha* (2); second: *duritaṃ hana hana* (2).

Then, recite the *asumant* mantra three times: *kīlāntṛtīyaṃ tripurīṃ svāhā*. Next, recite the *Śrīṣoḍaśī* ten times. Then the *Gāyatrī*: *aiṃ prathamakūṭaṃ tripure devi vidmahe*, *klīṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ kāmeśvari dhīmahi*, *sauṃḥ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ tannaḥ śaktiḥ pracodayāt*.

Then, having meditated upon Śrī Mahātripurasundarī as non-different from oneself in the center of the pericarp of the heart-lotus— reciting: "I worship the auspicious Goddess who possesses the luster of ten million suns, who has four arms and three eyes, and who holds a noose, a goad, a bow, and arrows"— [one should meditate upon] Śrī Kāmeśvara...
Having recited the *Rava-mantra* ten times (*daśadhā*), one should recite "Oṃ mūlaṃ oṃ" seven times for the purpose of warding off the two types of impurity (*aśauca*).

Then, [one should recite] over the rosary: "Oṃ māṃ māle māle mahāmāle, you whose nature is the embodiment of all powers (*sarva-śakti-svarūpiṇī*), the four aims of life (*catur-varga*) are entrusted to you; therefore, be the bestower of success upon me. Thus, [one should consecrate] the rosary.

Having placed [the rosary] in the *makara* [position], worship the rosary with sandalwood paste and other offerings while reciting "Oṃ Siddhyai Namaḥ. Then, taking the rosary in the right hand while reciting "Gaṃ, O Rosary, grant me freedom from obstacles," place one's own Guru upon one's head, the yellow-colored Root-Vidyā in the throat, the Śrī Paradevatā in the heart, and the Śrī Guru...

Having meditated upon one's own self within the two feet and having contemplated the unity of these four at the center of the eyebrows, one should bring the fourfold [elements] unified as the imperishable (akṣara) into the Viśuddhi [cakra]; then,
fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose, or closing the eyes, or bringing the tongue down to touch the teeth with the teeth—

Without causing pain [to the teeth], having formed a seal with the lips, with a steady mind and steady senses, one should always meditate on the Goddess in the heart and perform the recitation (japa) in silence. Having performed the recitation according to one's capacity, at the conclusion of the recitation, one should say: "O Rosary (mālā), you who grant pleasure to all the gods and are considered a bestower of auspiciousness; O auspicious one, bring me good fortune."

Having placed the garland "Yaśovīryaṃ ca sarvadā" upon one's own head, and having again performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), the selection of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and others, and the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*), one should recite the mantra of the venerable Lord ten times (*daśadhā*).
Then, with "Oṃ guhyāti... [and so forth], one should offer the fruit of the recitation, which is of the nature of radiant energy (*tejas*), into the left hand of the venerable Goddess.

Having offered [the rosary] with the *yonimudrā*, one should prostrate. Having worshipped the rosary with the root mantra, one should place the rosary in a secret location with this mantra: "Oṃ, in the morning I bow to the lotus feet of the Mother of the worlds, the venerable Tripurasundarī, who is saluted by Śiva and the other gods. (1) In the morning, [I bow to] Tripurasundarī...

I bow to the lotus feet of Tripurasundarī, by whose grace Hari, Hara, and Viriñci perform the acts of creation and the rest, just as they do now. (2) I bow to the lotus feet of Tripurasundarī in the morning, the water used for washing which appears upon the head of Maheśvara as the Gaṅgā. (3) In the morning, [I bow to her] who holds the noose, the goad, the arrow, and the bow...

I bow to the glorious Tripurasundarī, who resembles the rising sun. (4) In the morning, I bow to her lotus feet, by which this world shines; by her grace, that [world] ceases to exist. (5) The person who recites these five verses daily in the morning—

To her one should offer one's own state [of being], thinking: "O Śrī Tripurasundarī. Thus, having remembered the form of the Guru and having mentally bowed to the Goddess, one should offer one's own actions: *Oṃ prātaḥ prabhṛti sāyāntaṃ sāyādiprātarantataḥ / yat karomi jaganmātas tad...* (Oṃ, from morning until evening, and from evening until morning, whatever I do, O Mother of the World, that...)

Having offered this hymn of praise and worship, for the sake of performing one's own duties, [one should pray]: "Oṃ! O Goddess of the Gods, Śrī Sundarī, whose very essence is the consciousness of the three worlds, by the command of Your feet alone, having risen at dawn, I shall follow the course of worldly existence for the sake of Your pleasure. While following the course of worldly existence..."

O Śrī Tripurā, Supreme Goddess, by your command, O Mother, may rivalry, contempt, strife, negligence, and fear not overcome me. I know what is dharma, yet I have no inclination toward it; I know what is adharma, yet I do not desist from it; for I am directed by you, O Hṛṣīkeśī, who abide within my heart.

"I shall act accordingly"— having thus requested the command of the Goddess, one should offer to the deities beginning with Gaṇapati, who reside from the root [of the body] up to the twelve-spoked wheel, the *ajapā-japa* known through the guru’s instruction as spontaneously accomplished (*sahajasiddha*). *Oṃ adya...* [etc.]

The *ajapā-japa*, consisting of inhalation and exhalation performed throughout the day and night on the preceding day, numbering twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths, [is to be contemplated] within the four-petaled, six-petaled, ten-petaled, twelve-petaled, sixteen-petaled, two-petaled, and thousand-petaled lotuses located at the *mūlādhāra*,
*svādhiṣṭhāna*, *maṇipūra*, *anāhata*, *viśuddha*, *ājñā*, and *brahmarandhra* [cakras].

To Gaṇapati, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, the individual self (jīvātman), and the supreme self (paramātman)—to their respective *śrīpādukās* situated upon the eight-petaled, ten-petaled, twelve-petaled, two-petaled, and thousand-petaled lotuses, which possess the colors of gold, coral, blue, tawny, smoke-colored, lightning, and variegated—[I offer] as follows: (Note: The phrase "yathā-" indicates that the specific ritual offerings or mantras follow.)

"I shall offer [this] part by part"—having thus formed this resolve with palms joined in *añjali*, one should offer it. Just as the breath goes out with the letter *ha* and enters again with the letter *sa*, the individual soul (*jīva*) constantly recites the mantra "Haṃsa, Haṃsa. [One should offer it] properly into the support (*ādhāra*) which is endowed with the syllables *va-śa-ṣa-sa-da-la*.

One should meditate upon Gaṇeśa, the primordial form, who is youthful, red-limbed, elephant-faced, with hands granting fearlessness and boons, and holding a bow, a noose, and a goad in his pair of infinite hands. One should chant the Gāyatrī mantra:
*Gāṃ tatpuruṣāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi tanno dantī pracodayāt*.
Yāt (3) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I offer six hundred ajapa-japas to Gaṇapati residing in the Mūlādhāra-cakra;
obeisance (600).

[I worship] Him who is seated upon a lotus—the source of the three worlds—whose beautiful white form is fashioned from the petals marked by the letters known as Va, Bha, Ma, Ya, Ra, La, and Sa, and who grants fearlessness.
One should meditate upon the source of the universe, who possesses a pure form and holds a water-pot, a staff, and a rosary in his hands.
[We] know that Gāyatrī, whose self is the Veda; we meditate upon Hiraṇyagarbha;
may that Brahmā inspire us. (3) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to Brahmā residing in the Svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra...

"I offer six thousand recitations of the *Nṛyajapa*—*namaḥ* (6000). Thus, one should offer [the merit] to Brahmā at the Svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra. Hari, who is seated upon a lotus whose petals are fashioned from the letters beginning with *ḍa* and ending with *pha*, who possesses the luster of the sun, who is the primordial Puruṣa, the unborn Nārāyaṇa...

One should meditate upon [the Lord] who holds the discus, lotus, mace, and the stainless conch; who is clad in yellow garments, adorned with the Kaustubha jewel, marked by the Śrīvatsa, and wearing shimmering golden anklets and beautiful yellow robes. One should meditate thus:
"We know Nārāyaṇa, we meditate upon Vāsudeva; may that Viṣṇu inspire us. (3)
Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I offer six thousand recitations of the *ajapā* to Viṣṇu residing in the *maṇipūraka* cakra;
*namaḥ*. (6000). Thus one should offer [the recitation] to Viṣṇu in the *maṇipūraka* cakra.
O Pārvatī, [one should worship] in the lotus whose petals are fashioned with the letters beginning with *ka* and ending with *ṭha*.

One should meditate upon the beloved [Lord] who is as radiant as the shimmering rays of ten million moons; who holds in his hands the *hāṃ* and *ṭhaṃ* syllables, which grant fearlessness to those within his sight; who wears bracelets, necklaces, armlets, pearl strings, and anklets;
and who is clothed in a hide. One should contemplate Gāyatrī: "We know the Tatpuruṣa; we meditate upon Mahādeva."

Indeed, may Rudra impel that body. (3) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! To the one residing in the Anāhata Cakra, I offer six thousand recitations of the *japa*; obeisance. Thus, one should offer [the recitation] into the Anāhata Cakra. Residing within the limbs of mortals, established as the desired, peaceful, and nectar-like mouth.

One should meditate upon that pure light, comparable to a lamp, which pervades the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings with its multitude of qualities; which is the source of the world, both manifest and unmanifest, manifold yet stainless; the sixteen-petaled lotus-bannered, the supreme Jīva. [The Gāyatrī: "We know the Swan, the Great Swan; may the Supreme Swan inspire our intellect."

May that Great Swan impel us toward that [Truth]. (3) *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, I offer one thousand repetitions of the *ajapā* mantra to the *jīvātman* residing in the Viśuddha-cakra; *namaḥ*. (1000). Thus, one should offer the *jīvātman* into the Viśuddha-cakra. [The *jīvātman*] is fashioned by the two syllables *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ*.

One should meditate upon the pervasive and eternal Guru, who is the stainless, divine, and vast cause of the universe; who is twofold, transparent, and the abode of the body; who, by His own will alone, from that [cause], through fitness, is the sprout of the single lamp of the nature of His own place, body, and light; whose form is the manifest syllable Om. (Gāyatrī-haṃ).
We know the Haṃsa; we meditate upon the Supreme Haṃsa; may that Haṃsa, who is I, inspire us.
(3) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I offer one thousand repetitions of the *ajapā* mantra to the Supreme Self residing in the *ājñācakra*; obeisance. (1000). Thus, the Supreme Self resides in the *ājñācakra*.
One should offer salutation to the All-pervading Primordial God, who is stainless, eternally risen, partless,
whose thousand-petaled lotus is perpetually blossomed, who is adorned with the letters of the alphabet, who is eternal yet non-eternal,
the ever-full, the self-aware, the essence of true radiance, the Soul of the Universe, and formless.
In the cavity of the thunderbolt, which is pure and all-pervading according to its own will, we know Gāyatrī, who is stainless;

we meditate upon her who is without appearance. May she, who is subtle, yet both formless and multiform, inspire us. (3) Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [salutation] to the sandals of the venerable Guru, residing in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus.
"Whatever recitations I have performed, I offer this thousand-fold [of them]; *namaḥ* (1000).

Thus, one should offer [the merit] to the venerable Guru in the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasradalakamala*). If one is unable to perform this much, then from today's sunrise until the next sunrise—that is, throughout the day and night—[one should perform the recitation].

I offer this ajapā-japa, consisting of twenty-one thousand six hundred inhalations and exhalations, to the venerable sandals of the Guru situated in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus located in the *brahmarandhra*; obeisance to the venerable Guru.
Having offered the recitation of the *ajapā* with the words "vesamarpayet," and having made a formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*),

one should perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) by means of the *ajapā-mantra*, and then perform the resolve as follows: "Oṃ, of this King of Mantras, the Śrī Ajapā Gāyatrī, Haṃsa is the Seer (Ṛṣi), the Unmanifest is the Metre (Chandas)..."

The *ṛṣi* is Trichandas (the head), the *devatā* is Paramahaṃsa (the heart), the *bīja* is Haṃ (the secret place), the *śakti* is Saḥ (the feet), the *kīlaka* is So'haṃ (the navel), the *tattva* is Oṃkāra (the heart), the location is the station of the sky (the root), the color is golden (the whole body), and the accent is Udātta (the head). The application (*viniyoga*) is for my liberation during the recitation (*japa*). This is the ritual placement of the *ṛṣi* and others. Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*).
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsāṃ sūryātmane svāhā | To the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ*. (4) ṃ hsīṃ somātmane svāhā | To the two index fingers, *svāhā*; to the head, *svāhā*.
(4) ṃ hsūṃ nirañjanātmane svāhā | To the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*; to the tuft (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
(4) *ṃ hsaiṃ nirābhāsātmane svāhā*—to the two ring fingers, *huṃ kavacāya huṃ*.
(4) *ṃ hsauṃ anantatanuḥ sūkṣmā devī pracodayāt svāhā*—to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*. (4) *ṃ hsaḥ avyaktabodhātmane svāhā*—to the palms.
*Phaṭ* with the two palms, *astrāya phaṭ*—thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*):

"Oṃ! He whose head the wise declare to be the sky, whose navel is the atmosphere, whose eyes are the moon and sun, whose ears are the quarters, and whose feet are the earth—he is to be meditated upon as the inner self of all beings."
Having meditated upon one's own self as the nature of Virāṭ and contemplated that,

one should recite the *ajapā-mantra*— which consists of the inhalation and exhalation of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*)— twenty-five times, offer it, and then, following the path instructed by the Guru, proceed with the contemplation of the *nāda*.
Having contemplated, "I am proceeding as a mere play of consciousness, free from all limiting adjuncts whatsoever," one should, for the sake of performing one's duties, recite: "Oṃ!
O Goddess whose girdle is the ocean, whose breasts are the mountains, O Consort of Viṣṇu, salutations to you; forgive this touch of my feet."

"O Goddess, you have always been the sustainer and nourisher of all beings; by that truth, protect me and deliver me from evil, O Upholder! Having thus entreated the Earth, placing his foot upon her in accordance with his breath while reciting the root mantra at every step, may the practitioner rejoice.

Then everyone, having gone out from the house and beyond the village toward the southwest or the south direction, having crossed a distance of one arrow-shot (śara-kṣepa), should cover the ground with leaves or grass while reciting the mantra "moṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ svāhā," and then discard their waste and so forth. Glauṃ pṛthivī...

One should perform purification with clay and other materials using the mantra *vyenamaḥ*. Having gone there for the discharge of excrement and urine, the practitioner should then drive away all evil spirits with the following:
"May the Ṛṣis, gods, Piśācas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Pitṛs, and all hosts of Bhūtas depart."

Having recited the *Ṛṣyamalamocana* mantra and performed three *tāla*-claps toward Śiva, one should face north and cover one's head with earth. Wearing the sacred thread (*brahmasūtra*) over the ear, one should perform the evacuation of waste.
Having discharged urine and feces, one should then go elsewhere to cleanse oneself with earth.
Taking one part from the three-fold division [of the earth], and having carefully taken earth in the measure of a large *āmalaka* fruit,
one should diligently perform purification until the odor and the smear are removed:
once for the penis, three times for the anus, and ten times with the left hand for both hands.
"Recite [the mantra] three times over each foot; this is the rule for purification. Now follows the rule for cleaning the teeth:

O Śivā, one should perform three mouthfuls of water using the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*, and thereafter, on days other than those forbidden, one should clean the teeth with a twig. O Goddess, [avoid] the sixth, the new moon, and the first day of the lunar fortnight when cleaning the teeth."

O beloved Vanaspati, may you grant us that [wood] which is free from mango, campaka, jambū, kāpāmārga, and other such trees, and which measures eighteen or twelve finger-breadths; grant us longevity, strength, fame, splendor, progeny, cattle, wealth, Vedic knowledge, wisdom, and intelligence. Through this wood...
Having requested space and taken the tooth-stick, O Śivā, one should break it with the mantra *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ taḍit svāhā*.
Then, having cleansed the teeth with the mantra *oṃ klīṃ kāmadevāya sarvajanapriyāya namaḥ*,
and having scraped the tongue with the *vāgbhava* [syllable *aiṃ*], one should wash the tooth-stick.

In a pure place in the southwest, one should cast away the tooth-stick; having washed the mouth with the root-mantra and sipped water three times, O Śivā, one should further perform the ritual sipping (ācamana) three times with the following:
"The first peak-syllable for the Ātma-tattva, svāhā! The second peak-syllable for the Vidya-tattva, svāhā! The third peak-syllable for the Śiva-tattva, svāhā! Having thus sipped water three times.

Having removed the floral offerings (*nirmālya*) from the deity’s place, one should then proceed to bathe in a river; this is the rule for the morning rites. Now, the rule for bathing: one should purify the clay by consecrating it with the *astra-mantra* and sprinkling it with that same [mantra], O Śivā; having purified it with the *śikhā-mantra*, one should [proceed] with the root mantra (*mūla*).
One should consecrate one piece [of the powder] with mantras and cast it into the water while reciting the Astra-mantra;

one should smear another piece from the head down to the navel while reciting the Mūla-mantra, and smear the remainder from the feet up to the navel while reciting the Mūla-mantra. Then, having entered water reaching up to the navel, one should perform the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) according to one's own tradition.

Having performed the non-Vedic ritual bath according to the prescribed method, standing in water reaching up to the navel, one should say: "Om, today, on this lunar day of such-and-such a month, in such-and-such a fortnight, on the lunar day of such-and-such a number, in such-and-such a sacred field, I, [Name] Śarmā, for the sake of pleasing the Supreme Deity, [perform] the Tantric..."

Having made the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) with water mixed with *kuśa* grass and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) using the vessel for offerings (*arghapātra*) and so forth, saying "I shall perform the bath," and having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands and other parts of the body using one's own root mantra (*mūlamantra*).
Then, having demarcated a square bathing place (*tīrtha*) in the water in front of oneself measuring one cubit, [one should proceed with] the three...

Having drawn a corner-wheel (*koṇacakra*), one should pray to the Sun for the holy waters (*tīrtha*) from the interior of the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*): "O Lord of Gods, by that truth that the holy waters have been touched by the rays of the Sun, O Divākara, grant me the holy waters.
Having thus petitioned the Sun, and having entered the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) with the *kroṃ* syllable and the goad-gesture (*aṅkuśamudrā*), [one recites]: *oṃ gaṅge ca yamune caiva go...*
"O Sarasvatī of the Dāvarī, O Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī, establish your presence in this water!

O beautiful Goddess, I invoke you here for the sake of bathing; come, O Gaṅgā, salutations to you who are endowed with all sacred fords (tīrthas). Having thus drawn the sacred water from the solar orb, [he places it] before him as prepared.
Having again joined the Tīrtha with the solar orb, one should invoke the Tīrtha-śakti with the mantra: *oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ sarvānandamayī tīrthaśakti ehyehi svāhā*.
Then, one should meditate upon that Tīrtha-śakti within that Tīrtha-maṇḍala, [visualizing her] as *oṃ* Sarvānandamayī, who destroys all sins...

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the three principles (*tattva*) thus: "Oṃ, obeisance to the self of the second peak-syllable, the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*); Oṃ, obeisance to the self of the third peak-syllable, the principle of Śiva (*śiva-tattva*"); and having visualized the *Śrīcakra* therein, one should invoke the Goddess from the heart-lotus, perform the ritual of unification (*sakalīkaraṇa*) by means of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), and [recite] "Oṃ Hrīṃ."

"O Śrī Tripurā Devī, accompanied by your retinue, I bathe you in this sacred water; O you whose form is the mantra, salutations to you! Having bathed her along with her attendants with this mantra, one should consecrate that water eight times with the root mantra while employing the *yoni-mudrā*, and then, preceded by the remembrance of the deity therein, [perform] three...
Emerging again and again from the *kumbhamudrā*, one should consecrate one’s own head three times with the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*).

Having gratified the venerable Goddess (*śrīdevī*) with the root mantra, one should bring the Goddess into one’s own heart. (4) *Oṃ* first *kūṭa*, I purify the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*), svāhā. (4) *Oṃ* second *kūṭa*, I purify the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*).
*Yāmi svāhā*. (4) *Aṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ śivatattvaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā*.

Having thus rinsed the mouth three times, having meditated there according to the rule, having performed the ritual of personification (*sakalīkaraṇa*), and having mentally worshipped, one should invoke the deity with the *kuṃbha-mudrā* and sprinkle [the disciple] three times; [then] the seven apertures, beginning with the ears...
Having restrained the breath and emerged from the water, one should apply the *tripuṇḍra* mark on the forehead with the root mantra using clay;

one should purify it with water eight times while reciting the root mantra. Then, having satiated the Goddess three times with the root mantra, one should ascend to the bank, put on two washed garments, and complete the Vedic *saṃdhyā*, [and then] that [Goddess].
One should begin with *trikīm*. This is the procedure for bathing (*snānavidhi*). Now, for the twilight ritual (*saṃdhyā*): *sauṃḥ sakalahrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*.

Having cast water in the four directions of oneself with this weapon-mantra (*astramantra*) and having meditated upon a wall of fire (*vahni-prākāra*), the yogi Śivānanda, according to the *Ūrdhvaśruti*, [performed] the *pūrṇā*.
In the practice associated with consecration (*abhiṣeka*), the Great Twilight (*mahāsaṃdhyā*) is prescribed. The Twilight is to be known as fourfold:
the Child (*bālā*), the Youth (*kaumāra*), the Maiden (*yauvanā*), and the Mature (*prauḍhā*), as well as the Formless (*niṣkalā*); thus the Goddess Saṃdhyā is proclaimed.
At the time of dawn, O Mahādevī, she is Vidyā and Vāgīśvarī; at midday, she is Kāmeśvarī.

Tripureśvarī is to be known as being at the time of evening, and Mahādevī Tripurasundarī at midnight. One who has omitted the [proper] twilight worship (saṃdhyā) should perform the ritual of the preceding twilight during the [time of] another twilight, and then, with a concentrated mind, facing eastward, enter [the practice] by placing his feet [upon the pedestal].

One should wash the *stūpa* while reciting: "Aiṃ, the first peak-syllable, svāhā to the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*); Klīṃ, the second peak-syllable, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (*vidyātattva*); Sauṃḥ, the third peak-syllable, svāhā to the principle of Śiva (*śivatattva*).
Having thus performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) three times, one recites: "Oṃ, O Maṇidharī, O Vajriṇī, O Mahāpratisarā, protect [me]! Huṃ Phaṭ! (2)

Having tied the topknot with the mantra "Svāhā," having placed the sacred thread on the right arm with the mantra "Oṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ," and having tied the *trikhaṇḍā* (three-part) cord with the root mantra, one should perform the *prāṇāyāma*, the assignment of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth,
and the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). Then, in front of oneself, [one should visualize] that which has been formed in the same manner by means of the *dhenumudrā*.

Having rendered the water of the sacred ford (*tīrtha*) into nectar (*amṛta*) by consecrating it eight times with the root mantra, one should sprinkle one's own head with that water using the *tattvamudrā* while reciting the letters of the Mātṛkā from *aṃ namaḥ* up to the letter *kṣa*. Then,
having sprinkled it three times with the root mantra, one should take water in the right hand, cover it with the left hand, and [recite] *laṃ*.
Having consecrated [the water] seven times with the *pāñcabhautika* mantras— pronouncing "Vaṃ Raṃ Yaṃ Haṃ"— and having consecrated it three times with the root mantra (*mūla*),

one should sprinkle one's own head three times with drops of that water using the *tattvamudrā* formed with the left hand while reciting the root mantra; then, placing the remaining water in the left hand, [one should contemplate it as] being of the nature of light.

Having drawn [the impurity] out with the *lamiḍa* [mantra], one should wash all the defilements situated within one's own body; then, visualizing that water as black in color and exiting through the *piṅgalā* [nāḍī], one should take it in the right hand, meditate upon a blazing vajra-stone in one's left part, and [recite]: *oṃ ślīṃ paśu hūṃ phaṭ*.

Having struck that stone with the mantra of the *pāśupatāstra* weapon and washed his hands, he takes water with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), visualizes it as having become one with the supreme nectar (*paramāmṛta*) of the thousand-petaled lotus through the flowing channel (*pravahannāḍī*), and [offers it] by means of that water exiting [the mouth] with the mantra: *amṛtamālinyaisvāhā*.

Having sprinkled one's own head three times with *kuśa* grass while reciting the mantra: (4) *Oṃ prathamakūṭam ātmatattvaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā* (4); (4) *Oṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ vidyātattvaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā* (4); (4) *Oṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ śivatattvaṃ śodhayāmi svāhā*. Again: (4) *Oṃ tṛtīyaṃ śiva-ta...*

(4) *ṃ* I purify the *tattva* of *Vidyā*, svāhā. (4) *ṃ* I purify the first *kūṭa*, the *ātmatattva*, svāhā. (4) *ṃ* I purify the entire root, the *sarvatattva*, svāhā. Having thus sipped water three times—that is, having sipped water nine times with [the water]—

Yellow in color, wearing yellow garments, adorned with yellow garlands, ornaments, and unguents, possessing a luster equal to ten million flashes of lightning, and blazing like the stainless morning sun—having thus risen at the morning twilight, one should offer water with the hollowed palms while reciting:
"Aiṃ, we know Vāgīśvarī as the first; Ktīṃ, we meditate upon Kāmā as the second."
*Śvaridhīmahi sauṃḥ; may that Śakti inspire us.* Having offered the *arghya* three times with "To the *śrīpādukā* of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, this *arghya*, svāhā," [one then offers:
*Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ, this *arghya* for the venerable Sūrya, svāhā; aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ mā...*

Having offered the *arghya* to Kulasūrya with the mantra: "To Rtaṇḍabhairava, together with the power of illumination (*prakāśa-śakti*), accompanied by his retinue of planets, zodiac signs, lunar mansions, yogas, and karaṇas— this *arghya*, svāhā!"—
one should satisfy the Goddess of the Root [Mantra] three times and satisfy Śrīsūrya three times, first at the *mūlādhāra*.

Having meditated [on the energy] from the base of the *kūṭa* up to the *brahmarandhra*, having invoked her into the circle of fire situated in space, and having meditated there upon Bālā Vāgīśvarī with this [mantra]: "O Goddess Tripurā, we know thee; O Vāgīśvarī, we meditate upon thee; may that liberation impel us," one should [worship] with this root-mantra (*mūla*).

Having offered the *arghya* three times, having satiated [the deity] three times, and having prostrated to the venerable Guru, one should perform *prāṇāyāma*, followed by the assignment (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth upon the hands and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Then, having recited the previously mentioned root *Gāyatrī* and also the first *kūṭa*, and having recited the root mantra according to one's capacity, one performs the *prāṇāyāmas*.

Having offered the daily recitation (*japa*) to the Goddess, one should release the Root Goddess from the solar orb (*sūryamaṇḍala*) into one’s own heart, and Vāgīśvarī, together with her *kūṭa*, from the fire orb (*vahnimaṇḍala*) into the *mūlādhāra*. Then, having prostrated before the venerable Guru—this is the procedure for the morning twilight (*prātaḥsaṃdhyā*). Now follows the midday twilight (*madhyāhnasaṃdhyā*). [The morning] breaths...
Having performed the rites from the *yāma* [offering] up to the *sūryatarpaṇa* (libation to the sun) in the morning just as in the *prātaḥsaṃdhyā*, one should perform the *bījasandhyā*.

Therein, at midday, while meditating on the second *kūṭa* of the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) in the *anāhatacakra* as being red in color, one should invoke its radiance into the solar orb outside and, therein, into Kāmeśvara...

Having meditated at midday upon Kāmeśvarī— red in color, adorned with red garments and ornaments, holding a noose, a goad, and displaying the gestures of granting fearlessness and boons, possessing a pure smile, endowed with formidable youth,
and three-eyed— one should contemplate her, O Goddess Tripurā, with the syllable *klīṃ*.

Having offered *arghya* to the Goddess with this mantra: "We know her, we meditate upon the Mistress of Desire; may she, the Wet One, impel us," one should recite this [mantra] according to one's capacity, recite the fourth root *gāyatrī* three times, and also recite the second *kūṭa* of the root [mantra] according to one's capacity.

Having offered the recitation preceded by *prāṇāyāma* and other rites, having prostrated to the Root Goddess Kāmeśvarī and dismissed her into one's own heart, and having prostrated to the Śrī Guru—this concludes the midday *saṃdhyā*.
Now follows the evening *saṃdhyā*; therein, from *prāṇāyāma* and so forth up to the libation (*tarpaṇa*) to the Sun, as in the morning [rite].
Having performed the ritual of the twilight (saṃdhyā) in the same manner as before, one should perform the seed-sandhyā (bīja-saṃdhyā). Therein, at evening,

having invoked the third syllable (kūṭa) of the root-mantra (mūla-vidyā), which is as pure as clear crystal, into the lunar orb situated in the sky within the Command Wheel (ājñā-cakra), one should [worship] the mature Amṛteśvarī there.
Having meditated upon her, white-clad, adorned with white garments, unguents, garlands, and ornaments,

wearing a mass of matted locks, her lotus-face radiant with three eyes, possessing slightly protruding fangs, assuming a terrifying form, covered with the grey of old age, with breasts hanging down— pā...

Having meditated thus in the evening upon her who holds a goad, a noose, a book, and a crystal rosary in her hands, who arises from the seed-syllable *Śakti* (Śrīṃ), and who resides within the orb of the full moon—one should offer the *arghya* with this mantra: "O Goddess Tripurā, we meditate upon thee; O Sovereign of Power, may we contemplate thee; may that Immortal One inspire us. Thus, one should present the *arghya*.

Having recited this fourth Gāyatrī and the Gāyatrī [mantra] according to one's ability, as well as the third *kūṭa* and the root-vidyā, and having offered the recitation preceded by *prāṇāyāma* and other rites, one should bring the Root Goddess from the lunar orb (*somamaṇḍala*) into the heart, and Amṛteśvarī into the *ājñā-cakra*.

Having prostrated before the Śrī Guru, thus concludes the evening *saṃdhyā*. Now follows the midnight *saṃdhyā*: there, without the meditation on the Goddess within the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*), one should perform the rites from *prāṇāyāma* up to *ācamana* as previously described;
then, [one should meditate] upon the fourth seed-syllable in the *sahasrāra*, which consists of the thirteen syllables of the root-vidyā.
Having meditated on [the deity] with the luster of five rubies, having invoked Tārā into the external maṇḍala,

and having meditated there upon the Blessed Lady in her previously described form, one should offer the *arghya* to the Root Goddess there with the fourth *gāyatrī* together with the fourth seed-syllable; [this fourth syllable] consists of thirteen letters.

Having recited the *kūṭa*, and having recited the fourth *gāyatrī* and the root-vidyā as much as one is able, and having offered the recitation (*japa*), one should dismiss the goddess of the fourth state into the thousand-petaled lotus in the heart of one's own Goddess; then, having prostrated before the venerable Guru, one should meditate upon oneself in the form of the *kāmakalā*. Thus ends the [Fourth].

This is the procedure for meditation. This fourfold twilight ritual (*saṃdhyācatuṣṭaya*) must necessarily be performed; alternatively, all four may be performed in the morning alone. One should not abandon the morning twilight ritual alone;
having omitted the auspicious seat (*śivāsana*), the bath, and the twilight ritual, one should mutter [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.

Thus ends the procedure for the twilight rites (*saṃdhyā-vidhi*). Now follows the procedure for libation (*tarpaṇa-vidhi*): having sipped water as before, O Goddess, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*), followed by the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth, and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) on the hands.
Thereafter, having ascended to the sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*) as before and having visualized nectar with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), [one should proceed].

In that water, O Śivā, the master of the sādhaka, having meditated upon the yantra, should then invoke the Goddess from his own heart along with her retinue. Having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa and paramīkaraṇa by means of the six limbs,
he should satisfy the deities of the retinue with nectar through the application of the kuṇḍalinī, as follows.

May Kāmīśvarī-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Bhagamālinī-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Nityaklinnā-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Bhīruṇḍā-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Vahnivāsinī-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Vajreśvarī-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Śivadūtī-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Tvaritā-nityā be eternally satisfied; may Kulasundarī-nityā be eternally satisfied.
Nityānityā (0), Nīlapatākānityā (0), Vijayānityā (0), Sarvamaṅgalānityā (0), Jvālāmukhyānityā (0), Citrānityā (0), Tripurānityā (0).
Para-prakāśānandanātha (tṛ), Paraśivānandanātha (tṛ), Paraśakti.
May the goddess Ambā be satisfied; may Kuleśvarānandanātha be satisfied; may Kuleśvarānandanātha be satisfied;
may the goddess Kāmeśvarī be satisfied; may the goddess Śuklā be satisfied; may the Guru of the Divine Current (divyaugha) be satisfied;
may Bhoṭṭānandanātha be satisfied; may Klinnānandanātha be satisfied; may Samayānandanātha be satisfied.

Sahajānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Siddhaughaguru, may you be satisfied; Gaganānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Viśvānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Vimalānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Sadānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Bhuvanānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Līlānandanātha, may you be satisfied; Svātmānanda...

May Danātha be satisfied; may Priyānandanātha be satisfied; may Mānavaughaguru Śrīmacchrīsvāmipratāpakaulānandanātha be satisfied; may the supreme guru be satisfied; may the higher-and-lower guru be satisfied;
may the supreme-perfecting guru be satisfied; may the power of the heart of the Omniscient One be eternally satisfied.

May the power of the head, Tṛptā, be satisfied; may the power of the crest-lock, Anādibodhā, be satisfied; may the power of the armor, Svatantratā, be satisfied; may the power of the eye, Nityamaluptā, be satisfied; may the power of the weapon, Anantā, be satisfied; may the perfection of atomization (aṇimā-siddhi) be satisfied; may the perfection of levitation (laghimā-siddhi) be satisfied; may the perfection of magnitude (mahimā-siddhi) be satisfied.

May the accomplishment of sovereignty be satisfied; may the accomplishment of mastery be satisfied; may the accomplishment of irresistible will be satisfied; may the accomplishment of enjoyment be satisfied; may the accomplishment of desire be satisfied; may the accomplishment of attainment be satisfied; may the accomplishment that grants all desires be satisfied;
may Brahmī be satisfied; may Māheśvarī be satisfied; may Kaumārī be satisfied; may Vaiṣṇavī be satisfied.

Salutation to Vārāhī; salutation to Indrāṇī; salutation to Cāmuṇḍā; salutation to Mahālakṣmī; salutation to the mudrā that agitates all; salutation to the mudrā that subdues all; salutation to the mudrā that attracts all;
salutation to the mudrā that brings all under control; salutation to the mudrā that intoxicates all; salutation to the Great Goad Mudrā.

[The goddesses] who bestow the *khecarīmudrā*, [the goddesses] who bestow the *bījamudrā*, [the goddesses] who bestow the *yonimudrā*, [the goddesses] who bestow the *trikhaṇḍāmudrā*; [the goddesses who are] the eternal digits (*nityakalā*) of Kāmākarṣiṇī, [the goddesses who are] the eternal digits of Buddhyākarṣiṇī,
[the goddesses who are] the eternal digits of Ahaṃkārākarṣiṇī, [the goddesses who are] the [eternal digits] of Śabdākarṣiṇī.

The eternal digit Sparshakarshini (the Attractor of Touch) is satisfied; the eternal digit Rupakarshini (the Attractor of Form) is satisfied; the eternal digit Rasakarshini (the Attractor of Taste) is satisfied; the eternal digit Gandhakarshini (the Attractor of Scent) is satisfied;
the eternal digit Chittakarshini (the Attractor of Mind) is satisfied; the eternal digit Dhairyakarshini (the Attractor of Fortitude) is satisfied.

The eternal digit (kalā) that attracts memory; the eternal digit that attracts names; the eternal digit that attracts seeds; the eternal digit that attracts the self; the eternal digit that attracts nectar.
May Śarīrākarṣiṇī Nityākalā be satisfied; may Anaṅgakusumā be satisfied; may Anaṅgamekhalā be satisfied; may Anaṅgamadanā be satisfied; may Anaṅgamadanāturā be satisfied;
may Anaṅgarekhā be satisfied; may Anaṅgaveginī be satisfied; may Anaṅgāṅkuśā be satisfied; may Anaṅga... [be satisfied].

Mālinī-tṛ (0) Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvavidrāviṇī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvākarṣiṇī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvāhlādinī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvasaṃmohinī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvastambhinī-śakti-tṛ (0) Sarvajṛmbhiṇī-śakti-tṛ (0) ... [Sarvajṛmbhiṇī-śakti] ...
Salutations to the power that brings all under control; salutations to the power that delights all; salutations to the power that intoxicates all;

salutations to the power that accomplishes all aims; salutations to the power that bestows all prosperity; salutations to the power consisting of all mantras; salutations to the power that destroys all dualities.
Homage to the goddess who bestows all accomplishments; homage to the goddess who bestows all prosperity; homage to the goddess who makes all dear;

homage to the goddess who brings about all auspiciousness; homage to the goddess who grants all desires; homage to the goddess who liberates from all suffering; homage to the goddess who pacifies all death.

O Goddess who destroys all obstacles; O Goddess beautiful in every limb; O Goddess who bestows all good fortune; O Goddess who is omniscient; O Goddess who possesses all powers; O Goddess who grants all prosperity; O Goddess whose nature is all-knowledge; O Goddess who destroys all diseases.

Salutations to the Goddess who is the support of all; salutations to the Goddess whose nature is the foundation of all; salutations to the Goddess who removes all sins; salutations to the Goddess who consists of all bliss; salutations to the Goddess whose nature is the protection of all; salutations to the Goddess who bestows the fruits of all desires; salutations to the Goddess of Speech, Vaśinī; salutations to the Goddess of Speech, Kāmeśvarī.

Salutations to the goddess of speech Stṛmohinī; salutations to the goddess of speech Vimalā; salutations to the goddess of speech Aruṇā; salutations to the goddess of speech Jayinī; salutations to the goddess of speech Sarveśvarī; salutations to the goddess of speech Kaulinī; salutations to the arrow-goddess Jṛmbhaṇakāmeśvarī; [salutations to] Jṛmbhaṇa.

Salutation to the deities of the arrows of Kāmeśvarī; salutation to the deities of the bow of Mohana-Kāmeśvara; salutation to the deities of the bow of Mohana-Kāmeśvarī; salutation to the deities of the noose of Vaśīkaraṇa-Kāmeśvara;
salutation to the deities of the noose of Vaśīkaraṇa-Kāmeśvarī; [salutation to the deities of the goad] of Staṃbhana-Kāme...
Salutation to the goddess Śvarāṅkuśa; salutation to the goddess Stambhanakāmeśvary-aṅkuśa;

salutation to the goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī, the power of Rudra consisting of the power of will (icchā-śakti); salutation to the goddess Śrī Vajreśvarī, the power of Viṣṇu consisting of the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti); [salutation to the goddess] consisting of the power of action (kriyā-śakti).

O Goddess Bhagamālinī, the power of Brahmā; O Great Power, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman; O Sovereign of all mantras; O Sovereign of the entire universe; O Sovereign of all sacred seats (pīṭhas);
O Sovereign of all heroes (vīras); O Sovereign of all yogas; O Sovereign of all speech.
Salutations to the Sovereign Lady of All Siddhis; salutations to the venerable Goddess Mahāṣoḍaśī; salutations to Indra-śakti;
salutations to Agni-śakti; salutations to Yama-śakti; salutations to Nairṛti-śakti; salutations to Varuṇa-śakti;
salutations to Vāyu-śakti; salutations to Soma-śakti; salutations to Īśāna-śakti; salutations to Brahma-śakti.

May the one with infinite power be satisfied; may the one with vajra-power be satisfied; may the one with spear-power be satisfied; may the one with staff-power be satisfied; may the one with sword-power be satisfied; may the one with noose-power be satisfied; may the one with banner-power be satisfied;

may the one with hook-power be satisfied; may the one with mace-power be satisfied; may the one with trident-power be satisfied; may the one with lotus-power be satisfied; may the one with wheel-power be satisfied.

Having thus gratified the attendant deities with *kṣititṛ*, one should satisfy the venerable *Śrī-Āmukānandanātha-śrīgurupādukā* in the northeast (*aiśāna*), the venerable *Paramaguru-śrīpādukā* in the southeast (*vahni*), the venerable *Parameṣṭhigurū-śrīpādukā* in the southwest (*nairṛtya*), and [the venerable *Svagurū-śrīpādukā*] in the northwest (*vāyavya*).

Having offered libations to the supreme teacher, the venerable guru’s sandals (śrīpādukā), and the sacred bathing place (tīrtha), and having dismissed them to their respective abodes, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* and other preliminaries, offer the recitation (*japa*), and establish the venerable Goddess within one's own heart.
This is the procedure for the libation (*tarpaṇa*). Then, having risen, [one should recite]: *oṃ vajrodakena huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

Taking a water-pot filled with water, reciting "Oṃ hrīḥ, pacify all sins; remove all conceptual constructions, hūṃ," he should wash his hands and feet. Remaining silent and recollecting the root mantra, he enters the house of the deity and, according to the sequence to be described, [prepares] with the water for the general *argha* offering.

One should worship the deities of those gates: (4) *Oṃ sudhārṇavacatuṣṭayāya namaḥ*. (With *aṃ āṃ* and so forth, ending with *kṣāṃ*) (4) *Oṃ naṃdanodyānāya namaḥ*. (4) *Oṃ svarṇaprākārāya namaḥ*. Ta(-)
Above and below the right and left door-panels: on the right, (4) *Oṃ Gaṃ Gaṇapataye Namaḥ*; on the left, (4) *Oṃ Kṣaṃ Kṣetrapālāya Namaḥ*; above, (4) *Oṃ Dvaṃ Dvāraśriyai Namaḥ*;
below, (4) *Oṃ Kaṃ Kadamvakānanāya Namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ Ratnamaṇḍapa*.

Having worshipped with "Pāyanamaḥ" and "Mvārāhyai namaḥ," one should worship on the upper right branch of the door: "(4)ṃ Māṃ Mahālakṣmyai namaḥ"; on the left: "(4)ṃ Sāṃ Sarasvatyai namaḥ"; in the middle: "(4)ṃ Duṃ Durgāyai namaḥ"; and below: "(4)ṃ Dvāṃ Dvāraśriyai namaḥ. [Then worship] on the right and left of the door...
(4) To each branch, from bottom to top: *Namaḥ* (4) *ṃśaṃ* to Śaṅkhanidhi and Vasudhārā;
(4) *ṃgaṃ* to Gaṇapati; (4) *ṃkṣaṃ* to Kṣetrapāla; (4) *ṃmāṃ* to Māyā; (4) *ṃciṃ* to Cillakṣmī; (4) *ṃgaṃ* to Gaṅgā; (4) *ṃyaṃ* to Yamunā; (4) *ṃdhāṃ*.
(4) *Oṃ* *dhātryai* namaḥ; (4) *Oṃ* *viṃ* *vidhātryai* namaḥ; (4) *Oṃ* *dāṃ* *dehalyai* namaḥ—at the front of the door.

(4) *Oṃ* *vaṃ* *varuṇāya* namaḥ—at the northern upper branch of the western door. Having worshipped as before from Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī up to the threshold, [one worships] in the middle: (4) *Oṃ* *vaṃ*.
*Vaṭukāya namaḥ* (4). *Dvāṃ dvāraśriyai namaḥ* (4). *Saṃ somāya namaḥ* at the eastern gate (4).
*Laṃ indrāya namaḥ* (4). *Klīṃ glauṃ gaṇanāthāya namaḥ* (4). *Dvāṃ dvāraśriyai namaḥ*.
Then, having sprinkled with water for the *argha* offering at the front of the southern gate, [worship] Mahālakṣmī.

Having worshipped [the deities] from Sarasvatī, Gaṇanātha, and the Door-Lord Śrī Śaṅkhanidhi up to the threshold, [reciting] "OṂ ṬAṂ, obeisance to Yama," one goes again to the western door [reciting] "OṂ RAṂ, obeisance to the row of jewel-steps.
Having ascended them, [one recites]: "AIṂ, obeisance to the Blessed One, O Māheśvarī, [who severs] the minds of ignorant beings..."

Having worshipped with the mantra: *Kṣutiraskaraṇaṃ kurukuru svāhā, tiraskaraṇīṃ śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*, and having meditated thus: "I take refuge in the western door, the great abode of Bhavānī, which is guarded by Indra and the other guardians and resplendent with supreme sovereignty."
Salutation to the jeweled pavilion at the western gate. In front of the western gate, slightly outside, and in front of those [deities]:
(4) *ṃ gauṃ*—I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Goddess Gaurī. (4) *ṃ loṃ*—I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Goddess Lokadhātrī.
(4) *ṃ vāṃ*—I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Goddess Vāgīśvarī. Then, in that very place: (4) *ṃ diṃ*.

*Pū* (0) *jaṃ* Divine Current (*divyaugha*) Śrīpādukā; *pū* (0) *siṃ* Siddha Current (*siddhaugha*) Śrīpādukā; *pū* (0) *māṃ* Human Current (*mānavaugha*) Śrīpādukā. Then, having gone to the northern door and sprinkled [water] in the same manner: *pū* (0) *māṃ* Māyā Śrīpādukā; *pū* (0) *duṃ* Durgā Śrīpādukā. Then again, as before, Gaurī and the others.

Then, as before, perform worship on the right and left sides of the door: (4) *ṃ bhaṃ* to Bhadrakālī, worship the *śrīpādukā*; (0) (4) *ṃ svaṃ* to Svasti, worship the *śrīpādukā*. Then, as before, [worship] Gaurī; thereafter, having gone to the southern door, on its right and left sides: (4) *ṃ svāṃ* to Svāhā.
*Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*, *Śubhaṅkarī-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*. Then, as before, [worship] Gaurī and the others.
Then, having gone to the western door and worshipped the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*), having ascended that door preceded by three *tāla*-claps, [recite]: *Oṃ nīlaturagam adhiruhya suśobhamānā nī...*

May the Blessed One, richly adorned with silken garments, ornaments, garlands, and finery, protecting the worlds with her veil of sleep and armed with the sword as her weapon, protect me from this! Then, having taken white mustard seeds, blades of kusa grass, and flowers as nārāca missiles through yogic power, I departed.

"O spirits, piśācas, pretas, guhyakas, and whoever else dwells here—those beings who stand upon this earth, depart! May those beings who cause obstacles perish by the command of Śiva! Thus [is] the weapon-mantra (astramantra).
Having sprinkled [water] inside the Ācārya-maṇḍapa and having granted passage to the obstacles that have emerged from there by contracting one's own left side, [one recites] the Astra-mantra:
"Oṃ! Those beings who cause heresy on earth, those who dwell in the intermediate space, and those who reside in the heavenly world—may they perish by the command of Śiva. Thus, with the Astra-mantra.

Having dispelled terrestrial, atmospheric, and divine obstacles with three strikes of the left heel and by means of the divine vision, one should enter the interior of the pavilion preceded by the left foot; there,
having covered the door with a cloth, one should [proceed] while ringing the bell and reciting the mantra "Hauṃ" consecrated five times.
Having sprinkled everything up to the pavilion with cow-products and water sanctified by the mantra *astrāya phaṭ*,

and having adorned the pavilion with multi-colored powders, variegated flower garlands, and canopies, and having reddened the walls, pillars, and other parts with lac, vermilion, and so forth, [one should prepare] around the altar...

Having lit lamps from a steady source and perfumed them with black aloe-wood (*kālaguru*) and other incenses, one should meditate upon that [deity] in such a manner. Then, a lamp filled with ghee should be placed on the right, and one filled with oil on the left;
a white wick on the right and a red wick on the left. Thereafter, in the south of the pavilion...
In the southeast corner: (4) Oṃ, salutation to Vāstupuruṣa. (4) Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the Lord of the Vāstu site.

In the northeast: I worship the sandals of the venerable Kulanātha; salutation. (4) Oṃ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Dīpanātha, who is of red complexion and accompanied by twelve Śaktis. Salutation.

Having worshipped Dīpanātha with "I bow," one should request his permission as follows: "In this sacred field, for the sake of unimpeded success and for the purpose of the sequential worship of the Śrīcakra, may permission be granted to me.
Having thus requested the command of Dīpanātha, [one should then worship] the deities of the door, starting from the west.

In the four directions, in the center: (4)ṃ Madhyamdūtaryai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ Sundaryai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ Sumukhyai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | Virūpāyai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ Vimalāyai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ Ataryai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ Purandaryai śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ | (4)ṃ (Note: The "4" represents the *bīja* syllable *hrīṃ*; "ṃ" represents the *bindu*. The sequence follows the standard ritual order for the eight Śaktis.)

Having thus worshipped two Śaktis on the left and right of the door, one should worship in the center with: "Oṃ Puṣpamardinyai Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi. Then [one should address] Bhairava: "O you with sharp fangs and a massive body, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon, salutations to you, O Bhairava; please grant me permission. Thus [to] Bhairava.

Having taken up the *jñānājñā* [mantra] with "phaṭ," one should go to the altar of worship (*pūjā-vedī*). Then, having sprinkled the ground with the mantra "Oṃ rakṣa huṃ phaṭ svāhā," the practitioner should sit upon seats as prescribed for Śiva—either on soft grass mats (*mṛdu-cūḍa*), or on lotuses, or seated upon ritual grass seats (*viṣṭara*). Thus seated, the practitioner...

The wise say that one who dies within six months or after a month from conception has not attained the highest perfection; they consider such a person to be "firmly fallen" (*dṛḍhacyuta*). They know one who dies before the *cūḍā* (tonsure) and *upanayana* (initiation) rites have been performed as a *vācūḍaka*. A male who has completed the *cūḍā* rite but lacks the *upanayana*, and who dies in the fifth year, they know as "tender" (*komala*).

A woolen blanket (*kaṃvala*) for the sake of desired objects, and a superior red blanket; a black antelope skin (*ajina*) for the attainment of desires; and a tiger skin for liberation and prosperity. On a seat of *kuśa* grass, there is success in mantras; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. On the bare ground, there is an increase in suffering; on a wooden seat, misfortune; on a bamboo seat, [prosperity].

One who uses a stone as a seat becomes impoverished in the teachings and afflicted by disease; one who uses a grass seat suffers loss of fame; one who uses a leaf seat suffers mental delusion; and one who uses a cloth seat suffers the loss of recitation, meditation, and austerity—one should not use these as seats. A seat made of fifty *kuśa* blades is known as a *brahmaviṣṭara*, while half of that is known as a *viṣṭara*. *Kuśa*...
The wise one should prepare a seat using exactly thirty-two leaves; then he should perform the placement of the vital breaths (*jīvanyāsa*) and practice the recitation (*japa*) upon it.
Thereafter, he should have a square measuring four cubits prepared, adorned with circles, an eight-spoked wheel, and a triangle within a circle. Upon that, he should place the seat.
Remaining fearless, entirely pure, and with his inner organ (mind) fixed upon that site, he should perform the worship. He should perform the purification of the seat as follows: *Oṃ*.
Of this mantra for the purification of the seat (*āsana-śodhana*), Meru-pṛṣṭha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Sutala is the meter (*chanda*), and Kūrma is the deity.

The deity is *Āṃ* (the seed-syllable), *Gu* (the seed-syllable), *Hrīṃ* is the power (*śakti*), *Kroṃ* is the bolt (*kīlaka*), and *Tā* is the application (*viniyoga*) for the installation of the seat (*āsana*).
Now follows the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs on the hands: *Hrīṃ Āṃ Kroṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ* to the heart; *Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ* to the two index fingers, *svāhā* to the head.
