Svāhā ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ to the two middle fingers, VAṢAṬ to the crest-lock (śikhā), VAṢAṬ; ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ to the two ring fingers, HUṂ to the armor (kavaca), HUṂ; ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ to the two little fingers, VAUṢAṬ to the three eyes, VAUṢAṬ; ĀṂ HRĪṂ KROṂ to the palms and backs of the hands.

*Bhyām phaṭ*, *astrāya phaṭ*. Now, as for the meditation: one should meditate upon Mahāviṣṇu in the form of Kūrma (the Tortoise), whose nature is the support of all. He possesses the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem; he is the cause of stability for the practitioner, intent on the destruction of the wicked, blue in color, four-armed, [holding] the conch and the discus...

One should meditate on Indirā, who wears a crown of lotuses and a forest garland, and is seated upon the back of a lion; one should contemplate the Goddess as being clad in a pair of yellow garments and joined with the two Śaktis, Drāviṇī and Bhāminī.
Having spoken thus with palms joined in reverence: "Oṃ Prīṃ! O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you..."

"O Goddess, you who are supported by Śeṣa, support me and make this seat pure. Having thus prayed to the Earth, [one should perform the following]: *māṃ hrīṃ krauṃ vyāṃ*—*namaḥ* to the tiger-skin and lion-throne.

Then, having gazed at the place of worship with the root mantra (*mūla*), sprinkled it with the weapon mantra (*astra*), and struck it three times with *kuśa* grass using the same weapon mantra, [one should protect it] with the armor mantra (*kavaca*).

Having sprinkled [it] with the mantra: *Oṃ śatābhiṣeke śatābhiṣeke hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*, and with the mantra: *Oṃ puṣpaketurājārhāya samyaksaṃbuddhāya hūṃ | Oṃ puṣpe puṣpe mahāpuṣpe supuṣpe puṣpasaṃbhave puṣpapracayākīrṇe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

Having purified the flower, one should then worship the seat with perfumes, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and flowers: (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Maṇḍūkya; (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Kālāgnirudra; (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Mūlaprakṛti;
(4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Kūrma; (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Ananta; (4) *Oṃ* obeisance to Varāha.
Oṃ namaḥ to the Earth; Oṃ namaḥ to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice; Oṃ namaḥ to the Ocean of Wine; Oṃ namaḥ to the Ocean of Clarified Butter; Oṃ namaḥ to the Ocean of Milk;
Oṃ namaḥ to the Island consisting of nine jewels, resplendent with the nine divisions beginning with the letter *a* and ending with the letter *kṣa*.

*Namaḥ* (4) *maṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ* to the Flower-Jewel; (4) *ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aṃḥ* to the Vaiḍūrya Jewel, *namaḥ*; (4) *kaṃ* (4) *khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ* to the Sapphire Jewel, *namaḥ*; (4) *caṃ* (4) *chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ* to the Coral Jewel, *namaḥ*; (4) *ṭaṃ* (4) *ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ* to the Pearl Jewel, *namaḥ*; (4) *taṃ* (04) *thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ*.
Oṃ raṃ pañcara-tanāya namaḥ. (4) Oṃ paṃ vajra-ratnāya namaḥ. (4) Oṃ yaṃ iṃ gomedaka-ratnāya namaḥ. (4) Oṃ śaṃ padmarāga-ratnāya namaḥ. (4) Oṃ svarṇa-parvatāya namaḥ.
(4) Oṃ nandana-udyānāya namaḥ. (4) Oṃ kalpa-vṛkṣebhyaḥ namaḥ. (4) Oṃ vasaṃ...

Homage to those six seasons. (4) Homage to the Great Lotus Grove. (4) Homage to the preeminent sense faculties. Homage to the elephants that are the objects of the senses. (4) Homage to the ground of variegated jewels. (4) Homage to the thousand-spoked lotus. (4) Homage to the petals composed of primordial nature (*prakṛti*).

(4) Homage to the filaments consisting of transformation (*vikṛti*). (4) Homage to the pericarp adorned with the eight seed-syllables. (4) Homage to *dhama*. (4) Homage to knowledge (*jñāna*). (4) Homage to detachment (*vairāgya*). (4) Homage to sovereignty (*aiśvarya*). (4) Homage to the base (*adharma*). (4) Homage to ignorance (*ajñāna*). (4) Homage to non-detachment (*avairāgya*).

*Namaḥ* (4) *maṃ* to Maheśvara, *namaḥ* (4) *saṃ* to Satva, *namaḥ* (4) *raṃ* to Rajas, *namaḥ* (4) *taṃ* to Tamas, *namaḥ* (4) *āṃ* to Ātman, *namaḥ* (4) *aṃ* to Antarātman, *namaḥ* (4) *paṃ* to Paramātman, *namaḥ* (4) to Jñānātman, *namaḥ* (4) to Mahiṣāsana, *namaḥ* (4) to Yoga.

Having worshipped the seat with "Oṃ, obeisance to the Pīṭha," one should sit there upon a lotus-seat or similar seat, facing either east or north. One desiring liberation (mumukṣu) should remain facing east;
one seeking worldly power (vaśyārtha), facing west; and for the purpose of killing (māraṇa), facing south; and for expulsion (uccāṭana), facing north.
Having performed the ritual of immobilization (*khostambhana*) and stationed himself facing the southwest (*nairṛta*), he should place the *Śrīcakra* upon its pedestal in front of him. Then,

taking a handful of flowers and reciting the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), he should [offer it] to the Siddhas of all the manifest, secret, more secret, *Kula*, *Kaula*, *Nigarbha*, *Rahasya*, *Parāpara-rahasya*, and *Atirahasya* [traditions].
With the mantra "Oṃ namaḥ yoginīcakrebhyaḥ," one should scatter a handful of flowers upon the Śrīcakra.
Having thus performed the worship, one should spread the seat as prescribed there, sprinkle it with water while reciting the Astra-mantra,
and worship it with "Hrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti)," located to the southeast of the seat.
(4) *Oṃ gaṃ* to Gaṇapati, in the southwest; (4) *Oṃ duṃ* to Durgā, in the northwest; (4) *Oṃ saṃ* to Sarasvatī, in the northeast;

(4) *Oṃ kṣaṃ* to Kṣetrapāla—having thus worshipped them, one should sit there upon a lotus-seat or similar seat and assume the *saṃvit* [meditative state] according to the mantra. The procedure for that will be explained further on. [The syllable] *rakta*.

Adorned with perfumes, garments, garlands, and ornaments, his mouth filled with betel, his body exquisitely scented with camphor and musk, and his person marked by necklaces and armlets— contemplating "I am Śiva"—
and having established the Śrīcakra before him according to the procedure taught by the Guru, for as long as he lives...
O beloved, [the mantra] lasts for twenty-one years on bamboo, gold, or silver; twelve years on copper;

and six months on birch bark is traditionally taught. Excluding gems, coral, and stones produced from the Gaṇḍakī river, crystal is praised for all desires and purposes at all times, provided it possesses fine lines and is richly beautiful.
One should have [the image] fashioned by an initiated artisan from any one of these materials according to one's means;

having offered a handful of flowers with the *mūla-mantra*, and having given the *bhūta-bali* to the spirits in front of oneself to the left, saying "Salutation to the spirits (*bhūtebhyo namaḥ*")— to those spirits who dwell here upon this earth, take this *bali* which has been duly offered according to the rule.
"May they seek residence elsewhere; may they forgive me; salutations to them.

(3) Having thus offered the *bhūtabali*, one should meditate on the one situated in the northern direction as having the form of a winged insect (*pakṣa*), devouring the multitude of enemies of devotees, known as the fierce-formed locust (*śalabha*). Having thus meditated:

(4) Oṃ namo bhagavate śalabha-śālva-āya pakṣi-rājāya mama śatrūn nāśaya (2) hā~ gha gha huṃ phaṭ svāhā. I worship the venerable sandals of Śrī Śalabharudra; obeisance. To its left: (4) Oṃ namo bhagavati śalabha-śāli-pakṣi...

O Rājimama, destroy my enemies! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Obeisance, I worship the sandals of the goddess Śrīśalabhī. Oṃ! [I worship] the one who has the brilliance of the sun at the end of the aeon, who fills the entire triple world with his splendor, who is red-eyed, tawny-haired, and who strikes fear into the multitude of enemies. Bhī... [end of fragment].

Meditating thus upon the primordial enemy of Mura in the form of the Discus— bearing in his arms a fierce tusk, a loud laugh, a conch, a discus, a mace, a massive club, a bow, a noose, and a goad— one should recite: *Oṃ sahasrāra huṃ phaṭ, obeisance to the glorious Sudarśana weapon*.

Thus, in the eastern direction: "I meditate upon Aghora, who is equal to a water-laden cloud, possessing terrible fangs and three eyes, holding serpents, wearing red garments and red unguents, and bearing an axe, a *ḍamaru* drum, a sword, a shield, an arrow, a noose, a trident, and a human skull. Having thus meditated:
Oṃ hrīṃ sphura (2) prasphura (2) ghora (2) tanu (2) rūpa (2) caṭa (2) pracaṭa (2) kaha (2) cama (2) bandha (2) ghātaya (2) hūṃ phaṭ! Homage to the Aghorarudra-weapon! [Thus, on the right. Oṃ!
[I bow to her] who is joined with gold, who stands in the center, who has three eyes, and who resembles a flash of lightning.

One should meditate upon the Moon-faced Goddess dwelling in the Vindhya mountains, who holds a conch, a discus, a boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness; who bears a digit of the moon; who wears a neck-ornament, a breastplate, a necklace, and earrings; who is praised by Indra and the other gods; and who has a lion standing at her side. Having thus meditated upon Vanadurgā, [recite] *oṃ u*.
"O Puruṣikī, stay! What fear has come upon me? Whether it be possible or impossible, O Blessed One, pacify that for me, Svāhā! Salutation to Śrī Durgā of the Forest.
Having thus worshipped outside in the western direction, [place] the ritual implements such as scents and so forth to one's right.

Having deposited his own family materials and so forth on his left side and having established them, while reciting "HĀṂ HĪṂ HŪṂ HAIṂ HAUṂ HAṂḤ PHAṬ," he should gaze at the flowers and other offerings with the *nārāca-mudrā* and the divine vision (*divya-dṛṣṭi*). Then, having touched with his left hand the water-filled jar situated on the left side while reciting "ĀM," [he should recite] "KṢAUṂ."

Having touched the water situated there with the tip of the right hand, saying "Raṃ," and having touched the flame of the lamp, he should wash his hands. Then, on the left [he should touch] with: (4) *Oṃ aiṃ gurupādukābhyāṃ namaḥ*;
on the right: (4) *Oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ*; and in front: (4) *Oṃ hrīṃ paradevatāyai namaḥ*. Thus, he should perform the salutation (*praṇāma*).

Having performed the *mūrdhni-saṃghaṭṭa-mudrā* at the crown of the head, [recite]: *ṃ hsauṃḥ saha kṣa ma la va ya ra āṃ sa ha kṣa ma la va yūṃ sa ha kṣa ma la va ya rīṃ hsrauṃ śrīpara-pāvaka-sarvārādhya sarva-mūrdhva-pura-nātha sarva-guru svayaṃ-guru śrī-guru-nātha raha sa ha kṣa*.
Malavayūṃ Srauṃ Sahakṣamalavayarīṃ Sahakṣamalavayūṃ Sahakṣamala vayarāṃ Śrī-Śambhu-guru-hsrauṃ Sahakṣamalavayūṃ Śrīmat-Śrī-Svāmi-Pratāpakaula-Nandanātha-Śrīpādukāṃ Śrīmat-Śrī-Dayāvaty-Ambā-Śrī.
Having placed the *śrī-guru-pādukā* on one's head with the mantra "I worship the sandals;

obeisance," and having again worshipped the venerable Guru upon one's own head with this same vidyā using perfumes and other offerings, and having displayed the five mudrās beginning with perfume, [one should recite]: "Obeisance to that Guru, the chosen deity."

Having prostrated with the gesture of salutation (*namaskāramudrā*) while reciting: "To Him whose own form is the nectar of speech which destroys the poison known as saṃsāra," and having made [the substance] fragrant by rubbing it with scented materials while reciting *maṃ āṃ sauṃḥ*, and having rubbed it with the right hand using a fragrant flower and smelled it with the left hand;
"May all those who harm me, these violent ones, be liberated [from their sins] and go to dissolution;

may death, disease, fear, and afflictions fall upon the heads of my enemies. Having recited this mantra, one should cast that flower far toward the northern direction using the *nārāca-mudrā*. Then, once again—
Having purified the hands by rubbing them against one another with the *Karaśuddhi-vidyā*, [one should recite]:

(4) *maṃ namaḥ* to the two middle fingers; (4) *māṃ namaḥ* to the two ring fingers; (4) *sauṃḥ namaḥ* to the two little fingers; (4) *aṃ namaḥ* to the two thumbs; (4) *āṃ namaḥ* to the two index fingers; (4) *sauṃḥ namaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) with "ṣṭhayoḥ," and having performed the three-fold pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*) from the head to the feet while reciting "ṃaiṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ namas tripurasundari māṃ rakṣa" twice, one should again utter [the mantra] and perform the binding of the ten directions (*digbandhana*) by means of three upward *tāla* slaps and the sound of the index fingers and thumbs.

Having formed three walls of fire by rotating three times around one's own head with two hands held separately in the shape of tridents, and having performed three breath-controls (prāṇāyāma), one should perform the purification of consciousness (saṃvit-śodhana). The procedure for that is as follows: between the consciousness (saṃvit) and the wine (āsava)...
Consciousness (saṃvit) is most venerable; she has become the devourer of existence, devoid of smell, and having the form of the sky.
Furthermore, O Śiva, that consciousness is said to be fourfold: the Brāhmaṇī has white flowers, the Kṣatriyā has red flowers, the Vaiśyā has yellow flowers, and the Śūdrā [has dark flowers].

With black flowers and joy, there is no falling away, and the deities are never satiated. There, one should fashion a triangle, a circle, and a square; then, upon that, having worshipped the seat with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti," one should establish the Consciousness (Saṃvid).
Having offered a handful of flowers upon that [liṅga] with the syllable *dhīḥ*, one should invoke the *saṃvid* in Śivā.

Then, preceded by the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth. *Oṃ, of this venerable Vijayā-mantra, Śiva is the seer (ṛṣi), Triṣṭubh is the metre (chandaḥ), the goddess Vijayā is the deity (devatā), and its application is in the purification of consciousness (saṃvit).*

Having meditated thus: "I bow to Śrī Vijayā, who holds in her arms the *mudrā* of command (*niyoga*), meditation (*dhyāna*), the noose (*pāśa*), the goad (*aṅkuśa*), the bow (*cāpa*), and the arrow (*bāṇa*); who bestows all desired objects; who is divine, adorned with garments and ornaments, and seated upon a lotus," one should perform the purification (*śodhana*) with the mantra *saṃvide brahma*.
O you who are not born from a womb, daughter of Brahmā, eternally sinless, be forever pure for the sake of the satisfaction of the Brāhmaṇas.
(4) *Oṃ vāhmaṇyai namaḥ svāhā*. Having purified the Vāhmī [plant] with this mantra, [one recites]:
*Oṃ siddhamūlyakṣaye devi hīnavodhaprabodhini rājaprajā...*

Having purified the Kṣatriya woman with the mantra: "O you who bring others under control, O destroyer of the enemy faction! Hail to the Kṣatriya woman! Svāhā," [the officiant should pray: "O Fire, blazing with the fuel of ignorance, O Fire whose nature is Brahman-knowledge! Grant me bliss, the goal, love, and perfect knowledge."

Having purified the Vaiśya woman with the mantra: *me hrīṃ vaiśyāyai namaḥ svāhā*, [one should purify] the Śūdra woman with the mantra: *oṃ nasyāmi namasyāmi yogamārgapradarśini trailokyavijaye mātaḥ samādhiphaladā bhava klīṃ śūdrāyai namaḥ svāhā*.
Having purified the *drāṇī*, the wise practitioner should then purify all of them with a single mantra.
Having thus consecrated [the water] with: *oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtam ākarṣaya (2) siddhiṃ dehi śrīmahātripurasundarīpādaṃ me vaśam ānaya*.

Having recited "Ya-svāhā" and the root-mantra seven times over that, one should recite the mantra of Ānandeśvara Bhairava and Bhairavī seven times. Having rendered it nectarine by means of the Dhenu-mudrā, having displayed the Yoni-mudrā, having veiled it with "Huṃ," and having protected it with "Phaṭ," one should recite the root-mantra: "Come! Be present! (twice).

"Be present! Be fully restrained! Manifest before me! Accept this worship accompanied by all ritual services! Svāhā! Having thus displayed the mudrās for invocation and so forth, [one should perform] the three-fold [protection] by means of the triple *tāla* [clap], divine vision, and three strikes with the left heel.

Having dispelled obstacles with snapping sounds (*choṭikā*) and performed the binding of the ten directions with the syllable *phaṭ*, one should first satisfy Ānandeśvara and Bhairavī three times at the center of the eyebrows using the *tattvamudrā* formed with the left hand;
then, one should satisfy one’s own guru three times at the crown of the head. One’s own...

Having fully gratified the Supreme Deity within the heart, one should perform the acceptance of consciousness (*saṃvitsvīkāra*) as follows: with the mantra "Aiṃ vada vāgvādini mama jihvāgre sthirībhava sarvasattvavaśaṅkari svāhā," one should offer oblation into the mouth. Then, becoming composed of bliss, [one should perform] the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).

One should perform [the ritual] as follows: Oṃ, of this great mantra of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), Puruṣa is the Ṛṣi, Devī Gāyatrī is the Chandas, Ākāśa, Vāyu, Agni, Jala, and Bhūmi are the Devas, Haṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ are the Bījas; for the purpose of purifying my body composed of the five elements, [I shall recite it] in the form of a Japa.

The application (viniyoga): Now follows the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa). *Laṃ raṃ yaṃ vaṃ huṃ atanusūkṣmaprabhedātmane aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* — *Hṛdayāya namaḥ*. *Laṃ raṃ yaṃ vaṃ haṃ avyaktaprabodhātmane tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā* — *Śirase svāhā*. *Laṃ raṃ yaṃ vaṃ...*
*Haṃ*, to the self of inconceivable power, with the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*; to the crest (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
*Laṃ raṃ yaṃ haṃ*, to the self of infinite knowledge, with the two ring fingers, *huṃ*; to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*.
*Laṃ raṃ yaṃ vaṃ haṃ*, to the self of the impenetrable armor, with the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; to the eyes...

*Yāyavauṣaṭ*, *laṃ raṃ yaṃ vaṃ haṃ*, *aluptagatyātmane karatalakarapṛṣṭhābhyāṃ phaṭ*, *astrāya phaṭ*—thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) for the hands. *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ*—thus is the binding of the directions (*digbandha*). As for the meditation (*dhyāna*): [He is] Brahmā, born of the five elements, endowed with the five kalās.

"I worship that body which is the form of Śiva, endowed with the five lights, consisting of the group of the five-fold process (pañcīkaraṇa), and composed of five-fives. This is the meditation. From the feet to the knees is the region of Earth:
square, marked by a thunderbolt, yellow in color, having Brahmā as its presiding deity, and characterized by the Nivṛtti-kalā.

Having meditated upon the locus of water (apāṃ sthāna), which is presided over by Viṣṇu, established in the *pratiṣṭhā-kalā*, marked with the seed-syllable *vaṃ*, white in color, shaped like a half-moon, adorned with two lotuses at its two tips, and extending from the knees to the navel; and having meditated upon that which is presided over by the *adhiṣṭhāna-kalā*, joined with the seed-syllable *laṃ*... [nā]...

Having meditated upon the fire-maṇḍala, extending from the navel to the throat, shaped like a triangle, red in color, presided over by Rudra, established upon the *vidyā* and *kalā* [tattvas], and joined with the seed-syllable *raṃ*; and [having meditated upon] the wind-maṇḍala,
extending from the throat to the middle of the eyebrows, shaped like a hexagon, [and] twenty-six...
Having meditated upon [the element] marked by a circle, endowed with a circular shape, black in color, having Īśvara as its presiding deity, presided over by the power of tranquility (śāntikalā),
and joined with the seed-syllable *yaṃ*; and [having meditated upon] the station of space, from the middle of the eyebrows up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*),
circular in form, marked by a banner, smoke-colored, and having Sadāśiva as its presiding deity.

Having meditated upon the lotus of one's own heart, which is presided over by the *kalā* of Śāntyatītā, joined with the seed-syllable *Haṃ*, and situated within this body composed of the five elements— its root being Dharma, its stalk Jñāna, its eight petals being the [eight] sovereign powers (*aṇimā, mahimā, laghimā, garimā, prāpti, prākāmya, īśitva, vaśitva*),
and its pericarp Supreme Detachment— one should [meditate] upon that pericarp.

Having meditated upon the individual soul (jīvātman) as being the size of the tip of a goad, radiant like the flame of a lamp, and whose true conscious nature is concealed by beginningless existence, one should raise Kuṇḍalinī from the Mūlādhāra by means of the previously described form, along the path of the Suṣumṇā from the Mūlādhāra up to the Anāhata.
Having brought [the deity] who is at the head of the presiding deities of the letters and so forth into the heart-lotus,
and meditating upon the individual soul (jīvātman) as being swallowed by her, one leads [it] through the path of the *suṣumṇā*—
passing through the presiding deities of the letters of the *viśuddhi*-cakra and the others— to the *brahmarandhra*. There, [one should contemplate:]

Having joined the individual soul (jīvātman) with the host of deities of golden hue within the light of the Supreme Self (paramātma-jyotis) situated in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus by means of the mantra "Haṃsa," and having brought Kuṇḍalinī back to her own place, one should perform the withdrawal of the elements (tattva-saṃhāra).
There, at the location of the earth, having recollected the foot-sense organ, the action of walking, the destination, the scent, the sense of smell,
the earth, Brahmā, Nivṛtti, and the Samāna wind, one should [recite] the mantra: *oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe pṛthivyadhipataye nivṛttikalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

One should withdraw them through the door of Kuṇḍalinī into the midst of the waters. Then, at the location of the waters, having meditated upon the tongue of taste (rasanā) as the water, the essence to be given, and the installation (pratiṣṭhā) of Viṣṇu through the vital breath (udāna), one should recite: "Oṃ hrīṃ, to Viṣṇu, the lord of waters, whose self is the kalā of installation, huṃ phaṭ svāhā."

One should withdraw all of them into the midst of the fire at the door of Kuṇḍalinī. Then, in the place of the fire, having recollected the eye, fire, Rudra, Vidyā, and Vyāna—whose forms are the syllables *pa*, *a*, *vi*, *sa*, *rga*, *vi*, *sa*, *rja*, *nī*, *ya*, *rū*, *pa*, *ca*, *kṣu*—one should recite: *oṃ hrūṃ rudrāya tejodhipataye vidyākalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.

One should withdraw all those [elements] into the wind-maṇḍala. Then, at the station of the wind, having recollected the worship, the object of sound, touch, the tangible, the Lord of Wind, and the peaceful apāna, one should recite: "Oṃ hraiṃ! To the Lord of Wind, the Sovereign, whose nature is the peaceful kalā, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Thus, all of them—
One should not withdraw [the elements] while they remain in the space [of the void]. Therefore, while they remain in the space, one should utter the words of speech;
having recollected the speech, sound, hearing, space, Sadāśiva, Śāntyatītā, and Prāṇa, [one recites]: *oṃ hrauṃ sadāśivāya ākāśādhipataye śāntyatītākalātmane huṃ*.

Having withdrawn all those [elements] into Kuṇḍalinī with "Phaṭ Svāhā," one should withdraw that [Kuṇḍalinī] into the Bindu-śakti; the Bindu-śakti into the Nāda-śakti; and the Nāda-śakti into the Supreme Śakti (Parama-śakti) by means of the Praṇava.
Then, with "Oṃ Hrīṃ Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā," one should withdraw that Supreme Śakti into the previously mentioned Supreme [Reality].
Having directed [the disciple], he should contemplate the Person of Sin (*pāpapuruṣa*) within the left side of the body alone, as follows:

"Oṃ! The Person of Sin situated in the left side, with the luster of lampblack, having the murder of a Brahmin for his head, the theft of gold for his two arms, the drinking of liquor joined with his heart, and the violation of the Guru’s bed..."

Having two hips, with a pair of feet attached to them, his limbs and minor members are like a fallen tree; he has secondary limbs, body hair, red beard and eyes, a downward face, black complexion, and the size of a thumb;
he is the nourisher of all the factions of the asuras and is composed of impurity.

One should visualize the sinful person as wrathful, bearing a sword and shield, with a belly protruding like that of a crow. Having thus visualized the sinful person, one should fill the air through the left nostril while reciting the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, and join it with the wind-mandala in the shape of a hexagon located at the navel; therein is the wind-seed-syllable *yam*.
Having meditated upon the black-colored [wind], while revolving the wind-seed syllable *yam* during the retention (*kumbhaka*),
one should dry up the personification of one's own sins residing within one's body by means of the great wind arisen therefrom; then,
having exhaled the wind through the right nostril, one should again [inhale] through the right nostril with the seed-syllable *ram*.

Having filled the lungs with air and joined it at the *mūlādhāra*, one should contemplate there the red-colored fire-seed syllable "Raṃ" within the circle of fire; then, by rotating the seed-syllable "Ram" during the retention (*kumbhaka*), one should burn the personification of one's own sins residing within one's body with the great fire arising from that.

Having exhaled the air through the left nostril along with the ashes of the *pāpapuruṣa*, one should again fill the air through the left nostril while reciting the seed-syllable *vaṃ*. Joining it with the air at the *brahmarandhra*,
one should meditate upon the white-colored nectar-seed-syllable *vaṃ* within the lunar disc situated there, and then perform *kumbhaka*.

While rotating the *laṃ* seed-syllable, one should visualize one's own body, drenched in ashes, being flooded by the stream of nectar situated therein; then, exhaling that air through the right nostril, one should again fill the air through the right nostril along with the *laṃ* seed-syllable, [directing it] into the earthly mandala located at the *mūlādhāra*.

Having joined "laṃ" there and meditated upon the yellow-colored seed-syllable of Earth (pṛthvībīja), one should rotate the seed-syllable "laṃ" during the retention of breath (kuṃbhaka); then, having condensed the ashes moistened by nectar through the fire produced from that [syllable],
one should exhale that air through the left nostril using the seed-syllable again.

Having filled [the body] and visualized the *māyā* seed-syllable (*māyābīja*), shining with the color of the rising sun, in the center of the drop (*bindu*) situated at the *mūlādhāra*, one should rotate that *māyā* seed-syllable during the retention (*kumbhaka*). By means of that, one should contemplate one's own body as having been fully formed, complete with hands, feet, and all other limbs; then, one should exhale that wind through the right nostril.

Having thus produced the gross body, one should produce the subtle body (*sūkṣma-śarīra*). Therein, from the presence of the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) residing in the previously mentioned thousand-petaled lotus, one should [invoke] the Supreme Power (*para-śakti*), who is the form of the Will of the Supreme Brahman manifested by the desire to create the entire universe, with the mantra: *Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ*.

Having brought [the deity] to its own place with this mantra, and having touched the power of sound (*nāda-śakti*) and then the power of the point (*bindu-śakti*) with the *praṇava*, one should then, by means of the *praṇava*, draw forth Kuṇḍalinī—from the presence of the power of the point—she who is the cause of the creation of the entire universe; thereafter: *Oṃ hrauṃ sadāśivāya ākā...*

"Obeisance to the one whose self consists of the *Īśāna* [face], the *Śāntyatītā* [kalā], and *Ākālā*. With this, one should establish the *Prāṇa-Śāntyatītā*, Sadāśiva, in the place of space—namely, the ether, the ear, sound, that which is to be spoken, speech, and the organ of speech.
Then, from the sphere of space (*ākāśamaṇḍala*), [one recites]: "Oṃ Hraiṃ! Obeisance to Īśvara, the lord of wind..."

With the mantra "Oṃ Śāntikalātmane Namaḥ," one should establish the apāna, the Lord of Peace (Śāntīśvara), the wind, the skin, touch, the tangible objects thereof, their associated bliss, and the organ of generation in the region of the wind. Then,
with the mantra "Oṃ Hrūṃ Rudrāya Tejodhipataye Vidyākalātmane Namaḥ," [one establishes] the vyāna.
One should establish the eyes, form, the visarjanīya, the visarga, the anus, fire, and the *nistiṣṭhā* [vital breath] in the *sthāna*.

Then, with the mantra: *oṃ hrīṃ viṣṇave jalādhipataye pratiṣṭhākalātmane namaḥ*, one performs the *udāna-pratiṣṭhā*; Viṣṇu is the lord of water, the tongue is the sense of taste, and the object to be given is taste.

One should not place those which are without hands or feet in their respective places. Then, with the mantra: *oṃ hrāṃ brahmaṇe pṛthivyadhipataye nivṛttikalātmane namaḥ*, one should establish Brahmā, the Earth, the sense of smell, the object of smell, the act of smelling, and the organ of smell in the location of the Earth, along with the *nivṛtti-kalā*.

Then, having established Kuṇḍalinī in her own place by means of the Praṇava, and having meditated upon the pervasion of the powers of Nāda, Bindu, and Parama-Śakti within one's own body by means of the Praṇava,
[one should perform the extraction] from the Supreme Self situated in the Brahma-randhra by means of the mantra "So 'ham" [from the Kuṇḍalinī].

Having withdrawn Kuṇḍalinī and the individual soul (jīvātman), and having brought the phonemes (varṇas) along with their presiding deities (adhidevatās) to the heart-lotus, one should establish the individual soul within the heart-lotus; then,
by means of the path of Suṣumṇā, one should [place] Kuṇḍalinī into the respective phonemes within the Maṇipūraka and other cakras.
Having established the presiding deity of the syllable *Ṛṃ* and led it to the *mūlādhāra*, one should place it there.

Then, having visualized one’s own body as free from all impurities and fit for the worship of the deity, one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*. This is the procedure for the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).

Now, the Prāṇapratiṣṭhā: Oṃ. Of this Prāṇapratiṣṭhā mantra, the seers are Śrī-Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; the meters are Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman; the deity is the Supreme Vital Power (Parā-prāṇa-śakti); the seed-syllable is ĀṂ; the power is HRĪṂ; the pin is KROṂ; [may it be for] my Śrī-prāṇa...

The application for the purpose of the *ṇa*-seat (foundation) is as follows; this is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers and so forth. Now, the ritual placement of the hands and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*):
Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Aṃ Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ, salutation to the thumbs (Āṃ) and to the heart (Namaḥ), [addressed] to the self of ether, air, fire, water, and earth. Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Iṃ...
Oṃ Caṃ Śaṃ Vaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Ṭaṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers, who are the essence of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell;
svāhā to the head. Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Uṃ Ṭaṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers, who are the essence of the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose; vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock. Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Eṃ Taṃ... (5)ṃ.
To the self consisting of speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals: *aiṃ* to the two ring fingers; *huṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*);
*huṃ*. *Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ oṃ paṃ* (5) *auṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ*.

*Kroṃ aṃ yaṃ ṃ* (9) *ṃ*, to the mind, intellect, ego, consciousness, and self; *aṃḥ*, with the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*, for the weapon, *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs of the hands. Then, from the navel to the two feet: *āṃ namaḥ*; from the heart to the navel: [continue as follows].
*Hrīṃ namaḥ* from the head to the heart; *Kroṃ namaḥ* in the center of the lotus from the heart onwards.

(4) *Āṃ yaṃ tvagātmane namaḥ* on the eastern petal; (4) *Āṃ raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ* on the western petal; (4) *Āṃ laṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ* in the southeast; (4) *Āṃ vaṃ medasātmane namaḥ* in the northwest.
(4) *ṃ śaṃ* to the self of semen, salutation to Īśāna; (4) *ṃ ṣaṃ* to the self of marrow, salutation to Nairṛta;
(4) *ṃ saṃ* to the self of semen, salutation to Uttara; (4) *ṃ haṃ* to the self of breath, salutation to Dakṣiṇa;
(4) *ṃ laṃ* to the self of life, salutation [to Vāyu]; again, in the center of the pericarp: (4) *ṃ kṣaṃḥ* to the Supreme Self, salutation.

Having thus arranged [the mantras], one should meditate as follows: "I bow to the Goddess who is red, three-eyed, and seated upon a lotus as red as a boat in a sea of blood; she holds in her lotus-like hands a noose, a goad, a bow, arrows, a cup of liquor, a trident, and a skull-cup. Having meditated thus, one should place the hand upon the heart.

Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃḥ hauṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ. The vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, united with the venerable Kāmeśvara-Śiva, are here; [their] vital breaths are here. Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ [9] ṃ hauṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ. The life-force (*jīva*) is established here, as are all the sense organs.

Having recited the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra— *ihasthitāni oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ hauṃ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ vāṅ-manas-tvak-cakṣuḥ-jihvā-śrotra-ghrāṇa-prāṇā iha āgatya sukhaṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhantu svāhā*— either three times or once, one should meditate upon one's own body as consisting of light.

Thus, having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* and then the internal *mātṛkā-nyāsa*— wherein inhalation (*pūraka*) is performed with the vowels, retention (*kuṃbhaka*) with the consonants from *ka* to *ma*, and exhalation (*recaka*) with the consonants from *ya* onwards— one should perform the *mātṛkā-prāṇāyāma* and then make the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*). Therein, first [one performs] the internal *mātṛkā-nyāsa*.

Om. Of this Śrī Antarmātṛkā-nyāsa, the venerable Brahmā is the Ṛṣi (head), Gāyatrī is the Chandas (mouth), the venerable Antarmātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the Devatā (heart), the consonants are the Bījas (private parts), the vowels are the Śaktis (feet), and the Unmanifest is the Kīlaka (anus). [I perform this] for my own sake as a limb of the worship of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī.
Thus ends the application of the Ṛṣi and others (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now follows the application of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*):
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ kaṃ 4 āṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ; hṛdayāya namaḥ*.
*Iṃ caṃ 4 īṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā; śirase svāhā*. *Uṃ ṭaṃ 4 ūṃ madhyamābhyāṃ...* [and so forth].

Māṃ abhyāṃ vaṣaṭ; śikhāyai vaṣaṭ. (4) ṃaiṃ taṃ (4) ṃaiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ; kavacāya huṃ. (4) ṃoṃ paṃ (4) ṃauṃ kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ; netratrayāya vauṣaṭ. (4) ṃaṃ yaṃ (9) ṃ aṃḥ karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ phaṭ; astrāya phaṭ.

Thus ends the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): Oṃ! [I meditate upon] the lotus whose pericarp is the syllable *ṃ* (the nasal bindu), situated in the sky of the moon; its filaments shimmer with pairs of vowels; within its petals are the five consonant groups (*varga*) starting with *ya*, *śa*, and *la* respectively; and in the eight directions are the letters from *la* to *ṃ* joined with the *aṅgulī* (finger) mantra.
Having meditated upon the lotus of letters situated on the head as the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, which destroys poison and disease and is surrounded by the *ṇīpura*,
and having awakened the Moon-crested Goddess (Candramaulī) from the resonance of the *mūlādhāra*—
who resembles a blazing fire and consists of subtle light— from the *mūlādhāra*...

Visualizing her, who has the form of lightning, touching the lotus of his head, one should meditate on all the *mātṛkā* phonemes—which have issued from that lotus of the head touched by her in the form of a flood of nectar—and which remain pervading the body via the path of the *suṣumṇā*; having thus meditated, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Having thus meditated upon her in her subtle form, [one should proceed] otherwise...
Then, having meditated upon a sixteen-petaled lotus with its face turned upward for the sake of purification therein, [recite]: (4) *maṃ namaḥ*, (4) *āṃ namaḥ*, (4) *iṃ namaḥ*,

ḶṂ Namaḥ (4), EṂ Namaḥ (4), AIṂ Namaḥ (4), OṂ Namaḥ (4), AUṂ Namaḥ (4), AṂ Namaḥ (4), AḤ Namaḥ. Thus is the internal Mātṛkā-nyāsa according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) upon the sixteen petals of the Viśuddhi-cakra. Now follows the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa; therein, first, is the practice of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*).

The inhalation is performed with the vowels, the retention with the consonants beginning with *ka*, and the exhalation with those beginning with *ya*. *Oṃ*, of this external Mātṛkā-nyāsa: Brahmā is the Ṛṣi (at the head), Gāyatrī is the metre (at the mouth), Śrī-Vahirmātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (at the heart), the consonants are the seeds (at the secret place), the vowels are the powers (at the feet), and the Avyakta is the weapon (at all limbs).
The application [of the mantra] as the limbs of my Śrī Tripurasundarī is thus concluded.

This is the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*. Now follows the *kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Kaṃ (4) Āṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; salutation to the heart (4) Iṃ Caṃ (4) Īṃ, salutation to the two index fingers; Svāhā... [and so on].

Hā Śirase Svāhā (4) Muṃ Taṃ (4) Mūṃ Madhyamābhyāṃ Vaṣaṭ (4) Eṃ Taṃ (4) Aiṃ Anāmikābhyāṃ Huṃ Kavacāya Huṃ (4) Oṃ Paṃ (4) Auṃ Kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ Vauṣaṭ Netratrayāya Vauṣaṭ (4) Aṃ Yaṃ (9) Aṃḥ Karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ Phaṭ.

The *Trikara-Ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): Oṃ! She whose face, arms, feet, heart, flanks, and chest are fashioned from the distinctions of the fifty letters; who wears a radiant matted lock adorned with a crescent moon;
who is as white as the moon, jasmine, and snow; and who holds in her hands a rosary, a water-pot, a lotus, and a boon-granting gesture—she of the three eyes.
"I bow to that Bhāratī, seated upon a lotus, resembling a young fish, and burdened by full breasts and hips.
Having thus meditated, one should contemplate the weapons starting from the upper right hand and ending with the lower right hand, [reciting]:
*haṃ sauṃḥ aṃ āṃ* and so forth, up to *kṣaṃ namaḥ śauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ*, [from] the head down to the feet.
Having placed the pervasive *dānta*, one should perform the ritual deposition (*nyāsa*): (4) *ṃaṃ namaḥ* on the head; (4) *ṃāṃ namaḥ* on the face;

(4) *ṃiṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; (4) *ṃīṃ namaḥ* on the left; (4) *ṃuṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; (4) *ṃūṃ namaḥ* on the left; (4) *ṃṛṃ namaḥ* on the right nostril; (4) *ṃṝṃ namaḥ* on the left; (4) *ṃḷṃ namaḥ* on the [right]...

ḶṂḤ Namaḥ to the left [lip] (4); ṂEṂḤ Namaḥ to the upper lip (4); ṂAIṂḤ Namaḥ to the lower lip (4); ṂOṂḤ Namaḥ to the upper teeth (4); ṂAUṂ Namaḥ to the lower teeth (4); ṂAṂḤ Namaḥ to the forehead (4); Ṃ AṂḤ Namaḥ to the tongue (4); ṂKAṂ Namaḥ to the root of the right arm (4); ṂKHAṂḤ Namaḥ to the elbow.

(4) *ṃṭaṃḥ* namaḥ dakṣapādakakṣe; (4) *ṃṭhaṃḥ* namaḥ jānuni. Thus is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the *bindu* and *visarga* according to the order of manifestation (*sthiti-krama*). Now, the placement of the *bindu* and *visarga* according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhāra-krama*): therein, the visualization (*dhyāna*) preceded by the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other elements is as follows: (4) *ṃkṣaṃḥ* Paramātman.

(4) *Namaḥ* from the heart to the head: *ṃ laṃḥ* to the individual self (*jīvātman*). (4) *Namaḥ* from the feet to the heart: *ṃ haṃḥ* to the vital self (*prāṇātman*). (4) *Namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot: *ṃ saṃḥ* to the semen self (*śukrātman*). (4) *Namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot: *ṃ ṣaṃḥ* to the marrow self (*majjātman*). (4) *Namaḥ* from the heart to the left... [and so forth].
(4) *Ṃ Śaṃḥ*—homage to the self consisting of bone, from the heart to the right hand;
(4) *Ṃ Vaṃḥ*—homage to the self consisting of fat, on the left shoulder; (4) *Ṃ Laṃḥ*—homage to the self consisting of flesh, on the hump;
(4) *Ṃ Raṃḥ*—homage to the self consisting of blood, on the right shoulder; (4) *Ṃ Yaṃḥ*—homage to the self consisting of skin.

(4) *Maṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the heart; (4) *Bhaṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the abdomen; (4) *Baṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the navel; (4) *Phaṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the back; (4) *Paṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the left side; (4) *Naṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the right side; (4) *Dhaṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the tips of the toes of the left foot; (4) *Daṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the base of the toes; (4) *Ḍaṃ* *Ḥaṃ* *Maḥ*, obeisance to the ankle.

(4) *ṃthaṃḥ* namaḥ to the knee; (4) *ṃtaṃḥ* namaḥ to the armpit; (4) *ṃṇaṃḥ* namaḥ to the tip of the right toe; (4) *ṃḍhaṃḥ* namaḥ to the base of the toes; (4) *ṃḍaṃḥ* namaḥ to the ankle; (4) *ṃṭhaṃḥ* namaḥ to the knee;
(4) *ṃṭaṃḥ* namaḥ to the armpit; (4) *ṃñaṃḥ* namaḥ to the tip of the left arm’s finger.

(4) *ṃ ghaṃḥ* namaḥ to the base of the fingers; (4) *ṃ gaṃḥ* namaḥ to the wrist; (4) *ṃ khaṃḥ* namaḥ to the...

(4) *ṃ* *oṃ*: Homage to the upper teeth. (4) *ṃ* *aiṃ*: Homage to the lower lip. (4) *ṃ* *eṃ*: Homage to the upper lip. (4) *ṃ* *ḹṃ*: Homage to the left cheek. The placement of the *bindu* and *visarga* according to the sequence of dissolution; now, the placement of the *hṛllekhā* and others according to the sequence of creation. In that regard, one should perform *prāṇāyāma* with the *māyā-bīja* as before.
Of this venerable *mātṛkā-nyāsa* beginning with *hṛllekhā*, Śakti is the *ṛṣi* (śi) and Gāyatrī is the *chandas* (mu).

The deity Sarasvatī, whose form is the Hṛllekhā, is enjoined as a limb of Śrīvidyā for the purpose of Nyāsa; this is the Ṛṣyādinyāsa. Now follows the Kara-Ṣaḍaṅganyāsa: (4) *ṃ hrīṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ hrīṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ*. (4) *ṃ*... [and so forth].

*Hrīṃ iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ hrīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā śirase svāhā.* (4) *Hrīṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ hrīṃ madhyamābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ.* (4) *Hrīṃ eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ hrīṃ anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ kavacāya huṃ.* (4) *Oṃ paṃ phaṃ vaṃ bhaṃ...*
*Maṃ auṃ hrīṃ* to the two little fingers, *vaṣaṭ*. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃḥ aṃḥ hrīṃ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*, *astrāya phaṭ*.
Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs on the hands. Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): [She who is] like the brilliance of ten million rising suns...

We meditate upon the Mother of the Universe, the three-eyed bestower of happiness, seated upon a lotus; she possesses thighs as large and firm as elephants' trunks, is adorned with a crown, earrings, necklaces, a girdle, and anklets, and holds in her lotus-like hands a rosary, a noose, a goad, and a book.

Thus is the meditation: (4) *ṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ hrīṃ* on the head; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ āṃ namaḥ hrīṃ* on the face; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ iṃ namaḥ hrīṃ* on the right eye; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ īṃ namaḥ hrīṃ* on the left eye; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ uṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ* on the left [ear]; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* on the right nostril.

(4) *ṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* on the left cheek; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left [cheek]; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ eṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the upper teeth; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ auṃ namaḥ* on the lower teeth; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; (4) *ṃ hrīṃ*.

*Hrīṃ aṃḥ namaḥ jihvāyām* (on the tongue); *ṃ hrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ dakṣavāhumūle* (on the root of the right arm); *ṃ hrīṃ khaṃ namaḥ kurpare* (on the elbow); *ṃ hrīṃ gaṃ namaḥ maṇibandhe* (on the wrist); *ṃ hrīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle* (on the base of the fingers);
*ṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ aṅgulyagre* (on the tips of the fingers); *ṃ hrīṃ caṃ namaḥ vāmavāhumūle* (on the root of the left arm); *ṃ hrīṃ chaṃ*.

Namaḥ kurpare (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ maṇibandhe (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ aṅgulyagre (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ dakṣapādakakṣe (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ jānuni (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ gulphe (4) ˜ṃ hrīṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle.

(4) *ṃhrīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; (4) *ṃhrīṃ taṃ namaḥ* in the groin of the left leg; (4) *ṃhrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; (4) *ṃhrīṃ daṃ namaḥ* at the ankle; (4) *ṃhrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes;
(4) *ṃhrīṃ naṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the toes; (4) *ṃhrīṃ paṃ namaḥ* on the right side; (4) *ṃhrīṃ phaṃ namaḥ* on the left.

*Hrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the back; (4) *Hrīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* at the navel; (4) *Hrīṃ maṃ namaḥ* in the abdomen; (4) *Hrīṃ yaṃ*, salutation to the self of the skin, in the heart; (4) *Hrīṃ raṃ*, salutation to the self of the blood, on the right shoulder; (4) *Hrīṃ laṃ*, salutation to the self of the flesh, on the hump; (4) *Hrīṃ vaṃ*, salutation to the self of the fat, on the left [shoulder].

(4) *Māṃse* (in the flesh), *ṃ hrīṃ śaṃ*, obeisance to the self of bone; from the heart to the right hand. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ*, obeisance to the self of marrow; from the heart to the left hand. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ saṃ*, obeisance to the self of semen; from the heart to the right foot. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ haṃ*, obeisance to the self of vital breath (*prāṇa*); from the heart to the left foot.

(4) *ṃ hrīṃ laṃ* salutation to the individual soul (*jīvātman*); from the feet to the navel. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ* salutation to the supreme soul (*paramātman*); from the navel to the crown of the head. Thus ends the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *mātṛkā* beginning with *hṛllekhā*.

Oṃ. Of this *Mātṛkā-nyāsa* beginning with the seed-syllable *Śrīṃ*: Bhṛgu is the *ṛṣi*, the *Gāyatrī* is the *chandas*, Śrī Mahālakṣmī is the *devatā*, and its application (* viniyoga*) is in the *nyāsa* as a limb of the *Śrīvidyā*.
Thus ends the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*. Now follows the *kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*: [4] *Śrīṃ Aṃ Kaṃ* [5] *Āṃ Śrīṃ*.

To the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ* (4). *ṃ śrīṃ iṃ caṃ* (5) *ṃ īṃ śrīṃ*, to the two index fingers, *svāhā*; to the head, *svāhā* (4). *ṃ śrīṃ uṃ ṭaṃ* (5) *ṃ ūṃ śrīṃ*, to the two middle fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vauṣaṭ* (4). *ṃ śrīṃ eṃ taṃ* (5) *ṃ aiṃ śrīṃ*, to the two ring fingers, *huṃ*; to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*.

(4) *Oṃ* *Śrīṃ* *Oṃ* *Paṃ* (5) *Oṃ* *Śrīṃ*—with the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhikābhyām*) *Vaṣaṭ*; to the three eyes (*netratrayāya*) *Vaṣaṭ*. (4) *Oṃ* *Śrīṃ* *Yaṃ* (9) *Aṃḥ* *Śrīṃ*—with the palms and backs of the hands (*karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyām*) *Phaṭ*; to the weapon (*astrāya*) *Phaṭ*. Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): [She] whose radiance is like a flash of lightning, and who resembles the Snow Mountain...
One should meditate upon that Mahālakṣmī, who is constantly being sprinkled by elephants with jars of nectar lifted up by their trunks;
who bears in her lotus-like hands a rosary, a pair of lotuses, and a book; and who is radiant with shining jewels—thus having meditated, the practitioner on the right...
The meditation on the weapons begins from the left lower hand and extends to the end of the left lower hand:

(4) *Śrīṃ Aṃ Namaḥ Śrīṃ* at the head; (4) *Śrīṃ Āṃ Namaḥ Śrīṃ* on the face; (4) *Śrīṃ Iṃ Namaḥ Śrīṃ* on the right eye; (4) *Śrīṃ Īṃ Namaḥ Śrīṃ* on the left [eye]; (4) *Śrīṃ Uṃ Namaḥ Śrīṃ* on the right ear; (4) *Śrīṃ Ūṃ Na*... [on the left ear].

*Maḥ śrīṃ* on the left [ear] (4); *ṃ śrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the right nostril (4); *ṃ śrīṃ ṝṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the left [nostril] (4); *ṃ śrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the right cheek (4); *ṃ śrīṃ ḹṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the left [cheek] (4); *ṃ śrīṃ eṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the upper lip (4); *ṃ śrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the lower lip (4); *ṃ śrīṃ oṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* on the upper [lip] (4).

(4) *Śrīṃ auṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the upper teeth; (4) *Śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the lower teeth; (4) *Śrīṃ aṃḥ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the forehead; (4) *Śrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the tongue; (4) *Śrīṃ khaṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the root of the right arm;
(4) *Śrīṃ gaṃ namaḥ śrīṃ* to the elbow; (4) *Śrīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ*... to the wrist.
Śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ at the base of the right thumb; Śrīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ at the tip of the right thumb;
Śrīṃ caṃ namaḥ at the base of the left arm; Śrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ at the elbow; Śrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ at the wrist; Śrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the left thumb; Śrīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ at the tip of the left thumb.

(4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Ṭaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the groin of the right leg; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Ṭhaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the knee; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Ḍaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the ankle; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Ḍhaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the base of the toes; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Ṇaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the tips of the toes; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Taṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ, to the groin of the left leg; (4) *Oṃ* Śrīṃ *Thaṃ* namaḥ Śrīṃ...
(4) *Śrīṃ* *daṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the knees; (4) *Śrīṃ* *dhaṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the ankles;

(4) *Śrīṃ* *naṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the bases of the toes; (4) *Śrīṃ* *paṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the tips of the toes; (4) *Śrīṃ* *phaṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the right side; (4) *Śrīṃ* *baṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the left side; (4) *Śrīṃ* *bhaṃ* *namaḥ* *śrīṃ* to the back; (4) *Śrīṃ* to the navel.

*Maṃ namaḥ śrīṃ jaṭhare* (4) *ṃ śrīṃ yaṃ tvagātmane namaḥ śrīṃ hṛdi* (4) *ṃ śrīṃ raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ śrīṃ dakṣāṃse* (4) *ṃ śrīṃ laṃ māṃsātmane namaḥ śrīṃ kakudi* (4) *ṃ śrīṃ vaṃ medasātmane namaḥ śrīṃ vāmāṃse* (4) *ṃ śrīṃ śaṃ asthyātmane namaḥ*.

*Śrīṃ hṛdayādi-dakṣapāṇyantaṃ* (4) *śrīṃ ṣaṃ majjātmane namaḥ*. *Śrīṃ hṛdayādi-vāmapāṇyantaṃ* (4) *śrīṃ saṃ śukrātmane namaḥ*. *Śrīṃ hṛdayādi-dakṣapādāntaṃ* (4) *śrīṃ haṃ prāṇātmane namaḥ*. *Śrīṃ hṛdayādi-vāmapādāntaṃ* (4) *śrīṃ laṃ jīvātmane*.

*Namaḥ śrīṃ* from the feet up to the navel; *śrīṃ kṣaṃ paramātmane namaḥ śrīṃ* from the navel up to the head. Thus ends the *Mātṛkā-nyāsa* beginning with the seed-syllable *śrīṃ*. *Oṃ*, of this *Śrī-kāmavīja-ādi-mātṛkā-nyāsa*, the seer is Saṃmohana, the meter is Gāyatrī, [and the deity is] Śrī-Mahā...
The application for the worship of the *Śrīvidyā* as an auxiliary (*aṅga*) of the goddess Saṃmohinī is thus [concluded]. This is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and so forth.

Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) on the hands: (4) *ṃ klīṃ aṃ kaṃ (5) ṃ āṃ klīṃ* to both thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ*. (4) *ṃ klīṃ iṃ caṃ (5) ṃ īṃ klīṃ* to both index fingers, *svāhā*; to the head, *svāhā*.

Hāṃ klīṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ūṃ klīṃ, to the two middle fingers, vauṣaṭ; to the crest-lock, vauṣaṭ. Ṃ klīṃ eṃ taṃ ṃ klīṃ, to the two ring fingers, huṃ; to the armor, huṃ. Ṃ klīṃ oṃ paṃ ṃ auṃ klīṃ, to the two little fingers, vaṣaṭ; to the three eyes, vaṣaṭ. Ṃ klīṃ aṃ yaṃ ṃ aṃḥ klīṃ, to the palms and backs of the hands...

With *pṛṣṭābhyāṃ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ*, perform the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): Oṃ, I meditate upon her who has nine eyes, who enchants the world, whose breasts are like those of Varuṇa, and who holds in her own hands a rosary, a bow of sugarcane, two nooses, two lotuses, a goad, five arrows, and a fresh book.
Having meditated on her as "Candracūdā" (Moon-crested), one should perform the visualization of the weapons starting from the lower left hand up to the rightmost hand:

(4) *Klīṃ Aṃ Namaḥ Klīṃ* upon the head; (4) *Klīṃ Āṃ Namaḥ Klīṃ* upon the face; (4) *Klīṃ Iṃ Namaḥ Klīṃ* upon the right eye; (4) *Klīṃ Īṃ Namaḥ Klīṃ* upon the left [eye]; (4) *Klīṃ Uṃ Namaḥ*... [upon the right ear].

The application [of the mantra] as a limb of Śrīvidyā is for the worship of the Mātṛkā-deities who possess the form of others. This concludes the Nyāsa of the Seers and so forth (Ṛṣyādinyāsa).
