From the end of the feet to the head: *Oṃ laṃ* to the *ātman*, *namaḥ*. From the feet to the navel:

*Oṃ kṣaṃ* to the *paramātman*, *namaḥ*. From the navel to the top of the head: [the same]. This is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa encapsulated by the single *Tāra* (*Oṃ*). Now follows the Mātṛkā-nyāsa encapsulated by the four *Tāras*.

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ śirasi (4). Āṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ mukhavṛtte (4). Iṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ dakṣanetre (4). Īṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ vāmanetre (4). Uṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ [namaḥ] dakṣakarṇe (4). Ūṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ vāme (4). Ṛṃ śrīṃ... [text truncated]

*Hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril (4). *ṃ ṛṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the left [nostril] (4). *ṃ ḷṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the right cheek (4). *ṃ ḹṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the left [cheek] (4). *ṃ eṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the upper lip (4). *ṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the lower lip (4). *ṃ oṃ śrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*...

On the upper teeth: (4) *ṃ auṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: (4) *ṃ aṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. On the forehead: (4) *ṃ aṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the tongue: (4) *ṃ kaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the root of the right arm: (4) *ṃ khaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*. On the elbow: (4) *ṃ gaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*.
(4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the wrist; (4) *ṅ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the base of the fingers;

(4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the tips of the fingers; (4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the base of the left arm; (4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the elbow; (4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ at the wrist; (4) *ṃ* śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ... at the base of the fingers.

Oṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle (4) ṃ ñaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ aṅgulyagre (4) ṃ ṭaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ dakṣapādakakṣe (4) ṃ ṭhaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ jānuni (4) ṃ ḍaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ gulphe (4) ṃ ḍhaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle (4) ṃ ṇaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ...

Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the tips of the fingers (4); Ṃ Taṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ in the groin of the left leg (4); Ṃ Thaṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the knee (4); Ṃ Daṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the ankle (4); Ṃ Dhaṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the base of the toes (4); Ṃ Naṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the tips of the toes (4); Ṃ Paṃ.

*Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the right side; (4) *ṃ phaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the left; (4) *ṃ vaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the back; (4) *ṃ bhaṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* at the navel; (4) *ṃ maṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* in the abdomen; (4) *ṃ yaṃ tvagātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* in the heart; (4) *ṃ raṃ asṛgātmane*.

*Neśrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the right shoulder; (4) *ṃ laṃ māṃsātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the back; (4) *ṃ vaṃ medasātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; (4) *ṃ śaṃ asthyātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the right hand; (4) *ṃ ṣaṃ majjātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ...* [etc.]

Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ from the heart to the left hand—(4) Ṃ Saṃ to the Śukrātman; Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ from the heart to the right foot—(4) Ṃ Haṃ to the Prāṇātman; Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ from the heart to the left foot—(4) Ṃ Laṃ to the Jīvātman; Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Namaḥ from the feet... [upward].
*Bhyaṃ taṃ kṣaṃ paramātmane śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ namaḥ*—from the navel to the top of the head.
Thus is the Mātṛkā-nyāsa encased by the four *tāra*s. Oṃ.
Of this Śrīvidyā-yukta-mātṛkā-nyāsa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the Ṛṣi, Gāyatrī is the Chandas, and Śrī... [is the Devatā].
The application (*nyāsa*) of the deities of the *Vidyāmātṛkā* as limbs of Śrīvidyā is thus concluded.
This concludes the *Ṛṣyādinyāsa*. Now follows the *Kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*: (4) *Mā~ Keīlahrī~ Aṃ*—to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*;
to the heart, *namaḥ*. (4) *Mā~ Klīṃ Hasakahalahrī~*—to the index fingers... [and so on].
*Bhyāṃ svāhā*, *śirase svāhā* (4) *ṃsauṃḥ sakala hrīṃ* to the middle fingers *vaṣaṭ*,
to the crest-lock *vaṣaṭ* (4) *ṃaiṃ ke ī la hrīṃ* to the ring fingers *huṃ*, to the armor *huṃ* (4) *ṃ klīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ* to the little fingers *vauṣaṭ*, to the three eyes *vauṣaṭ* (4) *ṃ*.
*Sauṃḥ sakala hrīṃ karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ phaṭ astrāya phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual for the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the hands.

Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): [I meditate upon her] whose body is adorned with divine garments, who has the sun and fire as her eyes, who wears the moon as a crown, whose limbs are like snow, who sits upon a lion-throne, who holds an axe and a sword, who has three eyes, and who is saluted by Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra.
"We worship the measured Tripurā"—this is the meditation (4). *Mūla* *Aṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the head (4). *Mūla* *Āṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the mouth (4).

*Mūla* *Iṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the right eye (4). *Mūla* *Īṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the left (4). *Mūla* *Uṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the right ear (4). *Mūla* *Ūṃ* *Namaḥ*, *Mūla* at the left (4). *Mūla* *Ṛṃ*... [and so on].

*Laṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the right cheek (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the left (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Ḷṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the right nostril (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the left (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Eṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the upper lip (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Aiṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the lower lip (4); *Ṃ Mūlaṃ Oṃ Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] on the upper teeth.

(4) *Mūla* auṃ *namaḥ mūla* on the lower teeth; (4) *Mūla* aṃ *namaḥ mūla* on the forehead; (4) *Mūla* aṃḥ *namaḥ mūla* within the mouth; (4) *Mūla* kaṃ *namaḥ mūla* at the root of the right arm; (4) *Mūla* khaṃ *namaḥ mūla* at the elbow; (4) *Mūla* gaṃ *namaḥ mūla* at the wrist; (4) *Mūla* ghaṃ *namaḥ*.

Mūlaṃ Aṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right thumb; Mūlaṃ Āṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right thumb; Mūlaṃ Iṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right index finger; Mūlaṃ Īṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right index finger; Mūlaṃ Uṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right middle finger; Mūlaṃ Ūṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right middle finger; Mūlaṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right ring finger; Mūlaṃ Ṝṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right ring finger; Mūlaṃ Ḷṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right little finger; Mūlaṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right little finger; Mūlaṃ Eṃ Namaḥ at the base of the left thumb; Mūlaṃ Aiṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the left thumb; Mūlaṃ Oṃ Namaḥ at the base of the left index finger; Mūlaṃ Auṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the left index finger; Mūlaṃ Aṃ Namaḥ at the base of the left middle finger; Mūlaṃ Aḥ Namaḥ at the tip of the left middle finger; Mūlaṃ Kaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right arm; Mūlaṃ Khaṃ Namaḥ at the elbow; Mūlaṃ Gaṃ Namaḥ at the wrist; Mūlaṃ Ghaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right thumb; Mūlaṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the right thumb; Mūlaṃ Caṃ Namaḥ at the base of the right index finger; Mūlaṃ Chaṃ Namaḥ at the elbow; Mūlaṃ Jaṃ Namaḥ at the wrist; Mūlaṃ Jhaṃ Namaḥ at the base of the left thumb; Mūlaṃ Ñaṃ Namaḥ at the tip of the left thumb; Mūlaṃ [The mantra continues].
Ṭaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ dakṣapādamūle (4); Ṃ mūlaṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ jānuni (4); Ṃ mūlaṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ gulphe (4); Ṃ mūlaṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ aṅgulimūle (4);
Ṃ mūlaṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ aṅgulyagre (4); Ṃ mūlaṃ taṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ vāmapādamūle (4); Ṃ mūlaṃ thaṃ namaḥ mūlaṃ... [jānuni] (4).

(4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the knees; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the ankles; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the bases of the toes; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the tips of the toes; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the right side; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the left side; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the back; (4) *Mūla* ṃ *namaḥ* to the navel; (4) *Mūla* ṃ.

The root mantra: *Namaḥ* to the root at the navel; (4) *ṃ* to the root at the belly; *Namaḥ* to the root, the essence of the skin, at the heart; (4) *ṃ* to the root at the right shoulder; (4) *ṃ* to the root, the essence of the blood, at the left shoulder; (4) *ṃ* to the root, the essence of the flesh, at the back of the head; (4) *ṃ* to the root, the essence of the fat, at the left shoulder; (4) *ṃ* to the root, the essence of the bone, at the crown of the head.

Root mantra from the heart to the right hand: *Oṃ [Root Mantra] ṃ maṃ majjātmane namaḥ*. Root mantra from the heart to the left hand: *Oṃ [Root Mantra] ṃ saṃ śukrātmane namaḥ*. Root mantra from the heart to the right foot: *Oṃ [Root Mantra] ṃ haṃ jīvātmane namaḥ*. Root mantra from the heart to the left foot: *Oṃ [Root Mantra] ṃ laṃ paramātmane*.

*Namaḥ* to the root [mantra] from the feet up to the navel; *kṣaṃ namaḥ* to the root [mantra]; *Namaḥ* to the one whose self is knowledge (*jñānātmane*) from the heart up to the head. Thus ends the placement of the Mātṛkā associated with the Śrīvidyā. One should perform the placement thus far.
Of this venerable Haṃsamātṛkā-nyāsa, Nārāyaṇa is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Supreme Swan (*paramahaṃsa*) is the meter (*chandaḥ*), and the Supreme Self (*paramātman*) is the deity (*devatā*).

*Ramātmā* is the deity (*hṛ*), *haṃ* is the seed-syllable (*gu*), *saḥ* is the power (*pā*), *so'haṃ* is the bolt (*nā*), and for my Śrīvidyā-limbs, the application (*sa*) is the *Haṃsa-mātṛkā-nyāsa*. Thus ends the *ṛṣyādinyāsa*. Now follows the *kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*: *(4) ̐aṃ kaṃ (5) ̐āṃ haṃsaḥ* to both thumbs, *namaḥ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *(4) ̐iṃ*... [and so forth].

Caṃ (5) īṃ haṃsaḥ, with the two index fingers, svāhā; to the head, svāhā. (4) ūṃ ṭaṃ (5) ūṃ haṃsaḥ, with the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ; to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ. (4) eṃ taṃ (5) aiṃ haṃsaḥ, with the two ring fingers, huṃ; to the armor, huṃ. (4) oṃ paṃ (5) auṃ haṃsaḥ, with the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ; to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ. (4) ṃ.

Aṃ yaṃ maṃ haṃsaḥ phaṭ with the palms and backs of the hands; *phaṭ* for the weapon (*astra*). Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs on the hands. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): Oṃ, I behold that which abides in coming and going, yet is devoid of movement and the like; whose form is the nature of consciousness (*cidrūpa*), the destroyer of darkness; the foremost among all people—I bow to that Supreme Haṃsa.

Having meditated thus on the form of Mārtha, one should assign [the mantras] as follows: (4) *Haṃsaḥ aṃ namaḥ* to the head; (4) *Haṃsaḥ āṃ namaḥ* to the mouth; (4) *Haṃsaḥ iṃ namaḥ* to the right eye; (4) *Haṃsaḥ īṃ namaḥ* to the left [eye];
(4) *Haṃsaḥ uṃ namaḥ* to the right ear; (4) *Haṃsaḥ ūṃ namaḥ* to the left [ear]; (4) *Haṃsaḥ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the right cheek.

(4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ ṛṃ namaḥ* on the left [shoulder]; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ ḷṃ namaḥ* in the left nostril; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left [side of the face]; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ eṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ aiṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ oṃ namaḥ* on the upper teeth; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ auṃ namaḥ* on the lower teeth; (4) *ṃhaṃsaḥ aṃ namaḥ* [on the crown].

(4) *Haṃsaḥ Aṃ* Namaḥ on the forehead; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Kaṃ* Namaḥ within the mouth; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Khaṃ* Namaḥ at the base of the right arm; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Gaṃ* Namaḥ at the elbow; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Ghaṃ* Namaḥ at the wrist; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Ṅaṃ* Namaḥ at the base of the fingers; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Caṃ* Namaḥ at the tips of the fingers; (4) *Haṃsaḥ Chaṃ* Namaḥ on the left arm... [and so forth].

(4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ chaṃ namaḥ* to the elbow; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ jaṃ namaḥ* to the wrist; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ jhaṃ namaḥ* to the base of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ ñaṃ namaḥ* to the tips of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ ṭaṃ namaḥ* to the base of the right foot; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ ṭhaṃ namaḥ* to the knee; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ ḍaṃ namaḥ* to the ankle; (4) *Oṃ haṃsaḥ...* [to the toes].
*ṃ haṃ saḥ ṭaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers (4); *ṃ haṃ saḥ ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers (4);

*ṃ haṃ saḥ taṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left foot (4); *ṃ haṃ saḥ thaṃ namaḥ* at the knee (4); *ṃ haṃ saḥ daṃ namaḥ* at the ankle (4); *ṃ haṃ saḥ dhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the [left] toes (4); *ṃ* with the root mantra *ṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the [left] toes (4); *ṃ haṃ saḥ paṃ*.

*Namaḥ* on the right side: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ phaṃ namaḥ*. On the left side: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ vaṃ namaḥ*. On the back: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ bhaṃ namaḥ*. At the navel: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ maṃ namaḥ*. In the abdomen: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ yaṃ tvagātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of the skin). In the heart: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ* (salutation to the self of the blood). On the right shoulder: (4) *ṃ haṃ saḥ laṃ māṃsā-* (salutation to the self of the flesh).

(4) *Ṃ Haṃsaḥ*—salutation to the self as marrow at the crown of the head; (4) *Ṃ Haṃsaḥ*—salutation to the self as fat on the left shoulder; (4) *Ṃ Haṃsaḥ*—salutation to the self as bone from the heart to the right hand; (4) *Ṃ Haṃsaḥ*—salutation to the self as semen from the heart to the left hand; (4) *Ṃ Haṃsaḥ*—salutation to the self as [blood] from the heart to the right hand.

*Dāṃ* *Haṃsaḥ*, salutation to the Jīvātman; from the heart to the left foot. *Dīṃ* *Haṃsaḥ* *Laṃ*, salutation to the Paramātman; from the feet to the navel. *Duṃ* *Haṃsaḥ* *Kṣaṃ*, salutation to the Jñānātman; from the heart to the crown of the head. This is the *Haṃsamātṛkā-nyāsa*. Now, the *Paramahaṃsa-nyāsa*:

For the Mātṛkānyāsa: the Supreme Haṃsa is the Ṛṣi (head), Gāyatrī is the metre (mouth), the Mātṛkā whose nature is the Supreme Self is the deity (heart), and its application is in the ritual placement as a limb of Śrīvidyā (the whole). Thus is the Nyāsa of the Ṛṣi and others. Now follows the Kara-Ṣaḍaṅga Nyāsa: *ṃaṃ kaṃ* (forefinger), *ṃāṃ so'haṃ aṃ* (thumb).

To the thumbs, *namaḥ*; to the heart, *namaḥ*. (4) *ṃ iṃ caṃ* (5) *ṃ īṃ so'haṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā*, to the head, *svāhā*. (4) *ṃ uṃ ṭaṃ* (5) *ṃ ūṃ so'haṃ madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ*, to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*.
(4) *ṃ eṃ taṃ* (5) *ṃ aiṃ so'haṃ anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ*, to the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*. (4) *ṃ oṃ paṃ* (5) *ṃ*.

*Oṃ sohaṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Aṃ yaṃ aṃḥ sohaṃ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*; to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. This is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs of the hands.
Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*): [I meditate upon] Her whose form and color are manifested by the Supreme Self, whose state is inaccessible to the mind...

One should meditate on her who holds a rosary, a water-pot, and the *vidyā* [scriptural] mudrā; she is being fanned, possesses three eyes, and has a bright white lower garment covering all people. Thus is the meditation (*dhyāna*). *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ so'haṃ kṣaṃ paramātmane namaḥ*—from the navel to the top of the head. (4) *So'haṃ laṃ namaḥ*—from the feet to the navel. (4) *So'haṃ prā...*

(4) *ṃ so haṃ*—salutation to the self of semen (*śukrātman*), from the heart to the left foot; (4) *ṃ ṣaṃ*—salutation to the self of marrow (*majjātman*), from the heart to the right foot; (4) *ṃ śaṃ*—salutation to the self of bone (*asthyātman*), from the heart to the left hand; (4) *ṃ so haṃ vaṃ*—salutation to the self of fat (*medasātman*), [from the heart] to the... the left [hand].
On the right shoulder: *Ṃ So'haṃ raṃ asṛgātmane namaḥ*. On the left shoulder: *Ṃ So'haṃ yaṃ tvagātmane namaḥ*.
In the heart: *Ṃ So'haṃ maṃ namaḥ*. In the stomach: *Ṃ So'haṃ maṃ namaḥ*. At the navel: *Ṃ So'haṃ vaṃ namaḥ*. On the back: *Ṃ So'haṃ phaṃ namaḥ*. On the left side: [Ṃ So'haṃ bhaṃ namaḥ].

(4) *ṃ so'haṃ paṃ namaḥ* on the right side; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ naṃ namaḥ* on the toes of the left foot; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ dhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ daṃ namaḥ* on the ankle; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ thaṃ namaḥ* on the knee;
(4) *ṃ so'haṃ taṃ namaḥ* on the armpit; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ* on the tip of the right toe; (4) *ṃ so'haṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ* on the [toe]... aṃgu... [base].
(4) *ṃ so haṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the ankles; (4) *ṃ so haṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ* at the knees; (4) *ṃ so haṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ* at the armpits;
(4) *ṃ so haṃ ñaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers of the left arm; (4) *ṃ so haṃ jhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers;
(4) *ṃ so haṃ jaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist; (4) *ṃ so haṃ chaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; (4) *ṃ so haṃ caṃ namaḥ* at the upper arm.
(4) *ṃ so haṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers of the right hand; (4) *ṃ so haṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* at the bases of the fingers;

(4) *ṃ so haṃ gaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist; (4) *ṃ so haṃ khaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; (4) *ṃ so haṃ kaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the arm; (4) *ṃ so haṃ aṃḥ namaḥ* on the tongue; (4) *ṃ so haṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; (4) *ṃ so haṃ*.

*Haṃ auṃ namaḥ* to the lower teeth (4); *ṃ sohaṃ oṃ namaḥ* to the upper teeth (4); *ṃ sohaṃ aiṃ namaḥ* to the lower lip (4); *ṃ sohaṃ eṃ namaḥ* to the upper lip (4); *ṃ sohaṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* to the left cheek (4); *ṃ sohaṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* to the right cheek (4); *ṃ sohaṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the left nostril (4); *ṃ sohaṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril (4).

*So haṃ ūṃ namaḥ* to the left ear. (4) *So haṃ uṃ namaḥ* to the right ear. (4) *So haṃ īṃ namaḥ* to the left eye. (4) *So haṃ iṃ namaḥ* to the right eye. (4) *So haṃ āṃ namaḥ* to the face. (4) *So haṃ aṃ namaḥ* to the head. This is the Paramahaṃsa Mātṛkā Nyāsa. Now follows that which arises from the Praṇava...

For the Kalāmātṛkānyāsa: Śrī Prajāpati is the Ṛṣi (head); Gāyatrī is the Chandas (mouth); Śrī Śāradā Kalāmātṛkā Sarasvatī is the Devatā (heart); the consonants are the Vījas (secret parts); the vowels are the Śaktis (feet); the Unmanifest is the Kīlaka (privities); and its application ( viniyoga) is as a limb of Śrīvidyā. Thus is the Nyāsa of the Ṛṣis and others.

Now follows the six-limbed assignment (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): Aṃ Oṃ Āṃ, salutation to the two thumbs; salutation to the heart. Iṃ Oṃ Īṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers; svāhā to the head. Uṃ Oṃ Ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the two middle fingers; vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (*śikhā*). Eṃ Oṃ Aiṃ, huṃ to the two ring fingers; huṃ to the armor (*kavaca*). Oṃ Oṃ Auṃ... [to the two little fingers].
*Vaṣaṭ* to the two little fingers; *vaṣaṭ* to the three eyes; *Aṃ Oṃ Aṃḥ Phaṭ* to the palms and backs of the hands;
*Phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*). Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs of the hands. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*):
*Oṃ*, with his hands [he holds] a lotus, a discus, a bowstring, a deer, a book, a rosary of beads, and a bright axe.

Having meditated thus: "I bow to that Śāradā, who bears a supreme vessel—a golden jar shimmering with nectar—whose five faces, though three-eyed, are as beautiful as lightning, clouds, crystal, lotuses, and hibiscus flowers; she whose breasts press against her shoulders and who resembles the moon within a water-jar," one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: *Oṃ aṃ nivṛttyai namaḥ* on the head.

(4) Oṃ Āṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhā; [place] on the mouth. (4) Oṃ Iṃ, salutation to Vidyā; [place] on the right eye. (4) Oṃ Īṃ, salutation to Śānti; [place] on the left [eye]. (4) Oṃ Uṃ, salutation to Indhikā; [place] on the right ear. (4) Oṃ Ūṃ, salutation to Dīpikā; [place] on the left [ear]. (4) Oṃ Ṛṃ, salutation to Recikā; [place] on the right nostril. (4) Oṃ Ṝṃ, salutation to Mocikā; [place] on the left [nostril].

(4) *Oṃ* *ṃ* *Parāyai namaḥ* on the right cheek; (4) *Oṃ* *ḷṃ* *Sūkṣmāyai namaḥ* on the left [cheek]; (4) *Oṃ* *eṃ* *Sūkṣmāmṛtāyai namaḥ* on the upper lip; (4) *Oṃ* *aiṃ* *Jñānāmṛtāyai namaḥ* on the lower lip;
(4) *Oṃ* *oṃ* *Āpyāyinyai namaḥ* on the upper teeth; (4) *Oṃ* *auṃ* *Vyāpinyai namaḥ* on the lower teeth.

(4) Oṃ Aṃ, salutation to Vyomarūpiṇī on the forehead. (4) Oṃ Aṃḥ, salutation to Anantā on the tongue. (4) Oṃ Kaṃ, salutation to Sṛṣṭi at the base of the right arm. (4) Oṃ Khaṃ, salutation to Ṛddhi at the elbow. (4) Oṃ Gaṃ, salutation to Smṛti at the wrist. (4) Oṃ Ghaṃ, salutation to Medhā at the base of the fingers.
(4) Oṃ ṅaṃ Kāntyai namaḥ, on the tips of the fingers; (4) Oṃ caṃ Lakṣmyai namaḥ, at the base of the left upper arm;

(4) Oṃ chaṃ Dyutyai namaḥ, at the elbow; (4) Oṃ jaṃ Sthirāyai namaḥ, at the wrist; (4) Oṃ jhaṃ Sthityai namaḥ, at the base of the fingers; (4) Oṃ ñaṃ Siddhyai namaḥ, on the tips of the fingers; (4) Oṃ ṭaṃ Jarāyai...

Namaḥ dakṣapādakakṣe (4) oṃ ṭhaṃ pālinyai namaḥ jānuni (4) oṃ ḍaṃ śāntyai namaḥ gulphe (4) oṃ ḍhaṃ aiśvaryai namaḥ aṅgulīmūle (4) oṃ ṇaṃ ratyai namaḥ aṅgulyagre (4) oṃ taṃ kāminyai namaḥ vāmapādakakṣe (4) oṃ.

Oṃ thaṃ, salutation to Varadā, at the knee (4); Oṃ daṃ, salutation to Hlādinī, at the ankle (4); Oṃ dhaṃ, salutation to Prītī, at the base of the fingers (4); Oṃ naṃ, salutation to Dīrghā, at the tips of the fingers (4);
Oṃ paṃ, salutation to Tīkṣṇā, on the right side (4); Oṃ phaṃ, salutation to Raudrī, on the left side (4); Oṃ vaṃ...

Oṃ Bhaṃ, salutation to Bhayā on the back; Oṃ Maṃ, salutation to Nidrā at the navel; Oṃ Taṃ, salutation to Tandrā in the belly; Oṃ Yaṃ, salutation to Kṣudhā in the heart; Oṃ Raṃ, salutation to Krodhinī on the right shoulder; Oṃ Laṃ, salutation to Kriyā on the hump; Oṃ Vaṃ, salutation to Ulkā [on the left shoulder].

On the left shoulder: *Oṃ śaṃ* to Mṛtyurūpā, *Namaḥ*. From the heart to the right hand: *Oṃ ṣaṃ* to Pītā, *Namaḥ*. From the heart to the left hand: *Oṃ saṃ* to Śvetā, *Namaḥ*. From the heart to the right foot: *Oṃ haṃ* to Aruṇā, *Namaḥ*. From the heart to the left foot... [end of fragment].
*Dāṃtaṃ* (4) *Oṃ Laṃ Asitāyai namaḥ*, from the feet to the navel; (4) *Oṃ Kṣaṃḥ Anantāyai namaḥ*, from the navel to the top of the head. This is the Nyāsa of the Kalāmātṛkā arising from the Praṇava.
Now, for the Nyāsa of the Aṣṭātriṃśatkalāmātṛkā, the Seers are Soma, Sūrya, and Agni. (Śi)

The *anuṣṭubh* and *triṣṭubh* are the meters (*chandas*); the deity is Mātṛkā in the form of thirty-eight *kalās* (*mūrdhan*); the seeds (*bījas*) are the consonants (*guhya*); the powers (*śaktis*) are the vowels (*pāda*); the unmanifest (*avyakta*) is the bolt (*kīlaka*, *nābhi*); the application (*viniyoga*) is in the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as a limb of Śrīvidyā (*sadya*). Thus is the ritual placement of the seers and so forth (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs on the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

(4) *maṃ kaṃ* (5) *māṃ aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*, *hṛdayāya namaḥ*. (4) *iṃ caṃ* (5) *īṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā*, *śirase svāhā*. (4) *uṃ ṭaṃ* (5) *ūṃ madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ*. (4) *eṃ taṃ* (5) *aiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ*, *kavacāya huṃ*. (4) *oṃ paṃ* (5) *auṃ kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*.

*bhyāṃ vauṣaṭ*, *netratrayāya vauṣaṭ* (4) *maṃ yaṃ (9) maṃḥ karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ phaṭ*, *astrāya phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs upon the hands. Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*):
[She who is] like pure crystal, resplendent in pure silk, and shimmering with pearls and gems...

Meditation: One should meditate upon the Supreme Goddess Sarasvatī, the Mother of all letters (Mātṛkā), as she holds a lotus, a rosary, a water-pot, a book, and makes the gesture of granting boons, seated here within the lotus of the heart.
(4) *Aṃ*—Salutation to Amṛtā on the head. (4) *Āṃ*—Salutation to Mānadā on the face. (4) *Iṃ*... [and so forth].

(4) *Pūṣā* to this one, salutation to the right eye; (4) *Āṃ Īṃ Tuṣṭyai*, salutation to the left [eye]; (4) *Ūṃ Ūṃ Puṣṭyai*, salutation to the right ear; (4) *Ṛṃ Ṛṃ Ratyai*, salutation to the left [ear]; (4) *Ṝṃ Ṝṃ Dhṛtyai*, salutation to the right nostril; (4) *ṝṃ ṝṃ Śaśinyai*, salutation to the left [nostril]; (4) *Ḷṃ Ḷṃ Candrikāyai*, salutation to the right cheek; (4) *Ḹṃ Ḹṃ Kāntyai*, salutation to the left [cheek].

On the left [cheek]: (4) *ṃeṃ jyotsnāyai namaḥ*. On the upper lip: (4) *ṃaiṃ śriyai namaḥ*. On the lower lip: (4) *ṃoṃ prītyai namaḥ*. On the upper teeth: (4) *ṃauṃ aṅgadāyai namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: (4) *ṃaṃ pūrṇāyai namaḥ*. On the forehead: (4) *ṃaṃḥ pūrṇāmṛtāyai namaḥ*. On the chin: (4) *ṃkaṃ bhaṃ tapinyai namaḥ*.

At the base of the right arm: *Oṃ Khaṃ Bhaṃ Tāpinyai Namaḥ*; at the elbow: *Oṃ Gaṃ Phaṃ Dhūmrāyai Namaḥ*; at the wrist: *Oṃ Ghaṃ Paṃ Marīcyai Namaḥ*; at the base of the fingers: *Oṃ Ṅaṃ Naṃ Jvālinyai Namaḥ*;
at the tips of the fingers: *Oṃ Caṃ Dhaṃ Rucyai Namaḥ*. At the base of the left arm: *Oṃ Chaṃ Daṃ Suṣumṇāyai*.

(4) *Eṃ jaṃ* to Aṃjanī, the giver of enjoyment, salutation! At the wrist (4) *Eṃ jhaṃ taṃ* to Viśvā, salutation! At the base of the fingers (4) *Eṃ ñaṃ ṇaṃ* to Vodhinī, salutation! At the tips of the fingers (4) *Eṃ ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ* to Dhāriṇī, salutation!
At the groin of the right leg (4) *Eṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ* to Kṣamā, salutation! At the knee (4) *Eṃ yaṃ* to Dhūmrā...

(4) *Oṃ raṃ* salutation to Ūṣmā at the ankle; (4) *Oṃ laṃ* salutation to Jvalinī at the base of the toes; (4) *Oṃ vaṃ* salutation to Jvālinī at the tips of the toes; (4) *Oṃ śaṃ* salutation to Visphuliṅginī at the left knee; (4) *Oṃ ṣaṃ* salutation to Suśrī at the ankle; (4) *Oṃ saṃ* salutation to Svarūpā at the [left] heel.

At the base of the thumbs: *Aṃ Haṃ Kapilāyai namaḥ*. At the tips of the fingers: *Āṃ Laṃ Havyavāhāyai namaḥ*. On the head: *Iṃ Kṣaṃḥ Kavyavāhāyai namaḥ*. On all limbs. This is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the thirty-eight digits of the Mātṛkā. Now follows the procedure for the placement of the Mātṛkā beginning with Keśava.
Nārāyaṇa is the Ṛṣi (head); Gāyatrī is the Chandas (mouth); Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is the Devatā (heart);

the consonants are the Bījas (private parts); the vowels are the Śaktis (feet); the Unmanifest is the Kīlaka (navel). My application (*viniyoga*) is for the Nyāsa of the Mātṛkās, beginning with Keśava and the others, as limbs of the Śrī Vidyā. Thus is the Nyāsa of the Ṛṣi and so forth. Now, the [Nyāsa] on the hands...

The Six-Limbed Placement (Ṣaḍaṅganyāsa): Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya śuddholkāya svāhā oṃ śrīdevyai. To the two thumbs: *namaḥ* (Salutation). To the heart: *namaḥ* (Salutation). Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ.
Iṃ caṃ īṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya śuddholkāya svāhā | Śrīpadminyai tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā | Śirase svāhā | Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ sohaṃ uṃ ṭaṃ ūṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya.
*Vīrolkāya svāhā*, to the wife of Śrī Viṣṇu, *vaṣaṭ* with the middle fingers; *śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*.
*Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ so'haṃ eṃ taṃ aiṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya vidyudulkāya svāhā*, to the bestower of boons, [with] the ring fingers.

*bhyāṃ huṃ* for the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; *oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ sohaṃ oṃ paṃ* (5) *paṃ*; *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya sahasrolkāya svāhā* for the two little fingers (*anāmikā*) of the form of the glorious lotus, *vauṣaṭ*; *netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*.

Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya haṃsaḥ so 'ham aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so 'ham oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya anantolkāya svāhā. *Śrī* ramāyai karatalakarapṛṣṭābhyāṃ phaṭ, astrāya phaṭ. Thus is the six-limbed ritual for the hands (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga*). Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*).

Having meditated thus: "His hands are beautified by the lotus of knowledge (*vidyā-raviṃda*), the bud of immortality (*amṛta-kuṃbha*), the lotus, the mace (*kaumodakī*), the conch, and the Sudarśana discus; he is the undivided essence of the self-form, whose splendor shines with a luster like lightning—[I bow] to Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa"—one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with *oṃ*.
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ keśavāya kīrtyai namaḥ on the head.
(4) Siṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ āṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ nārāyaṇāya kāntyai namaḥ on the face. (4) Ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ iṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ mādhavāya tuṣṭyai namaḥ on the right eye. (4) Ṃ hrīṃ...

*Śrīṃ klīṃ īṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ goviṃdāya puṣṭyai namaḥ* on the left [ear] (4). *Ń hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ uṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ viṣṇave dhṛtyai namaḥ* on the right ear (4). *Ń hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ūṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ madhusūdanāya* [namaḥ] on the left [nostril] (4). *Ń hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṛṃ klīṃ śrīṃ* [namaḥ] on the right [nostril] (4).

*Hrīṃ trivikramāya kriyāyai namaḥ* on the right cheek. (4) *Ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṛṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ vāmanāya dayāyai namaḥ* on the left [cheek]. (4) *Ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ḷṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīdharāya medhāyai namaḥ* on the right nostril. (4) *Ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ḹ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ hṛ* [on the left nostril].

(4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ eṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* salutation to Śīkeśa and to Harṣā on the left [lip]. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* salutation to Padmanābha and to Śuddhā on the upper lip. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ oṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* salutation to Dāmodara and to Lajjā on the lower lip. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ oṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* salutation to Vāsudeva...
*Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ auṃ klīṃ hrīṃ saṃkarṣaṇāya sarasvatyai namaḥ* on the upper teeth;
(4) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ aṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ pradyumnāya prītyai namaḥ* on the lower teeth;
(4) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ aṃḥ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aniruddhāya ratyai namaḥ* on the forehead.

Within the arm-pit: (4) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ kaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ cakriṇe jayāyai namaḥ*. At the base of the right upper arm: (4) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ khaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ gadine durgāyai namaḥ*. At the elbow: (4) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ gaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śārṅgiṇe prabhāyai namaḥ*. At the wrist: (4) *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ...*

*klīṃ ghaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ khaḍgiṇe satyāyai namaḥ* at the base of the fingers. (4) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṅaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śaṅkhine cāmuṇḍāyai namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers. (4) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ caṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ haline vāṇyai namaḥ* at the base of the left arm. (4) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ chaṃ*...

*Klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the pestle (*musalin*), to the playful one (*vilāsinī*), obeisance to the elbow (*kurpara*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ jaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the trident (*śūlin*), to the victorious one (*jayā*), obeisance to the wrist (*maṇibandha*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ jhaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the noose (*pāśin*), to the stainless one (*virajā*), obeisance to the base of the fingers (*aṅgulīmūla*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ñaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the hook (*aṅkuśin*)... [obeisance to the tips of the fingers]. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṭaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the discus (*cakrin*), to the radiant one (*tejasvinī*), obeisance to the back of the hand (*pṛṣṭhapāṇi*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṭhaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the mace (*gadādhara*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the palm of the hand (*karatala*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ḍaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the sword (*khaḍgin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the back of the hand (*pṛṣṭhapāṇi*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ḍhaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the bow (*dhanvin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the thumb (*aṅguṣṭha*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ṇaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the thunderbolt (*vajrin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the index finger (*tarjanī*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ taṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the conch (*śaṅkhin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the middle finger (*madhyamā*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ thaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the lotus (*padmin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the ring finger (*anāmikā*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ daṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the spear (*śaktin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the little finger (*kaniṣṭhikā*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ dhaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the plough (*halin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the heart (*hṛdaya*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ naṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the staff (*daṇḍin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the head (*śiras*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ paṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the club (*mudgarin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the tuft of hair (*śikhā*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ phaṃ klīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ* to the wielder of the shield (*carmin*), to the one who possesses splendor (*tejovatī*), obeisance to the armor (*kavaca*). Of this Nyāsa of the Mātṛkās beginning with Śrī Śrīkaṇṭha and Pūrṇodarī, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the Ṛṣi (head), Gāyatrī is the Chandas (mouth), Śrī Ardhanārīśvara is the Devatā (heart), Haṃ is the Bīja (anus), Saḥ is the Śakti (feet), So'haṃ is the Kīlaka (navel); it is employed as a limb of my Śrī Vidyā for the purpose of Nyāsa.

*Gaḥ* (Saṃhitā): Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers and so forth. Now follows the ritual placement of the hands and the six limbs (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*). *Hsrāṃ* to both thumbs, *namaḥ*; *namaḥ* to the heart. *Hsrīṃ* to both index fingers, *svāhā*; *svāhā* to the head.

the Unmanifest (avyakta) is the bolt (kīlaka) (mā). My application (viniyoga) (sa) is for the purpose of the worship of the Prapañcayāga-mātṛkā as an ancillary to the venerable Tripurā.

*Oṃ svāhā namaḥ* to the right eye (4). *Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ svāhā āṃ namaḥ* to the perimeter of the face (4). *Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so'haṃ svāhāṃ namaḥ* to the forehead. Having recited the seed-syllable *gaṃ* there forty-four times, [recite]: *Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ glauṃ gaṇapataye varavarada sarvajanaṃ me vaśam*.

Having recited the *mālā-mantra* of Mahāgaṇeśa eight times—namely, "Mānayasvāhā"—one should then recite the *ṛc*: "We invoke you, Gaṇapati, the Lord of hosts; I call upon the Sage among sages, the one whose fame is great, the sovereign of the highest kingdom, the Brahmin who is the Lord of Prayer (*brahmaṇaspati*). May he hear us with his protections; sit down as our accomplisher."

Having recited once: *hrīṃ krauṃ oṃ gaṃ namaḥ sarvavighnādhipāya sarvārthasiddhidāya sarvaduḥkhapraśamanāya ehyehi bhagavan sarvān khādaya (2) staṃbhaya (2) hrīṃ gaṃ gāṃ namaḥ svāhā krauṃ hrīṃ*, one should then recite this garland-mantra (*mālāmantra*) four times.
Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) three times with the pure *mātṛkā* letters upon the face: (4) *maṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ādityāya namaḥ* from the base of the right arm to its tip;
(4) *ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ somāya namaḥ* from the base of the left arm to its tip; (4) *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ bhaumāya namaḥ* from the base of the right thigh to the foot...

(4) *ṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ* to the tip of the left toe, *namaḥ* to Śukra; from the root of the left thigh to the tip of the foot, (4) *ṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ* to Budha, *namaḥ*; in the belly, (4) *ṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ* to Bṛhaspati, *namaḥ*; in the heart, (4) *ṃ paṃ phaṃ vaṃ bhaṃ maṃ* to Śanaiścara, *namaḥ*. Having thus assigned the seven planets, [this is] the Prapañca...

The Mātṛkā-nyāsa of the Caya-āgama; now, the Pūrva-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa: Oṃ. Of this venerable Pūrva-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (ṛṣi), Paṅkti is the meter (chandas), Mātṛkā-Tripurasundarī is the deity (devatā), Aiṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Sauṃḥ is the power (śakti), and Klīṃ is the peg (kīlaka) for the nyāsa as a limb of Śrīvidyā.

The application (*viniyoga*) is as follows: first, the ritual placement of the seers and other elements (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*), then the ritual placement of the hands (*karanyāsa*). OṂ AIṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ AṂ KAṂ KHAṂ GAṂ GHAṂ ṄAṂ TO THE TWO THUMBS, NAMAḤ (4). IṂ CAṂ CHAṂ JAṂ JHAṂ ÑAṂ TO THE TWO INDEX FINGERS, SVĀHĀ (4). UṂ ṬAṂ ṬHAṂ ḌAṂ ḌHAṂ ṆAṂ TO THE TWO MIDDLE FINGERS, VAUṢAṬ (4). EṂ TAṂ THAṂ DAṂ DHAṂ NAṂ TO THE TWO RING FINGERS, HUṂ (4). OṂ PAṂ PHAṂ BAṂ BHAṂ MAṂ TO THE TWO LITTLE FINGERS... (4).

*Vaṣaṭ* to the two thumbs, *Haṃ* to the two index fingers, *Aṃ* to the two middle fingers, *Aḥ* to the two ring fingers, and *Phaṭ* to the palms and backs of the hands. This is the ritual placement of the hands (*karanyāsa*).

Thus is the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): *Oṃ*, she who possesses the luster of a thousand rising suns, with full and elevated breasts, adorned with red garlands, garments, and unguents, and decorated with red ornaments; [holding] a noose, a goad, and a bow...

Having meditated thus: "I meditate upon the supreme, beautiful Mother Mātṛkā, who consists of the seats of the Goddess; she who possesses four hands shining with weapons, three resplendent eyes, and a moonlight shining from her golden crown; she who is the form of the planets, constellations, yoginīs, and zodiac signs.
Having meditated in this way, one should contemplate her as the collective totality arising from supreme bliss.

Having thus meditated upon You— who resemble the rising sun, who have the faces of horses, who possess three eyes, who hold a noose, a goad, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness in Your hands, and who are endowed with power— and upon those [goddesses] who have the luster of vermilion, who are adorned with all ornaments,
who hold a lotus in one hand while embracing their beloved with the other; having meditated thus...
One should perform the ritual of Nyāsa for Maheśānī by means of which arrangement of Nyāsa even a mortal may attain divinity;
having thus meditated, one should perform the Nyāsa: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ vighneśvarāya śriyai namaḥ* on the head (4); *āṃ vighnarājāya hriyai namaḥ* on the face (4); *iṃ vinā...* [on the right eye].
(4) *Namaḥ* to Yakāyatuṣṭi at the right eye; (4) *Namaḥ* to Śivottama and Śānti at the left [eye];

(4) *Namaḥ* to Vighnakṛt and Puṣṭi at the right ear; (4) *Namaḥ* to Vighnahartṛ and Sarasvatī at the left [ear]; (4) *Namaḥ* to Vighnarāja and Rati at the right nostril; (4) *Namaḥ* to Gaṇanātha at the left [nostril].
(4) *ṃḷṃ* salutation to Ekadanta and Kānti on the left cheek; (4) *ṃḹṃ* salutation to Dvidanta and Kāminī on the right cheek; (4) *ṃeṃ* salutation to Gajavaktra and Mohinī on the upper lip;
(4) *ṃaiṃ* salutation to Nirañjana and Jaṭā on the lower lip; (4) *ṃoṃ* salutation to Kapardin and Tīvrā.
On the upper teeth: (4) *Oṃ Dīrghavaktrāya Jvālinyai namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: (4) *Oṃ Śaṃ Kukarṇāya Nandāyai namaḥ*. On the forehead: (4) *Oṃ Aṃḥ Vṛṣabhadhvajāya Rasāyai namaḥ*.
On the chin: (4) *Oṃ Kaṃ Gaṇanāthāya Rūpiṇyai namaḥ*. At the base of the right arm: (4) *Oṃ Khaṃ Ga...*

(4) *Namaḥ* to Jeṃdrāya Mudrāya at the elbow; (4) *namaḥ* to Gaṃ Śūrpakarṇāya Jayinyai at the wrist; (4) *namaḥ* to Ṃghaṃ Trinetrāya Satyāyai at the base of the fingers; (4) *namaḥ* to Ṃṅaṃ Laṃ Vodarāya Vighneśāyai at the tips of the fingers; (4) *namaḥ* to Ṃcaṃ Mahānādāya Svarūpiṇyai on the left.

At the base of the upper arm: *Oṃ chaṃ* salutation to Caturmūrti, the bestower of desires; at the elbow: *Oṃ jaṃ* salutation to Sadāśiva, who is overwhelmed by intoxication; at the wrist: *Oṃ jhaṃ* salutation to Āmoda, the formidable one; at the base of the fingers: *Oṃ ñaṃ* salutation to Durmukha, the smoke-colored one; at the tips of the fingers: *Oṃ ṭaṃ* salutation to Sumukhī.

(4) *ṃ* *ṭhaṃ*, obeisance to Bhūti and Pramoda, to the Earth (*bhūmi*), at the armpit of the right leg; (4) *ṃ* *ḍaṃ*, obeisance to Ekapāda and Rati, at the knee; (4) *ṃ* *ḍhaṃ*, obeisance to Dvijihva and Rasā, at the ankle;
(4) *ṃ* *ṇaṃ*, obeisance to Śūra and Mānuṣī, at the base of the toes; (4) *ṃ* *taṃ*, obeisance to Vīra and Makarī, at the tips of the toes.

*Oṃ dhvaṃ namo* to Dhvajāya, on the left armpit; *oṃ thaṃ ṣaṇmukhāya vikalāyai namo* to Ṣaṇmukha and Vikalā, on the knee; *oṃ daṃ varadāya bhrūkuṭyai namo* to Varada and Bhrūkuṭī, on the ankle; *oṃ dhaṃ vāmadevāya lajjāyai namo* to Vāmadeva and Lajjā, at the base of the toes; *oṃ naṃ vakratuṇḍāya dīrghaghoṇāyai namo* to Vakratuṇḍa and Dīrghaghoṇā, on the tips of the toes.
(4) *Oṃ paṃ* salutation to Dhanurdhara and Dviranda on the right side; (4) *Oṃ phaṃ* salutation to Senānī and Yāminī on the left;

(4) *Oṃ vaṃ* salutation to Grāmaṇī and Rātri on the back; (4) *Oṃ bhaṃ* salutation to Manojña and Candrikā at the navel; (4) *Oṃ maṃ* salutation to Vimala and Śaśiprabhā on the belly; (4) *Oṃ yaṃ* salutation to Mattavāhana... [and so forth].

*Oṃ hāṃ naṃ lalāṭāya lolāyai namaḥ* in the heart; (4) *Oṃ raṃ jaṭine cañcalāyai namaḥ* on the right shoulder; (4) *Oṃ laṃ muṇḍine ṛddhyai namaḥ* on the back of the neck; (4) *Oṃ vaṃ khaḍgine durbhagāyai namaḥ* on the left [shoulder];
(4) *Oṃ śaṃ vareṇyāya subhagāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right hand; (4) *Oṃ ṣaṃ vṛṣake* [on the left hand].
(4) *Taṃ saṃbhakṣapriyāyai Durgāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand;
(4) *Haṃ meghanādāya Kālikāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot;
(4) *Laṃ gaṇapataye Kālajihvāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot.

(4) *Mkṣaṃḥ*, salutation to Gaṇeśa and to the Dispeller of Obstacles (*Vighnahāriṇī*). Thus is the *Gaṇeśanyāsa* from the navel to the top of the head. Now follows the *Graha-nyāsa*: One should meditate [on the planets] as red, white, likewise red, dark-green (*śyāma*), yellow, pale-white (*pāṇḍura*), smoke-colored and black, black and smoke-colored, and smoke-colored and smoke-colored. Ra(-).

Having meditated thus: "The principal [consorts] should be visualized as having beautiful forms, adorned with all ornaments, with their left hands resting on their thighs and their right hands granting boons; likewise, the Śaktis should be visualized holding lotuses and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, each seated upon the lap of her own beloved and adorned with all ornaments."

One should place [the seed-syllables] below the heart: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ* (16) *sūryāya reṇukāmbāyai namaḥ* at the middle of the eyebrows; *ṃ yaṃ* (4) *ṃ candrāya amṛtāmbāyai namaḥ* in the three eyes; and *ṃ kaṃ* (4) *ṃ maṅgalāya dhāmāmbāyai namaḥ* above the heart.
(4) *ṃcaṃ* (4) *ṃvu* to the wind-form of Jupiter, salutation at the throat;
(4) *ṃṭaṃ* (4) *ṃvṛ* to the glorious wind-form of Bṛhaspati, salutation in the center of the heart;
(4) *ṃtaṃ* (4) *ṃśu* to the Śākambharī wind-form of Venus, salutation at the navel; (4) *ṃpaṃ* (4) *ṃśa* to the Śakti wind-form of Saturn, salutation at the mouth.
(4) *ṃ śaṃ iṃ* to Rāhu and Kṛṣṇā, *vāyave namaḥ* on the feet; (4) *ṃ laṃ kṣaṃḥ* to Ketu and Dhūmrā, *vāyave namaḥ* on all limbs. Thus is the *grahanyāsa*. Now the *nakṣatran-yāsa*.
Now the meditation (*dhyāna*): *Oṃ*, resembling the blazing fire of time (*kālāgni*), with hands granting boons and protection.
Having meditated thus: "The Aśvinīs and the other [nakṣatras] are not excessively large, led by Aśvinī, and adorned with all ornaments," one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*).
On the forehead: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ aśvinyai namaḥ*. In the right eye: *iṃ ī bharaṇyai namaḥ*. In the left [eye]: *uṃ ū kṛttikāyai namaḥ*. In the right ear: *ṛṃ*... [and so forth].

Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ ḹṃ, obeisance to Rohiṇī on the left [shoulder] (4); ṃ Eṃ, obeisance to Mṛgaśiras on the right nostril (4); ṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to Ārdrā on the left [nostril] (4); ṃ Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to Punarvasu at the throat (4);
ṃ Kaṃ, obeisance to Tiṣya on the right shoulder (4); ṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ, obeisance to Śleṣā on the left [shoulder] (4); ṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ...

(4) *ṃ caṃ* salutation to Maghā, on the right cheek; (4) *ṃ chaṃ* salutation to Pūrvaphalgunī, on the left; (4) *ṃ jaṃ* salutation to Uttaraphalgunī, on the right wrist; (4) *ṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ* salutation to Hastā, on the left;
(4) *ṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ* salutation to Citrā, on the right breast; (4) *ṃ ḍaṃ* salutation to Svātī, on the left; (4) *ṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ*.
(4) *ṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ* obeisance to Anurādhā at the navel;

(4) *ṃ dhaṃ naṃ* obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā on the right hip; (4) *ṃ paṃ phaṃ* obeisance to Mūlā on the left [hip]; (4) *ṃ vaṃ* obeisance to Pūrvāṣāḍhā on the right thigh; (4) *ṃ bhaṃ* obeisance to Uttarāṣāḍhā on the left thigh; [and] on the right knee...
(4) Oṃ maṃ śravaṇāyai namaḥ, on the left; (4) Oṃ yaṃ raṃ dhaniṣṭhāyai namaḥ, on the right shank;
(4) Oṃ laṃ śatabhiṣajyai namaḥ, on the left; (4) Oṃ vaṃ śaṃ pūrvabhadrapadāyai namaḥ, on the right foot;
(4) Oṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ uttarabhadrapadāyai namaḥ, on the left; (4) Oṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aṃ aṃḥ revatī.
Thus ends the Nakṣatra-nyāsa. Now follows the Mahāyoginī-nyāsa.

There, in the sixteen-petaled lotus of the Viśuddhi [cakra], the meditation is as follows: *Oṃ*, she is red, with three red eyes, holding in her hands a skull-topped staff (*khaṭvāṅga*) and a trident (*śūla*) which cause fear to common folk;
in her left hands she holds a shield (*kheṭa*) and a wine-cup (*caṣaka*) filled with liquor.

One should meditate upon you, Ḍākinī— whose face is *Ṛta*, who is exceedingly fierce with terrible fangs, the crusher of the host of enemies, intent upon milk-rice (*pāyasa*), whose body is surrounded by the syllables *Mṛta* and others located in the throat— and having thus meditated, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Ḍāṃ ḍīṃ ḍūṃ ḍaiṃ ḍauṃ ḍaṃ ḥ ḍama lava ra yūṃ ḍāki.
Protect me! Protect the element of my sense of "mine"! O Goddess who brings all beings under your control, come!
Come! Accept this worship! Aiṃ Ghore Devī Hrīṃ Saḥ Paramaghore Hūṃ Ghorarūpe Ehyehi Namaḥ Cāmuṇḍe Ḍara Lakasa Haiṃ Śrī Mahātripurasundari De!

Fulfilling the desire of the goddesses of the openings: "Oṃ, I worship and bow to the venerable sandals of the pure Lord and the pure Goddess, who abide upon the pure seat. Having thus placed [the mantra] at the pericarp with the thumb and ring finger, one should then [worship] the powers of that enclosure starting from its tip and proceeding around it.

One should place [the seed-syllables]: *aṃ* to Amṛtā, *namaḥ*; *āṃ* to Ākarṣiṇī, *namaḥ*; *iṃ* to Indrā, *namaḥ*; *īṃ* to Īśānī, *namaḥ*; *uṃ* to Umā, *namaḥ*; *ūṃ* to Ūrdhvakeśinī, *namaḥ*; *ṛṃ* to Ṛddhidā, *namaḥ*;
*ṝṃ* to Ṛṣā, *namaḥ*; *ḷṃ* to Ḷṅkārā, *namaḥ*; *ḹṃ* to Ḷṃṣā, *namaḥ*.
*Maḥ*—homage to Ekapadā; *Aiṃ Aiṃ*—homage to Śvaryātmikā; *Oṃ*—homage to Okārātmikā;
*Auṃ*—homage to Auṣadhātmikā; *Aṃ*—homage to Aṃvikā; *Aṃḥ*—homage to Akṣarātmikā.
Having meditated upon [her] as Dākinī, [one proceeds] to the east and south...
Then, one should place [the mantra] in the twelve-petaled lotus of the *anāhata* [cakra]: "Oṃ!

One should visualize the Goddess of gods as dark-complexioned, holding a trident and a skull-topped staff (*khaṭvāṅga*) in her hands, bearing a sharp discus, possessing three red eyes, with a blazing face due to the radiance of her bared teeth flickering from the knitting of her brows."

One should meditate upon that Rākiṇī, who resides in the heart-lotus, who is the sole mistress of the blood-element, who is intent on pure foods, and who is delighted by wine and intoxication. Having thus meditated upon Rākiṇī along with her retinue, one should place her mantra within its pericarp: 𑀫  ī ū ai au aḥ ama la va ra yūṁ.

O Rākini, protect me! Protect my blood-element! O Goddess who brings all beings under control, come, come! Accept this worship! Aiṃ! O most terrible Goddess! Saḥ! O supremely terrible one! Hūṃ! O you of terrible form! Ehyehi! Homage to Cāmuṇḍā! Ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-ha-eṃ! O Śrī Mahā...

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with: "O Tripurasundarī, O Supreme Goddess, O Sovereign Goddess! *Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ*! I worship the venerable feet of the Lord Anāhatanātha and the goddess Anāhatarākiṇī, who reside in the sacred seat of Anāhata," one should then [worship] that enclosure on the petals all around.

One should assign the deities: (4) *ṃ kaṃ* to Kaṅkālarātri, obeisance; (4) *ṃ khaṃ* to Khātītā, obeisance; (4) *ṃ gaṃ* to Gāyatrī, obeisance; (4) *ṃ ghaṃ* to Ghaṇṭādhāriṇī, obeisance; (4) *ṃ ṅaṃ* to Ṅārṇātmikā, obeisance;
(4) *ṃ caṃ* to Cāmuṇḍāriṇī, obeisance; (4) *ṃ chaṃ* to Chāyā, obeisance; (4) *ṃ jaṃ* to Jayā, obeisance.
(4) *Namaḥ* to her who makes the sound *m-jhaṃ-m-jhaṃ*; (4) *namaḥ* to her whose nature consists of the syllables *m-ñaṃ-m-ñaṃ*; (4) *namaḥ* to her who holds a *ṭaṃ-ṭaṃka* in her hand;

(4) *namaḥ* to her who makes the sound *m-ṭhaṃ-m-ṭhaṃ*. Having meditated upon her as being like Rākinī, one should then perform the placement (*nyāsa*) in the ten-petaled lotus of the *maṇipūra*. [Therein is] Oṃ, the black goddess Trivaktrā, with three eyes and dark blue [complexion].

The lord of practitioners, having meditated upon her—who has fangs, a fierce form, and holds a thunderbolt, a spear, a staff, and a boon-granting gesture in her right and left hands; who resides in the lotus of the navel shining with ten petals; who dwells in the heart of Kālī; who stays in the flesh; and whose heart yearns for rice cooked in molasses—should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). Having thus meditated... (4) ṃ.

LĀṂ LĪṂ LŪṂ LAIṂ LAUṂ LAṂḤ LAMALAVARAYŪṂ! O Lākinī, protect me (2)! Protect my flesh-element (2)! O Goddess who brings all beings under control, come (2)! Accept this offering (2)! AiṂ! O terrible Goddess, most terrible one, HŪṂ! O you of terrible form, come, come! Homage to Cāmuṇḍā! ḌARALAKASA!
*O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, O Goddess of Devas, O Varadādevī! Ccaṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ maṃ!

I worship the sandals of the Lord Maṇipūraka-nātha, who resides at the Maṇipūraka-pīṭha and is accompanied by the Maṇipūraka-lākinī.* Having thus placed [the mantra] upon the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should place the deities of those syllables all around it.
Having meditated upon her as Lākinī, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): (4) *ṃ ḍaṃ ḍāmaryai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ ḍhaṃ ḍhaṃkāriṇyai namaḥ*;

(4) *ṃ ṇaṃ ṇaṃkāriṇyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ taṃ tāmasyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ thaṃ sthānadevyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ daṃ dākṣāyiṇyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ dhaṃ dhātryai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ naṃ nandāyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ paṃ pārvatyai namaḥ*.

(4) *ṃphaṃphetkāriṇyai namaḥ*. Having meditated upon her as [described for] Lākinī, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Then, in the six-petaled lotus at the Svādhiṣṭhāna: "Oṃ! In the six-petaled lotus known as Svādhiṣṭhāna, [I worship her] who has four faces and three eyes, who is yellow in luster, and who, full of pride, holds a trident, a rosary, a skull-cup, and the gesture of granting fearlessness."

One should meditate upon that Kākinī—who is established in the marrow-element (*medodhātu*), who is free from impurity, intoxication, and pride, who binds [the world] with joy, and whose mind is intent on the desired fruit—as she bestows the cherished result. Having thus visualized her in the ear-ornament (*karṇikā*), one should place her mantra: *ṃ kīṃ kūṃ kaiṃ kauṃ kaḥ kamalavaraya*.
Ūṃ! Protect me, O Ākīnī! O Goddess who brings all beings under control, come, come!
Accept this offering! Aiṃ! O terrible Goddess, Hrīṃ Saḥ! O most terrible one, Hūṃ! O you of terrible form, come, come! Salutations, O Cāmuṇḍā! Ḍa Ra La Ka Sa Ha Aiṃ!
O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, O best of goddesses, O boon-granting goddess! Cce Vaṃ Bhaṃ!

Having performed the placement [of mantras] with: *maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ svādhiṣṭhānapīṭhasthe svādhiṣṭhānakākinisvādhiṣṭhānanāthadeva śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*, one should place the attendant deities upon its petals all around: (4) *ṃ vaṃ vandinyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ bhaṃ bhadrakālyai namaḥ*.
(4) *ṃ maṃ* salutation to Mahāmāyā; (4) *ṃ yaṃ* salutation to Yaśasvinī; (4) *ṃ raṃ* salutation to Ramā;

(4) *ṃ laṃ* salutation to Laṃboṣṭhī—having meditated thus as in the case of Kākinī, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Then, at the Mūlādhāra, upon the pericarp of the four-petalled lotus, [one should worship] Oṃ Devī, whose nature is light, the three-eyed...

I meditate upon you, Śākinī: five-faced and laughing, with beautiful fangs, holding in your lotus-like hands a sugarcane bow and a goad, as well as a book and the gesture of wisdom (jñānamudrā); you who intoxicate all animal-natured beings from the lotus at the *mūlādhāra*, residing within the bones, delighting in mung-bean food, and rejoicing in the intoxication of honeyed wine.

Having meditated thus: *ṃsāṃ sīṃ sūṃ saiṃ sauṃ saḥ samalavarayūṃ śākinīm ā rakṣa (2) mama asthidhātuṃ rakṣa (2) sarvasattvavaśaṅkari devi āgaccha (2) imāṃ pūjāṃ gṛhṇa (2) aiṃ ghoradevi hrīṃ saḥ paramaghore hūṃ ghorarūpe ehi ehi*.

"Oṃ namo cāmuṇḍe ḍa ra la ka sa haiṃ śrī mahātripurasundari devī varade vicce vaṃ śaṃ saṃ. To the Śākini of the Mūlādhāra-pīṭha situated in the Mūlādhāra, to the Lord of the Mūlādhāra, I worship the Śrīpādukā; salutations. Having thus performed the placement (nyāsa), [one worships] her retinue upon its petals.

Likewise, having meditated upon the deities, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): (4) *Oṃ vaṃ varadāyai namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ śaṃ śaṅkhinyai namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ ṣaṃ ṣoḍhāyai namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ saṃ sassvatyai namaḥ*. Having meditated upon them as Śākinīs, one should perform the placement.
Then, in the pericarp of the Ājñā-cakra between the eyebrows: *Oṃ*, [the drop] at the midpoint of the eyebrows.

O Hā! [I bow to her] who is seated upon a lotus with six petals, beautiful and white in color; who holds in her lotus-hands the gesture of wisdom (*jñānamudrā*), a water-lily together with a rosary, and a skull-cup; who has six faces, resides within the marrow, is radiant with three eyes, is accompanied by Haṃsavatī and others, is intent on yellow rice, and is bowed to by all the gods.

Having meditated thus, "One should cause her to be nourished," [one recites]: *Hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ hamalavarayūṃ hākinīmāṃ rakṣa (2) mama majjādhātuṃ rakṣa (2) sarvasattvavaśaṅkari devi āgaccha (2) imāṃ pūjāṃ gṛhṇa (2) aiṃ ghore devi hrīṃ saḥ paramaghore hūṃ ghorarūpe ehy ehi*.

*Hīnamaścāmuṇḍe ḍaralakasahaiṃ śrīmahātripurasundarī devī varadevi cce haṃ kṣaṃḥ ājñāpīṭhasthe ājñāhākini ājñānāthadeva śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ.* On its two petals: (4) *ṃ Haṃsavatyai namaḥ*; (4) *ṃ Kṣaṃḥ Kṣamāvatyai namaḥ*. Thus.
Having meditated upon her as Hākinī, one should then place [her] in the Brahma-aperture (*brahmarandhra*) within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus with the mantra: *Oṃ Muṃ*.

One should visualize Yākinī Bhairavī seated upon the throne of the void of the skull (*ḍavyomāsana*), endowed with all petals, possessing a Yakṣiṇī-like form, with hands gracefully holding all weapons, multicolored, with fists clenched, possessing all faces, and bestowing all happiness.
One should meditate on her who is the nature of all elements (*dhātu*), whose mind is not attached to any food, who delights in the supreme Śiva, and who possesses every form.
Having thus meditated: *Yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ yaiṃ yauṃ yaṃḥ yamala-varayūṃ yākini māṃ rakṣa (2) mama śukrādi-sarva-dhātu-rakṣa (2) sarva-sattva-vaśaṃ-kuru*.

Oṃ ṛṃ oṃ ṛṃ oṃ ṛṃ namaḥ to the left nostril; oṃ ḷṃ oṃ ḷṃ oṃ ḷṃ namaḥ to the right cheek; oṃ ḹ oṃ ḹ oṃ ḹ namaḥ to the left cheek; oṃ eṃ oṃ eṃ oṃ eṃ namaḥ to the upper lip; oṃ aiṃ oṃ aiṃ oṃ aiṃ namaḥ to the lower lip;
oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ namaḥ to the upper teeth; oṃ auṃ oṃ auṃ oṃ auṃ namaḥ to the lower [teeth].

*Oṃ aṃ oṃ aṃ oṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the teeth; *Oṃ aṃḥ oṃ aṃḥ oṃ aṃḥ namaḥ* on the forehead; *Oṃ kaṃ oṃ kaṃ oṃ kaṃ namaḥ* on the tongue; *Oṃ khaṃ oṃ khaṃ oṃ khaṃ namaḥ* on the root of the right arm; *Oṃ ghaṃ oṃ ghaṃ oṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* on the right elbow; *Oṃ gaṃ oṃ gaṃ oṃ gaṃ namaḥ* on the right wrist; *Oṃ ghaṃ oṃ ghaṃ oṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* on the right fingers.
Oṃ ṅaṃ oṃ ṅaṃ oṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right fingers; oṃ caṃ oṃ caṃ oṃ caṃ namaḥ at the base of the left arm;
oṃ chaṃ oṃ chaṃ oṃ chaṃ namaḥ at the left elbow; oṃ jaṃ oṃ jaṃ oṃ jaṃ namaḥ at the left wrist;
oṃ jhaṃ oṃ jhaṃ oṃ jhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the left fingers; oṃ ñaṃ oṃ ñaṃ oṃ ñaṃ namaḥ at the [left]... the left finger.

At the tip of the right thumb: *oṃ ṭaṃ oṃ ṭaṃ oṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the right foot: *oṃ ṭhaṃ oṃ ṭhaṃ oṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. At the right knee: *oṃ ḍaṃ oṃ ḍaṃ oṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the right ankle: *oṃ ḍhaṃ oṃ ḍhaṃ oṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the right toes: *oṃ ṇaṃ oṃ ṇaṃ oṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the right toes: *oṃ taṃ oṃ taṃ oṃ taṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the left foot: *oṃ thaṃ oṃ...*

OṂ THAṂ OṂ THAṂ OṂ THAṂ NAMAḤ to the left knee; OṂ DAṂ OṂ DAṂ OṂ DAṂ NAMAḤ to the left ankle; OṂ DHAṂ OṂ DHAṂ OṂ DHAṂ NAMAḤ to the base of the toes of the left foot; OṂ NAṂ OṂ NAṂ OṂ NAṂ NAMAḤ to the tips of the toes of the left foot; OṂ PAṂ OṂ PAṂ OṂ PAṂ NAMAḤ to the right side; OṂ PHAṂ OṂ PHAṂ OṂ PHAṂ NAMAḤ to the left side; OṂ VAṂ OṂ VAṂ OṂ VAṂ NAMAḤ to the back.
Oṃ bhaṃ oṃ bhaṃ oṃ bhaṃ namaḥ at the navel; oṃ maṃ oṃ maṃ oṃ maṃ namaḥ in the stomach; oṃ yaṃ oṃ yaṃ oṃ yaṃ namaḥ in the heart;

oṃ raṃ oṃ raṃ oṃ raṃ namaḥ on the right shoulder; oṃ laṃ oṃ laṃ oṃ laṃ namaḥ on the back; oṃ vaṃ oṃ vaṃ oṃ vaṃ on the left shoulder; oṃ śaṃ oṃ śaṃ oṃ śaṃ namaḥ from the heart to the end of the right hand.

Oṃ ṣaṃ oṃ ṣaṃ oṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ from the heart to the left hand; oṃ saṃ oṃ saṃ oṃ saṃ namaḥ from the heart to the right foot; oṃ haṃ oṃ haṃ oṃ haṃ namaḥ from the heart to the left foot; oṃ laṃ oṃ laṃ oṃ laṃ namaḥ from the feet to the navel; oṃ kṣaṃ oṃ kṣaṃ oṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ from the navel to the crown of the head—thus [the assignment].

The *tattva-nyāsa* (1): *śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the head; *śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ śrīṃ āṃ namaḥ* on the face; *śrīṃ iṃ śrīṃ iṃ śrīṃ iṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *śrīṃ īṃ śrīṃ īṃ śrīṃ īṃ namaḥ* on the left eye;
*śrīṃ uṃ śrīṃ uṃ śrīṃ uṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ śrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ* on the left ear.

*Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ* to the right nostril; *Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Śrīṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ* to the left [nostril]; *Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Śrīṃ Ḷṃ Namaḥ* to the right cheek; *Oṃ Ḷṃ Oṃ Ḷṃ Oṃ Ḷṃ Namaḥ* to the left [cheek]; *Śrīṃ Eṃ Śrīṃ Eṃ Śrīṃ Eṃ Namaḥ* to the upper lip;
*Śrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Namaḥ* to the lower lip; *Śrīṃ Oṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ*.

*Śrīṃ oṃ namaḥ* upon the upper teeth; *śrīṃ auṃ śrīṃ auṃ śrīṃ auṃ namaḥ* upon the lower teeth; *śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the forehead; *śrīṃ aṃḥ śrīṃ aṃḥ śrīṃ aṃḥ namaḥ* on the tongue; *śrīṃ kaṃ śrīṃ kaṃ śrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right arm; *śrīṃ khaṃ śrīṃ khaṃ śrīṃ khaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *śrīṃ gaṃ*.
Śrīṃ gaṃ śrīṃ gaṃ śrīṃ gaṃ namaḥ to the wrist; śrīṃ ghaṃ śrīṃ ghaṃ śrīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ to the base of the fingers;
śrīṃ ṅaṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ to the tips of the right fingers; śrīṃ caṃ śrīṃ caṃ śrīṃ caṃ namaḥ to the base of the left arm;
śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ śrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ to the elbow; śrīṃ jaṃ śrīṃ jaṃ śrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ to the wrist.

*Śrīṃ jhaṃ śrīṃ jhaṃ śrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *śrīṃ ñaṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *śrīṃ ṭaṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right foot; *śrīṃ ṭhaṃ śrīṃ ṭhaṃ śrīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *śrīṃ ḍaṃ śrīṃ ḍaṃ śrīṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ* at the ankle; *śrīṃ ḍhaṃ śrīṃ ḍhaṃ śrīṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right toes; *śrīṃ ṇaṃ*.
*Śrīṃ ṇaṃ śrīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *śrīṃ taṃ śrīṃ taṃ śrīṃ taṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left foot;

*śrīṃ thaṃ śrīṃ thaṃ śrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ śrīṃ daṃ namaḥ* at the ankle; *śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes; *śrīṃ naṃ śrīṃ naṃ śrīṃ naṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the toes; *śrīṃ paṃ śrīṃ paṃ*.

*Śrīṃ paṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *Śrīṃ phaṃ Śrīṃ phaṃ Śrīṃ phaṃ namaḥ* on the left; *Śrīṃ vaṃ Śrīṃ vaṃ Śrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the back; *Śrīṃ bhaṃ Śrīṃ bhaṃ Śrīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *Śrīṃ maṃ Śrīṃ maṃ Śrīṃ maṃ namaḥ* in the stomach; *Śrīṃ yaṃ Śrīṃ yaṃ Śrīṃ yaṃ namaḥ* in the heart; *Śrīṃ raṃ Śrīṃ raṃ Śrīṃ raṃ namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *Śrīṃ laṃ*.

*Śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ namaḥ* on the hump [of the back]; *śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ śrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ śrīṃ śaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the right hand; *śrīṃ ṣaṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand; *śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ śrīṃ saṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot; *śrīṃ haṃ śrīṃ*... [and so forth].

*Haṃ śrīṃ haṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand; *śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ śrīṃ laṃ namaḥ* from the feet to the navel; *śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ śrīṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ* from the navel to the head—this is the second nyāsa. *Klīṃ aṃ klīṃ aṃ klīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the head; *klīṃ āṃ klīṃ āṃ klīṃ āṃ namaḥ* on the mouth.

*klīṃ iṃ klīṃ iṃ klīṃ iṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *klīṃ īṃ klīṃ īṃ klīṃ īṃ namaḥ* on the left; *klīṃ uṃ klīṃ uṃ klīṃ uṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *klīṃ ūṃ klīṃ ūṃ klīṃ ūṃ namaḥ* on the left; *klīṃ ṛṃ klīṃ ṛṃ klīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* on the right nostril; *klīṃ ṝṃ klīṃ ṝṃ klīṃ ṝṃ namaḥ* on the left; *klīṃ ḷṃ klīṃ ḷṃ klīṃ*.
*Ḷṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; *klīṃ ḷṃ klīṃ ḷṃ klīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* on the left [cheek];

*klīṃ eṃ klīṃ eṃ klīṃ eṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; *klīṃ aiṃ klīṃ aiṃ klīṃ aiṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *klīṃ oṃ klīṃ oṃ klīṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the upper teeth; *klīṃ auṃ klīṃ auṃ klīṃ auṃ namaḥ* on the lower teeth; *klīṃ aṃ klīṃ aṃ klīṃ* [on the palate].

Aṃ namaḥ on the forehead; Klīṃ aṃḥ klīṃ aṃḥ klīṃ aṃḥ klīṃ aṃḥ namaḥ on the tongue; Klīṃ kaṃ klīṃ kaṃ klīṃ kaṃ namaḥ at the root of the right arm; Klīṃ khaṃ klīṃ khaṃ klīṃ khaṃ namaḥ at the elbow; Klīṃ gaṃ klīṃ gaṃ klīṃ gaṃ namaḥ at the wrist; Klīṃ ghaṃ klīṃ ghaṃ klīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ at the base of the fingers; Klīṃ... [at the tips of the fingers].
Ṅaṃ klīṃ ṅaṃ klīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ—on the tips of the fingers; klīṃ caṃ klīṃ caṃ klīṃ caṃ namaḥ—at the base of the left arm;

klīṃ chaṃ klīṃ chaṃ klīṃ chaṃ namaḥ—at the elbow; klīṃ jaṃ klīṃ jaṃ klīṃ jaṃ namaḥ—at the wrist; klīṃ jhaṃ klīṃ jhaṃ klīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ—at the base of the fingers; klīṃ ñaṃ klīṃ ñaṃ klīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ—at the [tips of the] fingers...

At the base of the spine: *klīṃ ṭaṃ klīṃ ṭaṃ klīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ*. At the root of the right foot: *klīṃ ṭhaṃ klīṃ ṭhaṃ klīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ*. At the knee: *klīṃ ḍaṃ klīṃ ḍaṃ klīṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*. At the ankle: *klīṃ ḍhaṃ klīṃ ḍhaṃ klīṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the toes: *klīṃ ṇaṃ klīṃ ṇaṃ klīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*. At the tips of the toes: *klīṃ taṃ klīṃ taṃ klīṃ taṃ namaḥ*.

At the base of the left foot: *klīṃ thaṃ klīṃ thaṃ klīṃ thaṃ namaḥ*; at the knee: *klīṃ daṃ klīṃ daṃ klīṃ daṃ namaḥ*; at the ankle: *klīṃ dhaṃ klīṃ dhaṃ klīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ*; at the base of the toes: *klīṃ naṃ klīṃ naṃ klīṃ naṃ namaḥ*; at the tips of the toes: *klīṃ paṃ klīṃ paṃ klīṃ paṃ namaḥ*; on the right side: *klīṃ phaṃ klīṃ phaṃ klīṃ phaṃ*.

*Namaḥ* on the left side; *klīṃ vaṃ klīṃ vaṃ klīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the back; *klīṃ bhaṃ klīṃ bhaṃ klīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *klīṃ maṃ klīṃ maṃ klīṃ maṃ namaḥ* in the belly; *klīṃ yaṃ klīṃ yaṃ klīṃ yaṃ namaḥ* in the heart;
*klīṃ raṃ klīṃ raṃ klīṃ raṃ namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *klīṃ laṃ klīṃ laṃ klīṃ laṃ namaḥ* on the neck.

*klīṃ vaṃ klīṃ vaṃ klīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *klīṃ śaṃ klīṃ śaṃ klīṃ śaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right hand; *klīṃ ṣaṃ klīṃ ṣaṃ klīṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the left hand; *klīṃ saṃ klīṃ saṃ klīṃ saṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right foot; *klīṃ haṃ klīṃ haṃ klīṃ haṃ namaḥ* from the heart... [to the end of the left foot].
From the beginning of the left foot to its end: *klīṃ laṃ klīṃ laṃ klīṃ laṃ namaḥ*. From the beginning of the foot to the navel:

*klīṃ kṣaṃ klīṃ kṣaṃ klīṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*. From the navel to the top of the head: [this is the third nyāsa]. *Hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the head. *Hrīṃ āṃ hrīṃ āṃ hrīṃ āṃ namaḥ* on the face. *Hrīṃ iṃ hrīṃ...* [and so forth].

*Hrīṃ īṃ namaḥ* to the right eye; *hrīṃ īṃ hrīṃ īṃ hrīṃ īṃ namaḥ* to the left [eye]; *hrīṃ uṃ hrīṃ uṃ hrīṃ uṃ namaḥ* to the right ear; *hrīṃ ūṃ hrīṃ ūṃ hrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ* to the left [ear]; *hrīṃ ṛṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the right nostril; *hrīṃ ṛṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ* to the left [nostril]; *hrīṃ ḷṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ* to the right [cheek].

On the cheek: *gaṃḍe* hrīṃḷṃ hrīṃḷṃ hrīṃḷṃ namaḥ; on the left [cheek]: *vāme* hrīṃ eṃ hrīṃ eṃ hrīṃ eṃ namaḥ; on the upper lip: *ūrdhvoṣṭe* hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ aiṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ; on the lower lip: *adharoṣṭe* hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ; on the upper teeth: *ūrdhvadaṃteṣu* hrīṃ auṃ hrīṃ auṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; on the lower teeth: *adhodaṃteṣu* hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ; on the forehead: *lalāṭe* hrīṃ aṃḥ hrīṃ aṃḥ.

*Hrīṃ aṃḥ namaḥ* on the tongue; *hrīṃ kaṃ hrīṃ kaṃ hrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right arm; *hrīṃ khaṃ hrīṃ khaṃ hrīṃ khaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *hrīṃ gaṃ hrīṃ gaṃ hrīṃ gaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist; *hrīṃ ghaṃ hrīṃ ghaṃ hrīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers;
*hrīṃ ṅaṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *hrīṃ caṃ hrīṃ caṃ hrīṃ caṃ namaḥ* on the left [arm].

*Hrīṃ chaṃ hrīṃ chaṃ hrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right arm; *hrīṃ jaṃ hrīṃ jaṃ hrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ* at the elbow; *hrīṃ jhaṃ hrīṃ jhaṃ hrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ* at the wrist; *hrīṃ ñaṃ hrīṃ ñaṃ hrīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *hrīṃ ṭaṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right foot; *hrīṃ ṭhaṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *hrīṃ ḍaṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ hrīṃ*.

Ḍaṃ namaḥ to the ankles; Hrīṃ ḍhaṃ Hrīṃ ḍhaṃ Hrīṃ ḍhaṃ Hrīṃ namaḥ to the bases of the toes; Hrīṃ ṇaṃ Hrīṃ ṇaṃ Hrīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ to the tips of the toes; Hrīṃ taṃ Hrīṃ taṃ Hrīṃ taṃ namaḥ to the root of the left foot; Hrīṃ thaṃ Hrīṃ thaṃ Hrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ to the knee; Hrīṃ daṃ Hrīṃ daṃ Hrīṃ daṃ namaḥ to the ankle; Hrīṃ dhaṃ Hrīṃ dhaṃ Hrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ to the base of the toes; Hrīṃ... [to the tip of the toes].

Naṃ hrīṃ naṃ hrīṃ naṃ namaḥ on the tips of the fingers; hrīṃ paṃ hrīṃ paṃ hrīṃ paṃ namaḥ on the right side; hrīṃ phaṃ hrīṃ phaṃ hrīṃ phaṃ namaḥ on the left side; hrīṃ vaṃ hrīṃ vaṃ hrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ on the back; hrīṃ bhaṃ hrīṃ bhaṃ hrīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ on the navel; hrīṃ maṃ hrīṃ maṃ hrīṃ maṃ namaḥ on the belly; hrīṃ yaṃ hrīṃ yaṃ hrīṃ yaṃ namaḥ on the heart; hrīṃ raṃ hrīṃ raṃ... [on the chest].

*Hrīṃ raṃ namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *hrīṃ laṃ hrīṃ laṃ hrīṃ laṃ namaḥ* on the back of the neck (*kakudi*); *hrīṃ vaṃ hrīṃ vaṃ hrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *hrīṃ śaṃ hrīṃ śaṃ hrīṃ śaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right hand; *hrīṃ ṣaṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the left hand;
*hrīṃ saṃ hrīṃ saṃ hrīṃ saṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the right... [end of text].

To the end of the feet: *hrīṃ haṃ hrīṃ haṃ hrīṃ haṃ namaḥ*. From the heart to the end of the left foot: *hrīṃ laṃ hrīṃ laṃ hrīṃ laṃ namaḥ*. From the feet to the navel: *hrīṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*. From the navel to the top of the head: [as above]. This is the fourth nyāsa. *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the head.

*Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, [the root mantra], *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the face; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, [the root mantra], *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, [the root mantra], *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left [eye]; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, [the root mantra], *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ* on the right ear; *hrāṃ*.

*Hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* in the right nostril; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* in the right ear.
Ḍe hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ on the left;
hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ on the upper lip;
hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ on the lower lip; hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ on the upper [face].

On the upper teeth: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. On the forehead: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. On the tongue: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ*.

*Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* to the elbow; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* to the wrist; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* to the base of the fingers; *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* to the tips of the fingers.

*Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left arm. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the elbow. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the wrist. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ...*

*Ḷṃ Ḹṃ namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right foot; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ Ḹṃ namaḥ* at the knee.

*Ḷṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ gulphe* | *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ aṅgulīmūle* | *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ aṅgulyagre* | *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ vāmapāda-*

At the root: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. At the knees: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. At the ankles: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ*. At the base of the fingers: *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ...*

*Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Mūlaṃ Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* on the right side; *Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Mūlaṃ Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* on the left side; *Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Mūlaṃ Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* on the back; *Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ*.

*Ḷṃ Ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the stomach; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the heart; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* at the right shoulder.

*Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, root mantra, *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the hump [of the back]. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, root mantra, *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* on the left shoulder. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, root mantra, *hrāṃ hrāṃ* from the heart to the end of the right hand. *Hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ*, root mantra, *hrāṃ hrāṃ*.

*Ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ* [and] *ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ* [and] *ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot; *hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ mūlaṃ hrāṃ hrāṃ ṛṃ*.

*Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* from the feet up to the navel; *Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Mūlaṃ Hrāṃ Hrāṃ Ṛṃ Ṛṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Namaḥ* from the navel up to the head—this is the fifth placement (*nyāsa*). *Mūlaṃ Aṃ Mūlaṃ Kṣaṃ Mūlaṃ Kṣaṃ Namaḥ* on the head; *Mūlaṃ Āṃ Mūlaṃ Laṃ Mūlaṃ Laṃ Namaḥ* on the face; *Mūlaṃ Iṃ Mūlaṃ...* [and so forth].

*Haṃ* mūla *haṃ* *namaḥ* to the right eye; *mūla* *īṃ* mūla *saṃ* mūla *saṃ* *namaḥ* to the left [eye]; *mūla* *uṃ* mūla *ṣaṃ* mūla *ṣaṃ* *namaḥ* to the right ear; *mūla* *ūṃ* mūla *śaṃ* mūla *śaṃ* *namaḥ* to the left [ear]; *mūla* *ṛṃ* mūla *vaṃ* mūla *vaṃ* *namaḥ* to the right nostril; *mūla* *ṝṃ* mūla *laṃ* mūla *laṃ* *namaḥ* to the left [nostril]; *mūla* *ḷṃ* mūla... [to the right nostril].

*Laṃ raṃ mūlaṃ raṃ namaḥ* on the right cheek; *mūlaṃ ḷṃ mūlaṃ yaṃ mūlaṃ yaṃ namaḥ* on the left [cheek]; *mūlaṃ eṃ mūlaṃ maṃ mūlaṃ maṃ namaḥ* on the upper lip; *mūlaṃ aiṃ mūlaṃ bhaṃ mūlaṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* on the lower lip; *mūlaṃ oṃ mūlaṃ vaṃ mūlaṃ bhaṃ namaḥ* on the upper teeth; *mūlaṃ auṃ mūlaṃ phaṃ mūlaṃ phaṃ namaḥ* on the lower teeth; *mūlaṃ aṃ mūlaṃ*.

*Mūla* *Paṃ* *Namaḥ* on the forehead; *Mūla* *Aṃḥ* *Mūla* *Naṃ* *Mūla* *Naṃ* *Namaḥ* on the tongue; *Mūla* *Kaṃ* *Mūla* *Dhaṃ* *Mūla* *Dhaṃ* *Namaḥ* at the root of the right arm; *Mūla* *Khaṃ* *Mūla* *Daṃ* *Mūla* *Daṃ* *Namaḥ* at the elbow; *Mūla* *Gaṃ* *Mūla* *Thaṃ* *Mūla* *Thaṃ* *Namaḥ* at the wrist; *Mūla* *Ghaṃ* *Mūla* *Taṃ* *Mūla* *Taṃ* *Namaḥ* at the base of the fingers of the right hand; *Mūla* *Ṅaṃ* *Mū*...

*Laṃ* *naṃ* *mūlaṃ* *naṃ* *namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *mūlaṃ* *caṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ḍhaṃ* *mūḍhaṃ* *namaḥ* at the root of the left arm; *mūlaṃ* *chaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ḍaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ḍaṃ* *namaḥ* at the elbow; *mūlaṃ* *jaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ṭhaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ṭhaṃ* *namaḥ* at the wrist; *mūlaṃ* *jhaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ṭaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ṭaṃ* *namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; *mūlaṃ* *ñaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ñaṃ* *mūlaṃ* *ñaṃ* *namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; *mū*... [the text continues].

*Laṃ ṭaṃ mūlaṃ jhaṃ mūlaṃ jhaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the right foot; *mūlaṃ ṭhaṃ mūlaṃ jaṃ mūlaṃ jaṃ namaḥ* at the knee; *mūlaṃ ḍaṃ mūlaṃ chaṃ mūlaṃ chaṃ namaḥ* at the ankle; *mūlaṃ ḍhaṃ mūlaṃ caṃ mūlaṃ caṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes; *mūlaṃ ṇaṃ mūlaṃ ṅaṃ mūlaṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ* at the tips of the toes; *mūlaṃ taṃ mūlaṃ ghaṃ mūlaṃ ghaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the left foot.

*Mūlaṃ thaṃ mūlaṃ gaṃ mūlaṃ gaṃ namaḥ* at the knees; *mūlaṃ daṃ mūlaṃ khaṃ mūlaṃ khaṃ namaḥ* on the left ankle; *mūlaṃ dhaṃ mūlaṃ kaṃ mūlaṃ kaṃ namaḥ* at the base of the toes; *mūlaṃ naṃ mūlaṃ aṃḥ mūlaṃ aṃḥ* at the tips of the toes; *mūlaṃ paṃ mūlaṃ aṃ mūlaṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the right side; *mūlaṃ phaṃ mūlaṃ auṃ mūlaṃ auṃ namaḥ* on the left side.

*Mūla* (the root mantra), *vaṃ*, *mūla*, *oṃ*, *mūla*, *oṃ namaḥ* on the back; *mūla*, *bhaṃ*, *mūla*, *aiṃ*, *mūla*, *aiṃ namaḥ* at the navel; *mūla*, *maṃ*, *mūla*, *eṃ*, *mūla*, *eṃ namaḥ* in the belly; *mūla*, *yaṃ*, *mūla*, *ḷṃ*, *mūla*, *ḷṃ namaḥ* in the heart; *mūla*, *raṃ*, *mūla*, *ḷṃ*, *mūla*, *ḷṃ namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *mūla*, *laṃ*, *mūla*, *ṛṃ*, *mūla*, *ṛṃ namaḥ* on the hump (back of the neck); *mūla*, *vaṃ*, *mūla*, *ṛṃ*, *mūla*.

*Laṃ Ṛṃ Namaḥ* on the left shoulder; *Mūlaṃ Śaṃ Mūlaṃ Ūṃ Mūlaṃ Ūṃ Namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right hand; *Mūlaṃ Ṣaṃ Mūlaṃ Uṃ Mūlaṃ Uṃ Namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the left hand; *Mūlaṃ Saṃ Mūlaṃ Īṃ Mūlaṃ Īṃ Namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the right foot; *Mūlaṃ Haṃ Mūlaṃ Iṃ Mūlaṃ Iṃ Namaḥ* from the heart to the end of the left foot; *Mūlaṃ Laṃ*.

*Mūlam āṃ mūlam āṃ namaḥ* from the feet up to the navel; *mūlam kṣaṃ mūlam aṃ mūlam aṃ namaḥ* from the navel up to the head—this is declared to be the sixteen-fold placement (*ṣoḍhā-nyāsa*) of the King of Mantras, Tripurā. Having performed the placement in this manner, the practitioner becomes Bhairava himself, possessing the eight supernatural powers beginning with *aṇimā*.
He shall undoubtedly be the Lord Himself; He is Hara, He is Hari—O Goddess, there is no doubt in this.
Thus ends the Ṣoḍhā-mātṛkā-nyāsa. Now begins the Mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa:
Of this Śrī Mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa, the Seer (Ṛṣi) is Śrī Parabrahman, the Metre (Chandas) is Jagatī, and the Deity (Devatā) is Śrī Mārdhanārīśvara. Haṃ.

The seed-syllable is *saḥ*, the power (*śakti*) is *auṃ*, and the peg (*kīlaka*) is *auṃ*. This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the attainment of worldly enjoyment and liberation through the limbs of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, in the performance of the venerable Great Ṣoḍhā Nyāsa. Having thus placed [the mantras] with palms joined in reverence, one should then perform the placement upon the fingers of the hands: (4) *ṃ hsāṃ hsāṃḥ īśānāya namaḥ* on the two thumbs. (6) *ṃ*... [and so forth].

(6) *Hsīṃ hsīṃ*—*namaḥ* to Tatpuruṣa; on the two index fingers. (6) *Hsaṃḥ hsūṃḥ*—*namaḥ* to Aghora; on the two middle fingers. (6) *Hsaiṃḥ hsaiṃḥ*—*namaḥ* to Vāmadeva; on the two ring fingers. (6) *Hsauṃ hsauṃ*—*namaḥ* to Sadyojāta; on the two little fingers. (6) *Hsaṃḥ hsaṃḥ*—*namaḥ* to Īśāna; on the head. (6) *Hseṃḥ*... [etc.]
HSEṂḤ TATPURUṢĀYA NAMAḤ on the face; (6) Ṃ HSUṂḤ SHUṂḤ AGHORĀYA NAMAḤ on the heart; (6) Ṃ HSIṂḤ SHIṂḤ VĀMADEVĀYA NAMO on the liṅga; (6) Ṃ HSAṂḤ SHAṂḤ SADYOJĀTĀYA NAMAḤ on the feet;
(6) Ṃ HSOṂḤ SHOṂḤ ĪŚĀNĀYŪRDHVAVAKTRĀYA NAMAḤ on the head; (6) Ṃ HSEṂḤ SHEṂḤ TATPURUṢĀYA...
(6) *Oṃ hsuṃḥ shuṃḥ* to the face of Aghora, the southern face, salutation to the southern ear;

(6) *Oṃ hsiṃḥ shiṃḥ* to the face of Vāmadeva, the northern face, salutation to the left ear; (6) *Oṃ hsaṃḥ shaṃḥ* to the face of Sadyojāta, the western face, salutation to the hollow of the navel (*caurakūpa*). Thus it is said.

The placement of the five *ktras* (*ktrapañcakanyāsa*) should be performed in sequence with the thumbs and other fingers, one face at a time: (6) *Oṃ hsaṃḥ shāṃḥ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ* (6) (6) *Oṃ hsīṃ hsīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā* (6) (6) *Oṃ hsūṃ shūṃ madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ* (6) (6) *Oṃ hsaiṃ shaiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ* (6) (6) *Oṃ hsauṃ* [kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ vauṣaṭ] (6)

*Śauṃ* to the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; *ṃ hsaḥ shaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). This constitutes the sixfold placement (*ṣaḍanyāsa*). The visualization (*dhyāna*): [He is] situated within a forest of wish-fulfilling trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*) on a delightful Golden Island (*svarṇadvīpa*) arising in the midst of an ocean of nectar.

Seated upon a lotus on a glorious lion-throne made of the nine gems within a pavilion of rubies, resting in the center of a triangle, possessing the splendor of hundreds of moons and suns— [therein dwells] the Goddess Ambikā in her half-form.

(4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ṛṃ* salutation to the one in the form of a field (*kṣetra-rūpa*) and to Ekamātṛ; [place this] in the left nostril. (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ṛṃ* salutation to the one in the form of a forest (*vana-rūpa*) and to Kamalavāsinī; [place this] in the right nostril. (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ḷṃ* salutation to the one in the form of a hermitage (*āśrama-rūpa*) and to Indirā; [place this] on the right cheek. (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ḹṃ* salutation to the one in the form of a cave (*guhā-rūpa*) and to Mahāmāyā.

(4) *Namaḥ* vāme *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ eṃ* to her who has the form of a river, to Irāmā, *namaḥ*. On the upper lip: (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ aiṃ* to her who has the form of a lotus, to Padmā, *namaḥ*. On the lower lip: (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ oṃ* to her who has the form of that which is born from moisture, to the beloved of Nārāyaṇa, *namaḥ*. On the upper teeth: (4) *ṃ hsauṃ shauṃ auṃ* to her who has the form of that which is born from sweat, to Siddhalakṣmī, *namaḥ*. On the lower...

On the teeth: (4) 𑁠ṃhsauṃshauṃaṃaṃ ṇaṃ to the Egg-born form, to Rājyalakṣmī, salutation! On the forehead: (4) 𑁠ṃhsauṃshauṃaṃḥ ṭaṃ to the Womb-born form, to Mahālakṣmī, salutation! On the tongue: (4) 𑁠ṃhsauṃshauṃkaṃ to the Sweat-born form, to Āryā, salutation! At the base of the right arm: (4) 𑁠ṃhsauṃshauṃkhaṃ to the Sprout-born form, to Umā, salutation! On the knee...

(4) *Oṃ hsaum shraum* to Caṇḍikā, who has the form of a skull, salutations! At the wrist; (4) *Oṃ hsaum shraum* to Durgā, who has the form of wood, salutations! At the base of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ hsaum shraum* to Śivā, who has the form of a blink, salutations! At the tips of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ hsaum shraum* to Aparṇā, who has the form of breath, salutations!

At the base of the left upper arm: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ chaṃ* salutation to Aiṃvikā, who has the form of a ghaṭikā. At the elbow: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ jaṃ* salutation to Satī, who has the form of a muhūrta. At the wrist: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ jhaṃ* salutation to Aiśvaryā, who has the form of a prahara. At the base of the fingers: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ñaṃ* salutation to Śāmbhavī, who has the form of a day (*dinam*).

*Namaḥ* to the tip of the finger, *aṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ṭaṃ saṃ*, obeisance to *Dhyārūpā* (the form of twilight), to *Īśānī*. *Namaḥ* to the base of the right foot, *aṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ṭhaṃ*, obeisance to *Pārvatī*, who is the form of night. *Namaḥ* to the knee, *aṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ḍaṃ*, obeisance to *Sarvamaṅgalā*, who is the form of the lunar days (*tithi*). *Namaḥ* to the ankle, *aṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ḍhaṃ*, obeisance to *Dākṣāyaṇī*, who is the form of the days of the week (*vāra*).

At the base of the left toes: (4) *Oṃ hsaḥ śauṃ ṇaṃ* salutation to Haimavatī, who has the form of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
