*Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ dhaṃ naṃ namaḥ* to the Noble Māyāmbā Devī at the base of the right upper arm; *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ paṃ phaṃ namaḥ* to the Noble Kuṇḍalinīmbā Devī, who is served by the family of thousands of millions of Bhairavas, at the left upper arm; *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ sahasrakoṭigaṇeśvarakulasevitāyai māyāmbādevyainamaḥ* on the right arm.

Mūla: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ baṃ bhaṃ*, salutation to the Goddess Ekālinī, who is served by a multitude of thousands of crores of Vaṭukas; [place this] on the left arm. Mūla: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ maṃ yaṃ*, salutation to the Goddess Kālarātrī, who is served by a multitude of thousands of crores of Kṣetrapālas; [place this] on the right shoulder. Mūla: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ raṃ laṃ*, [salutation to the multitude of thousands of crores...]
Salutation to the Blessed Goddess Ambādevī, served by the host of Pramathas—on the left shoulder. The root mantra: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ vaṃ śaṃ*.
Salutation to the Goddess Sarveśvaryā, served by thousands of millions of Brahma-families—on the right ear.
The root mantra: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ ṣaṃ saṃ*. Salutation to the Goddess Sarvājñā, served by thousands of millions of Kula-families.

In the left ear: the root mantra *oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ haṃ laṃ*, followed by *namaḥ* to the Goddess who is served by the lineage of a thousand crores of Rudras and who is the all-pervading power (*sarvakatravādevī*). On the forehead: the root mantra *oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ kṣaṃ*, followed by *namaḥ* to the Goddess who is the Kula-power (*kulaśakti*) and who is served by the lineage of a thousand crores of moving and non-moving beings (*carācarakula*). In the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*): the root mantra *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃ shauṃ*.
*Am ām*, etc., up to *kṣam*: "Salutation to the venerable Goddess Parāmbā, who is the embodiment of all deities;

shauṃ hsauṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ on all limbs. This is the placement of the deities (*daivata-nyāsa*). Now, the placement of the Mātṛkās (*mātṛkā-nyāsa*): *Mūla*: *Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ kaṃ (4)ṃ* [to] *Āṃ kṣāṃ maṅgalāyai vā devyai āṃ*, together with the lineage of infinite millions of Earth-dwellers (*bhūcarī-kula*).

*Kṣāṃ* to the goddess Kṣamā, accompanied by infinite millions of *bhūta*s; *aṃ kṣaṃ* to Maṅgalanātha; *aṃ kṣaṃ* salutations (*namaḥ*) to the lord Asitāṅgabhairava at the *mūlādhāra*. The root mantra is *oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ caṃ*. *Īṃ lāṃ* to the goddess Carcikā, accompanied by infinite millions of *khecarī* clans; *īṃ lāṃ* to the goddess Māheśvarī... [infinite millions].

Salutation to the Lord Carcika along with his family of infinite crores of Vetālas; salutation to the Lord Ruru-Bhairava at the Svādhiṣṭhāna [cakra]. The root mantra: OṂ HSAUṂ SHAUṂ ṬAṂ (4). Salutation to the Goddess Yogīśvarī Ambā along with her family of infinite crores of Pālālacarīs; salutation to the Goddess Kaumārīśvarī Ambā along with her family of infinite crores of Piśācas.
Obeisance to Yogīśvara Kulanātha along with his family; obeisance to Caṇḍabhairava Nātha.
In the Maṇipūra [cakra], the root mantra is OṂ HSAUṂ SHAUṂ TAṂ (4) Ṃ. Obeisance to ṚṂ SĀṂ HARA (-) Siddhyambā Devī, and to ṚṂ SĀṂ Vaiṣṇavyambā Devī, along with infinite crores of Apasmāra families.
Obeisance to Ṛṃsaṃhara Siddhanātha; obeisance to Ṛṃsaṃkrodhabhairava Nātha. In the Anāhata [cakra], the root mantra is:
Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ paṃ (4) anaṃtakoṭisahacarīkulasahitāya ḷṃ ṣāṃ bhaṭṭiny-ambādevyai; ḷṃ ṣāṃ vārāhy-ambādevyai anaṃtakoṭibrahmarākṣasakulasahitāya ḷṃ ṣaṃ bhaṭṭināthāya.

Yaṃṣaṃ, obeisance to Unmattabhairavanātha; in Viśuddha, the root mantra: Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ yaṃ iṃ, obeisance to the Goddess Śāṃ, who is accompanied by the family of infinite koṭis of Giricarīs; iṃ vā devyai aiṃ śāṃ, obeisance to the Goddess Indrāṇī, who is accompanied by the family of infinite koṭis of Ceṭakas; aiṃ śaṃ kilakila nāthāyai aiṃ śaṃ, obeisance to Kapālabhairavanātha.

*Yanamaḥ* (salutation) at the *ājñā* [center]: *Mūla-oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ namo 'nantakoṭivanacarīkulasevitāyai oṃ vāṃ kālarātryai vāṃ devyai oṃ vāṃ cāmuṇḍādevyai anantakoṭipretakulasahitāyai oṃ vaṃ kālarātrināthāya oṃ vaṃ bhīṣaṇabhairavanāthāya namaḥ* on the forehead (*bhāla*). *Mūla*.
Oṃ hsauṃ shauṃ laṃ kṣaṃ! Salutation to the Mother Goddess Aṃḥlāṃ Bhīṣaṇā, accompanied by a host of infinite crores of aquatic beings;

to the Mother Goddess Aṃḥlāṃ Mahālakṣmī, accompanied by a host of infinite crores of Kūṣmāṇḍas; to the Lord Aṃlaṃ Bhīṣaṇanātha; to the Lord Aṃlaṃ Saṃhārabhairava—namas! [At] the Brahma-randhra: Mūla-mantra Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃ shauṃ aṃ.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) on all the limbs with "Āṃ" and so forth up to "Kṣāṃ," [reciting] "Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Parāmbā, the deity of all the Mothers, Bhairavas, and others;

Shauṃ Hsauṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ," one whose body is thus consecrated should meditate upon the God with undistracted mind: [He who resides] within a thousand-petaled lotus, possessing the luster of all the cool-rayed [moon], His lotus-hands granting boons and fearlessness, and adorned with pure perfumes, flowers, and excellent garments.
One should meditate upon the Guru, who has a serene face and eyes, who embodies the form of all deities, and who is seated upon a swan on the crown of the head;

this indeed is the preliminary meditation. O Goddess, for one who performs the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, he becomes manifest as Paraśiva himself; there is no doubt that the practitioner is capable of both restraint and grace. He who performs the ritual placement known as Mahāṣoḍhā day after day [is honored] by all the gods.
O Pārvatī, there is no doubt that those who perform this nyāsa called Mahāṣoḍhā worship Him;

indeed, an area extending ten yojanas in every direction is declared to be a divine field (divyakṣetra). O Goddess, wherever a practitioner goes after performing this nyāsa, there he finds prosperity, victory, gain, and personal prowess, O Beloved—provided he is one who has performed the Mahāṣoḍhā nyāsa, for it is not for the ignorant.

If one pays homage in this manner for a month, one attains liberation from death, provided that Śiva himself is the protector; and he who performs this Nyāsa known as Vajrapañjara— O Maheśvarī, the beings dwelling in the heavens, the atmosphere, on the earth, in mountains, waters, and forests, including Uddaṇḍas,
Bhūtas, Vetālas, Devas, Rākṣasas, Grahas, and others, shall not look upon him with minds seized by fear.

O Goddess, even all the gods, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, as well as sages, yogis, and lords of ascetics, perform this nyāsa known by six names. What is the use of speaking much, O beloved? This nyāsa is dear to me. O Goddess, one should not speak of it to one who is not a son, nor should one reveal it to one who is not a disciple. One attains perfection through ignorance [of worldly knowledge] when one performs this secret nyāsa. From this...

This bestows the direct attainment of the state of divinity for those devoted to the Supreme (Tparatama); there is no doubt about this in the world—I speak the truth, the absolute truth. Entry into the Urdhvāmnāya, contemplation upon the grace of Parā, and the thorough knowledge of the Mahāṣoḍhā—these are not the fruit of minor austerity. Thus ends the Mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa. Now, [the ritual] prescribed by rule...
Seated in the *māyā-āsana*, with the fluctuations of the mind fixed upon the *mūlādhāra*, one should contemplate the root mantra or the *praṇava* a single time.

Having filled the breath through the *iḍā* and brought it to the *mūlādhāra*, one should retain that air by closing the nostrils with the thumb, ring finger, and little finger. At the moment of retention (*kumbhaka*), while reciting the root mantra or the *praṇava* four times, one should again [fill] the *piṅgalā*.

Reciting that same [mantra] twice as many times as the duration of the throat [retention], one should slowly exhale; this is one *prāṇāyāma*. Again, filling [the breath] by the same method as it was exhaled and retaining it in the same manner, one should exhale from the other side; this is another. In this very way, alternating [the sequence], one should perform it twenty times, or sixteen, twelve, or six times, at the beginning of the practice.

At the end, *prāṇāyāma* (breath control) should be performed; having thus performed *prāṇāyāma*, one should perform the recollection (*smaraṇa*) of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and other attributes of the Root Mantra (*mūlavidyā*). *Oṃ, of this King of Mantras of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, the Seer is the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the Metre is Paṅkti, the Deity is the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, and the first peak-syllable is Aiṃ.*

The seed-syllable *sauṃḥ* is the third peak (*kūṭa*), the power (*śakti*); *klīṃ* is the second peak, the pin (*kīlaka*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of my fourfold aims of human life (*puruṣārtha*) at the beginning of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and so forth. Thus is the ritual placement of the seers (*ṛṣi*) and others. Now follows the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*): *aiṃ*, the first peak, *namaḥ* to both thumbs; *klīṃ*, the second peak, *svāhā* to both index fingers.

*Sauṃḥ*, the third *kūṭa*, with the two middle fingers, *vaṣaṭ*; *Aiṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, with the two ring fingers, *huṃ*; *Klīṃ*, the second *kūṭa*, with the two little fingers, *vauṣaṭ*; *Sauṃḥ*, the third *kūṭa*, with the palms and backs of the hands, *phaṭ*. Thus is the *karanyāsa*. Likewise is the *ṣaḍaṅganyāsa* for those who worship the venerable sixteen-syllable mantra: *Śrīṃ Hrīṃ*.
*klīṃ aiṃ sauṃḥ hṛdayāya namaḥ; oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śirase svāhā; ke ī la hrīṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ; ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ kavacāya huṃ; sa ka la hrīṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ;

sauṃḥ aiṃ klīṃ śrīṃ astrāya phaṭ.* Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Having performed the triple *tāla* with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), [one should perform] the snapping of fingers (*choṭikā*).

One should perform the binding of the ten directions with [the mantras]. Now follows the placement of the Yoga-pīṭha (yogapīṭhanyāsa): having meditated upon one's own body as the Yoga-pīṭha, which has four legs formed by the two shoulders and the two thighs, one should perform the placement. Om.
Now the meditation: [one's] body, produced from the five elements, enveloped by all the sense organs, and complete with the thirty-six principles...

The auspicious abode of all enjoyments, possessing six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*), sixteen supports (*ṣoḍaśādhāra*), three targets (*trilakṣya*), and five voids (*vyomapañcaka*), that is the sacred seat (*pīṭha*) which is the abode of all seats and is eternally worshipped by consciousness. Thus, one's own body should be known as the lineage of the *Kula* to be worshipped.
Then, the hero, free from all impurities, should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon it: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ maṇḍūkāya namaḥ*.

At the *mūlādhāra*: (4) *Oṃ Kālāgnirudrāya namaḥ*. At the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: (4) *Oṃ Mūlaprakṛtyai namaḥ*. At the *maṇipūra*: (4) *Oṃ Ādhāraśaktyai namaḥ*. At the *anāhata*: (4) *Oṃ Kūrmāya namaḥ*. In the heart, at that very place: (4) *Oṃ Anantāya namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ Varāhāya namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ Pṛthivyai namaḥ*; (4) *Oṃ Paścimāyai namaḥ*.
In the direction of the gods (divi-loma): (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of sugarcane juice; (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of wine; (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of clarified butter;

(4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of milk. In the middle of that: (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of milk; (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of curds; (4) *Namaḥ* to the ocean of salt. [And the syllables] from *aṃ āṃ*, etc., ending with *kṣāṃ*.

Salutation to the island consisting of excellent jewels, adorned with the syllable *va*. To its west: *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ*, salutation to the flower-jewel (*puṣparatna*). To the southwest (*naiṛta*): *ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aṃḥ*, salutation to the lapis lazuli jewel (*vaiḍūryaratna*).

To the south: *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ*, salutation to the sapphire jewel (*nīlaratna*). To the southeast (*āgneya*): *caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ*, salutation to the coral jewel (*vidrumaratna*). To the east...
To the *ṭaṃ* [syllable], obeisance to the pearl-jewel in the northeast (*īśāna*). To the *taṃ* [syllable], obeisance to the emerald-jewel in the north (*uttara*).

To the *paṃ* [syllable], obeisance to the diamond-jewel in the northwest (*vāyavya*). To the *yaṃ iṃ* [syllables], obeisance to the agate-jewel in the southwest (*nairṛtya*). In the central section, to the *śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ* [syllables], obeisance to the topaz-jewel. To the *laṃ kṣaṃḥ* [syllables], obeisance to the ruby-jewel in its center.
In the center of the square: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ svarṇaparvatāya namaḥ*. Above that: *(4) naṃdanodyānāya namaḥ*.
In its center: *(4) kalpavṛkṣebhyo namaḥ*. In its center: *(4) vasantādiṣaṛtubhyo namaḥ*.
To its west: *(4) indriyāśvebhyo namaḥ*. To its east: *(4) indriyārthagajebhyo namaḥ*.
Homage in the center to the ground of variegated jewels; homage to the Mistress of the Kāla-cakra in its western direction;

homage to the Mistress of the Mudrā-cakra in the southwest; homage to the Mistress of the Mātṛ-cakra in the south; homage to the Mistress of the Ratna-cakra in the southeast; homage to the Mistress of the Deśa-cakra in the east; [homage to] the Guru in the northeast.

(4) *Namaḥ* to Cakreśvarī in the north; (4) *namaḥ* to Tattvacakreśvarī in the northwest; (4) *namaḥ* to Graha-cakreśvarī in the center; (4) *namaḥ* to the moat of the waters of compassion; *namaḥ* to the golden rampart; in its center, *namaḥ* to the jeweled pavilion;
in its four corners, beginning from the southwest and proceeding counter-clockwise, (4) *namaḥ* to the Śakti Kālarūpiṇī.
Salutation (4) to the power whose form is the earth; salutation (4) to the power whose form is space;
salutation (4) to the power whose form is sound. In the center, salutation to the Saṅgīta-yoginīs.
Right there, salutation to the entire circle of secret and manifest Siddha-yoginīs. In the middle of that, salutation to the jeweled altar.
"Obeisance to the white umbrella; obeisance to the jewel lion-throne"—having thus placed these in the heart, [one should place]:

"Obeisance to the Brahma-corpse-seat" on the right shoulder; "obeisance to the Viṣṇu-corpse-seat" on the left shoulder; "obeisance to the Rudra-corpse-seat" on the left thigh; "obeisance to the Īśvara-corpse-seat" on the right thigh; and "hsauṃḥ sadā" on the entire body.

*Oṃ namaḥ śivamahāpretāsanāya namas* (Salutation to the Great Corpse-seat of Śiva). Again, on the right shoulder: *namaḥ dharmāya* (Salutation to Dharma); on the left shoulder: *namaḥ jñānāya* (Salutation to Jñāna); on the left thigh: *namaḥ vairāgyāya* (Salutation to Vairāgya); on the right thigh: *namaḥ aiśvaryāya* (Salutation to Aiśvarya); on the face: *namaḥ adharmāya* (Salutation to Adharma);
on the left side: *namaḥ ajñānāya* (Salutation to Ajñāna); at the navel: *namaḥ avairāgyāya* (Salutation to Avairāgya); on the right side [of the navel]: *namaḥ*.
Salutation to Anaiśvarya; again, salutation to Māyā in the heart; salutation to Vidyā; salutation to Ananta;
salutation to Padma; salutation to Dharma; salutation to Ānandakanda; salutation to Saṃvināla;
salutation to the petals consisting of Prakṛti; salutation to the filaments consisting of Vikāra; [salutation to] the fifty...

Salutation to the single pericarp, which embodies all the principles (tattvas) enriched by the seed-syllables of the three debts (*ṛṇabīja*). Within that very [pericarp]: salutation to the solar disc (*arka-maṇḍala*);

salutation to the lunar disc (*soma-maṇḍala*); salutation to the fiery disc (*vahni-maṇḍala*). Salutation to Sattva, whose nature is awakening; salutation to Rajas, whose nature is primordial matter (*prakṛti*); salutation to Tamas, whose nature is delusion (*moha*). Āṃ.
Salutation to the Self (ātman); salutation to the inner self (antarātman); salutation to the supreme self (paramātman); *hrīṃ*, salutation to the self that is knowledge (jñānātman).

In the four directions and the center of the pericarp (*karṇikā*): salutation to the self that is the principle of knowledge (*jñānatattva*); salutation to the self that is the principle of the arts (*kalātattva*); salutation to the self that is the principle of illusion (*māyātattva*); salutation to the self that is the principle of wisdom (*vidyātattva*); [salutation] to the self that is the supreme principle (*paratattva*).

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) starting from the west and proceeding clockwise with the mantra *Namaḥ*, and having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with *Klīṃ sarvaśaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ*, one should visualize the Śrīcakra in its center.

[Then one should worship] the entire collection of the manifest, the secret, the more secret, the oral tradition (*sampradāya*), the Kula, the Kaula, the Nigarbha, the secret, the supreme-secret, and the beyond-supreme-secret...

Having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) on all limbs with the mantra: *oṃ rā-parā-ti-rahasya-yoginī-cakra-pādukābhyo namaḥ*, one should perform the pervasive placement on all limbs as follows:

the first *kūṭa* with "Salutation to the Self of the Body" (*śarīrātmane namaḥ*), the second *kūṭa* with "Salutation to the Self of the Intellect" (*buddhyātmane namaḥ*), and the third *kūṭa* with "Salutation to the Self of the Vital Breath" (*prāṇātmane namaḥ*). Then, [placing] at the heart...

In the front corner of the northeast corner: *aiṃ kāmarūpapīṭhāya namaḥ*. In the northeast (*īśāna*): *klīṃ pūrṇagiripīṭhāya namaḥ*. In the southeast (*āgneya*): *sauṃḥ jālandharapīṭhāya namaḥ*. In the *bindu* situated in the center of that: *turīyavidyā-mahodḍyānapīṭhāya namaḥ*. In the *binducakra* situated in the center, [worship] the ninefold golden [lotus].

*Oṃ āṃ sauṃḥ*, salutation to the lotus-seat of the thousand-petaled lotus on the back of the right shoulder. *Aiṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ*, salutation to the lotus-boat-seat of Tripureśvarī on the back of the right ear.
*Hrīṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ*, salutation to the seat of the self of the goddess Tripurasundarī on the right forehead. Dakṣa... [text continues]
In the eyes: *hklīṃ hsauṃḥ tripuravāsinī sarvacakrāsanāya namaḥ*. On the right side of the chin: *hsaiṃḥ hasakalrīṃ tripurāśrī sarvamantrāsanāya namaḥ*. In the three corners of the heart:
*hlīṃ klīṃ vlīṃ tripuramālinī sādhyasiddhāsanāya namaḥ*. (4) *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ*.
Ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃḥ.
[Salutations to] Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Śuddhavidyā, Māyā, Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati, Puruṣa, Prakṛti, Ahaṃkāra, Buddhi, Manas, Śrotra, Tvak, Cakṣus, Jihvā, Ghrāṇa, Vāk, Pāṇi... [Pāda].

"Obeisance to the one whose nature consists of the thirty-six *tattvas*—the feet, anus, genitals, sound, touch, form, taste, smell, ether, air, fire, water, and earth—who is the seat of the *yogapīṭha* of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī.
With this, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) over all limbs. This is the *yogapīṭha-nyāsa*. Now, the *śrīcakra-nyāsa*.

Having performed there the six-limbed nyāsa (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa) of the root-mantra (mūlavidyā), beginning with the rṣi and so forth, he should perform meditation as follows: "Oṃ, one should first contemplate one's own body as having the form of the Śrīcakra, free from the appearance of skin and other [elements],
resembling the blazing fire of cosmic destruction (kālāgni), consisting of all supports, a form endowed with all parts (kalās), and containing all the gods."

The region adorned by Laya-pīṭheśvarī is the supreme Brahman, beautiful with bliss, and dear to the deities. In that place, one should always worship the Goddess with all royal offerings. Thereafter, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa), which takes the form of the Śrīcakra.
Having thus meditated upon one's own body as being the form of the Śrīcakra, one should perform the placement as follows: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ.

(4) *Laṃ* to Indra, salutation to the right big toe; (4) *Raṃ* to Agni, salutation to the right knee; (4) *Ṭaṃ* to Yama, salutation to the right side; (4) *Kṣaṃ* to Nairṛta, salutation to the right shoulder; (4) *Vaṃ* to Varuṇa, salutation to the left shoulder;
(4) *Yaṃ* to Vāyu, salutation to the left side; (4) *Saṃ* to Soma, salutation to the left knee; (4) *Haṃ* to Īśāna...

(4) *Śāṇāyanamaḥ* to the left big toe; (4) *Āṃ Brahmaṇenamaḥ* to the *brahmarandhra*; (4) *Āṃ Anantāyanamaḥ* to the *mūlādhāra*; (4) *Gaṃ Gaṇeśāyanamaḥ* to the left knee; (4) *Kṣaṃ Kṣetrapālāyanamaḥ* to the left shoulder;

(4) *Mohanābhyāṃ kāmeśvara-kāmeśvarī-cāpābhyāṃ namaḥ*. (4) *Māṃ hrīṃ vaśīkaraṇābhyāṃ kāmeśvara-kāmeśvarī-pāśābhyāṃ namaḥ*. (4) *Kroṃ kroṃ staṃbhanābhyāṃ kāmeśvara-kāmeśvarī-aṅkuśābhyāṃ namaḥ*. In the front corner of the triangle: (4) *M* [the first *kūṭa*].

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī, who is the nature of Rudra as the power of Will (*icchā-śakti*), who resides at the seat (*pīṭha*) of Kāmagiri within the Fire-wheel (*agni-cakra*), who is the essence of the Lord Mitrīśa, and who presides over the waking state (*jāgrat*). [At] the front corner of the triangle:
*ṃ* (the second *kūṭa*), who is the nature of the Lord Ṣaṣṭhīśa at the seat of Jālandhara within the Sun-wheel (*sūrya-cakra*), [presiding over] the dream state (*svapna*).

Salutation to the goddess Śrī-Vajreśvarī, who is the nature of Viṣṇu, whose essence is the power of knowledge (*jñāna-śakti*), and who presides over the tenth state (*daśā*) in the right corner of the triangle.
(4) *Ūṃ*, the third seed-syllable (*kūṭa*), in the Moon-wheel (*soma-cakra*) at the Pīṭha of Pūrṇagiri, whose essence is Uḍḍīśanātha,

*Oṃ Brahmātmaśaktiśrībhagamālinīdevyai namaḥ*—[place this] in the heart. (4) *Oṃ Haṃsraiṃ Hasakalarīṃ Hsauṃḥ Tripurāṃvikācakreśvaryai namaḥ*. To its right: (4) *Oṃ Icchāsiddhyai namaḥ*. "May the lords of the circles of deities, together with their siddhis, weapons, vehicles, and retinues, be worshipped with all offerings; *namaḥ*. Thus one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). This is the eighth enclosure-placement (*aṣṭamāvaraṇanyāsa*).

Then, having recited the fifteen-syllable root mantra, one should perform the pervasive placement [with the formula]: "Salutation to the wheel consisting of universal bliss" (*sarvānandamayacakrāya namaḥ*).

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the Supreme Brahman and Self-power (*ātmaśakti*), the presiding deity over the state beyond the fourth (*turyātīta*) and the fourth (*turya*) itself, who resides at the Cakra of the Brahma-randhra in the sacred seat of Uḍḍiyāna."

Having thus placed [the mantra] in the heart, recite the fifteen-syllable root mantra followed by: *śrīmahātripurasundarī cakreśvaryai namaḥ*. Salutation to the Goddess; on her right (4)ṃ salutation to Sarvakāmasiddhi; on her left (4)ṃ hrasraiṃ hasakalarīṃ hsauṃḥ, salutation to the Trikhaṇḍā Mudrā—having thus performed the placement upon the heart: (4)ṃ Eṣā aparāparāparātirahasyayoginī sarvānandamayī vaiṃda-cakre parabrahmasvarūpiṇī parāmṛtaśaktiḥ.

The sovereign of all mantras, the sovereign of all vidyās, the sovereign of all pīṭhas, the sovereign of all yogas, the sovereign of all speech, the sovereign of all siddhis; the Mother of the origin of the entire world, together with her cakra, her deities, her ocean [of retinue], her siddhis, her weapons, her seat, her vehicle, her retinue, her ornaments, and all [her attendants].
