(4) *ṃ laṃ* namaḥ to the left earring; (4) *ṃ kṣaṃḥ* namaḥ to the crown. This is the *bhūṣaṇanyāsa* (assignment of ornaments). Now follows the *kāmaratyānyāsa*: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ *aṃ* namaḥ to Kāmarati, on the head;
(4) *āṃ* namaḥ to Prīti, the giver of desire, on the face; (4) *iṃ* namaḥ to Kāminī, the beloved, on the right [ear].

(4) *ṃīṃ* Kāntimatī Mohinī, salutation on the left; (4) *ṃuṃ* Kāmagā Kamalā, salutation on the right ear; (4) *ṃūṃ* Kāmacārā Vilāsinī, salutation on the left; (4) *ṃṛṃ* Kāminī Kalpalatā, salutation on the right nostril; (4) *ṃṛṃ* Kāmuka Śyāmā, salutation on the left...

(4) *Oṃ* *Mlaṃ* salutation to the one who increases desire, who possesses a pure smile, on the right cheek; (4) *Oṃ* *Lṃ* salutation to the dark-complexioned one, who is smiling, on the left [cheek]; (4) *Oṃ* *Eṃ* salutation to the lovely one, who has large eyes, on the upper lip; (4) *Oṃ* *Aiṃ* salutation to the one who delights, who licks [the lips], on the lower lip; (4) *Oṃ* *Oṃ* salutation to the Lord of Rati, who is naked, on the chin.

(4) *Namaḥ* to the upper teeth; *Oṃ* to Ratipriya and Vāmā, *namaḥ* to the lower teeth. (4) *Ṃaṃ* to Rātrinātha and Kuvjikā, *namaḥ* to the forehead. (4) *Ṃaṃḥ* to Ramākānta and Kāntā, *namaḥ* to the tongue. (4) *Ṃkaṃ* to Ramamāna and Nityā, *namaḥ* to the root of the right arm. (4) *Ṃkhaṃ* to Niśā...

(4) *Caṃ* to Carāya, to Kalyāṇī, salutation to the left shoulder; (4) *ṅaṃ* to Nandakāya, to Bhoginī, salutation to the elbow; (4) *ghaṃ* to Nandāya, to Kāmadā, salutation to the wrist; (4) *ṅaṃ* to Nandine, to Sulocanā, salutation to the base of the fingers; (4) *caṃ* to Nandayitre, to Sulocanā, salutation to the tips of the fingers; (4) *chaṃ* to the root of the left arm.

*Oṃ paṃ vāṇāyamardinyai namaḥ* on the elbow; (4) *Oṃ jaṃ ratipriyāya kalahapriyāyai namaḥ* on the wrist; (4) *Oṃ jhaṃ puṣpadhanvane vārāhyai namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ ñaṃ mahādhnuṣe sumukhyai namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; (4) *Oṃ ṭaṃ bhrāmakāya ramāyai namaḥ* on the right side of the foot.
(4) *ṃ* Ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Bhīṣma and Jaṭinī at the knee; (4) *ṃ* Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Bhrāmaṇa and Pālinī at the ankle;

(4) *ṃ* Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Bhramaṇa and Śikhinī at the base of the toes; (4) *ṃ* Ṇaṃ, obeisance to Śānta and Mugdhā at the tips of the toes; (4) *ṃ* Taṃ, obeisance to Bhrāmaka and Rāmā at the left foot-socket.

(4) *ṃ thaṃ bhr̥ṃgāya bhramāyai namaḥ* on the knee; (4) *ṃ daṃ bhrāntacārāya lolāyai namaḥ* on the ankle; (4) *ṃ dhaṃ bhramāvahāya cañcalāyai namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; (4) *ṃ naṃ mohanāya dīrghajihvāyai namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers; (4) *ṃ paṃ mohakārāya ratipriyāyai namaḥ* on the right side; (4) *ṃ phaṃ*.
(4) *Oṃ* *vaṃ*, obeisance to Moha (Delusion), the one with tremulous eyes, on the left; (4) *Oṃ* *bhaṃ*, obeisance to Madana (Passion), the bee-like woman, on the back;

(4) *Oṃ* *maṃ*, obeisance to Manmatha (the Mind-born), the intoxicating woman, at the navel; (4) *Oṃ* *yaṃ*, obeisance to Mātaṅga (the Elephant), the garlanded woman, in the belly; (4) *Oṃ* *raṃ*, obeisance to Bhṛṅganātha (Lord of Bees), the female swan, in the heart.

On the right shoulder: *Oṃ laṃ* to the singer (*gāyaka*), who faces all directions, salutation to the one who delights the world (*jagadānandinī*). On the left [shoulder]: *Oṃ śaṃ* to the dancer (*nartaka*), salutation to the beautiful woman (*ramaṇī*). From the heart to the right hand: *Oṃ ṣaṃ* to the playful one (*khelaka*), salutation to splendor (*kānti*). From the heart to the left hand: *Oṃ saṃ* to the one beyond the mind (*unmanāya*).

*Oṃ* *Ka* *La* *Kaṃṭhyai* *Namaḥ* from the heart to the right hand; (4) *Oṃ* *Ṃ* *Haṃ* *Matta-kāyavṛkodaryai* *Namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot; (4) *Oṃ* *Ṃ* *Laṃ* *Vilāsinyai* *Meghaśvāsāyai* *Namaḥ* from the feet to the navel; (4) *Oṃ* *KṢaṃḥ* *Kṣobhavardhanāya* *Puruṣottamāya* *Namaḥ* from the navel to the crown of the head. Thus is the *Kā*.

The Maratīnyāsa. Now, the Nyāsa of the fifty Tripuras: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Kāminī Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the head. (4) Āṃ Mohinī Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the mouth. (4) Iṃ Madanā Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the right eye. (4) Īṃ Unmādinī Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the left [eye]. (4) Uṃ...
(4) *Oṃ* Drāviṇī Tripurā, salutations to her on the right ear; (4) *Oṃ* Khecarī Tripurā, salutations to her on the left [ear];

(4) *Oṃ* Ṛṃ Kalāvatī Tripurā, salutations to her on the right nostril; (4) *Oṃ* Ṛṃ Ghaṭikā Tripurā, salutations to her on the left [nostril]; (4) *Oṃ* Ḷṃ Kledinī Tripurā, salutations to her on the right cheek; (4) *Oṃ* Ḷṃ Śivādūtī Tripurā, salutations to her on the [left] cheek.

On the left lip: (4) *ṃeṃ subhagātripurāyai namaḥ*. On the upper lip: (4) *ṃaiṃ bhagātripurāyai namaḥ*. On the lower lip: (4) *ṃoṃ viśvaśāntitripurāyai namaḥ*. On the upper teeth: (4) *ṃauṃ mahālakṣmītripurāyai namaḥ*. On the lower teeth: (4) *ṃaṃ kaulinītripurāyai namaḥ*. *La*.

On the left temple: (4) *ṃaṃ* to the Tripurā Maṅgalasukeśvarī, salutation. On the tongue: (4) *ṃkaṃ* to the Tripurā Kulamālinī, salutation. At the base of the right arm: (4) *ṃkhaṃ* to the Tripurā Vyāpinī, salutation. At the elbow:
(4) *ṃgaṃ* to the Tripurā Bhagānandā, salutation. At the wrist: (4) *ṃghaṃ* to the Tripurā Vāgīśvarī, salutation.

At the base of the left fingers: (4) *Oṃ ṅaṃ vaśaṅkarī-tripurāyai namaḥ*. At the tips of the left fingers: (4) *Oṃ caṃ piṅgalā-tripurāyai namaḥ*. At the base of the left arm: (4) *Oṃ chaṃ bhagasarpiṇī-tripurāyai namaḥ*.
At the elbow: (4) *Oṃ jaṃ sundarī-tripurāyai namaḥ*. At the wrist: (4) *Oṃ jhaṃ nīlapatākāyai...*

(4) *Oṃ* *ñaṃ* salutation to Tripurā, the Ancient One; at the base of the fingers. (4) *Oṃ* *ṭaṃ* salutation to Tripurā, the Mistress of Siddhas; on the right foot. (4) *Oṃ* *ṭhaṃ* salutation to Tripurā, the Unfailing One; at the knee. (4) *Oṃ* *ḍaṃ* salutation to Tripurā, She Who Wears a Garland of Jewels; at the ankle. (4) *Oṃ* *ḍhaṃ* salutation to Tripurā, Maṅgalā.

(4) *Namaḥ* to the finger-base: *Aṃ Ṇaṃ Bhagamālinī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. (4) *Namaḥ* to the fingertip: *Āṃ Taṃ Nityā Tripurāyai namaḥ*. (4) *Namaḥ* to the left foot: *Iṃ Thaṃ Raudrī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. (4) *Namaḥ* to the knee:
*Īṃ Daṃ Vāmeśvarī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. (4) *Namaḥ* to the ankle: *Uṃ Dhaṃ Ambikā Tripurāyai namaḥ*. (To the toes...)
At the root of the left leg: *ṃ naṃ Aṭṭahāsā Tripurāyai namaḥ*. At the tips of the fingers:

*ṃ paṃ Āpyāyinī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. On the right side: *ṃ phaṃ Vajreśvarī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. On the left: *ṃ vaṃ Kṣobhiṇī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. On the back: *ṃ bhaṃ Śāmbhavī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. At the navel: *ṃ maṃ Stambhinī Tripurāyai namaḥ*. In the belly: *ṃ*.

Yaṃ Anāmātripurāyai namaḥ, in the heart; (4) Ṃ Raṃ Ratnātripurāyai namaḥ, on the right shoulder; (4) Ṃ Laṃ [omitted], on the back of the neck; (4) Ṃ Vaṃ Aparājitātripurāyai namaḥ, on the left [shoulder]; (4) Ṃ Śaṃ Saṃ Saṃvartikātripurāyai namaḥ, from the heart to the right hand; (4) Ṃ Ṣaṃ Vimalātripura...

*Rāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the left hand; (4) *Ṃ Saṃ Ghorātripurāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the right foot; (4) *Ṃ Haṃ Aghorātripurāyai namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot; (4) *Ṃ Laṃ Vindubhairavītripurāyai namaḥ* from the feet to the navel; (4) *Ṃ Kṣaṃḥ Sarvākarṣiṇītri-*
*Purāyainamaḥ*, from the navel up to the crown of the head—this is the placement (*nyāsa*) of the fifty *purās*.
Now follows the placement of the sixteen *kāmakalās*: on the right foot, *(4)ṃaṃ śraddhākalāyai namaḥ*;
on the right calf, *(4)ṃāṃ prītikalāyai namaḥ*; on the right knee, *(4)ṃiṃ ratikalāyai namaḥ*; on the...

(4) *Oṃ Āṃ* salutation to Dhṛtikālā on the right breast; (4) *Oṃ Ūṃ* salutation to Kāntikalā on the base of the right arm; (4) *Oṃ Ṛṃ* salutation to Manoramākalā on the right side of the face; (4) *Oṃ Ṝṃ* salutation to Manobhavākalā on the right head; [on the left...]

On the crown of the head: (4) *Oṃ ṃḷṃ* salutation to the digit Manonmādinī. On the left side of the face: (4) *ṃḹṃ* salutation to the digit Mohinī. At the root of the left arm: (4) *ṃ eṃ* salutation to the digit Dīpinī. On the left chest: (4) *ṃ aiṃ* salutation to the digit Ṣoḍaśī. On the left thigh: (4) *ṃ oṃ* salutation to the digit Vaśaṅkarī. On the left knee...
(4) *ṃauṃ* obeisance to the digit *Aurajinī* on the left calf; (4) *ṃaṃ* obeisance to the digit *Subhagā* on the left foot;

(4) *ṃaṃḥ* obeisance to the digit *Priyadarśinī* on the left foot. Thus ends the placement (*nyāsa*) of the digits of Kāma. Now follows the placement of the digits of Soma: on the right back part [of the body], (4) *ṃaṃ* obeisance to the digit *Pūṣā*. On the left back part... [and so forth].
(4) *Māṃ* Oṃ, obeisance to the digit of fame (*mānyaśaḥ-kalā*) on the back of the right shoulder; (4) *Iṃ* Oṃ, obeisance to the digit of good-will (*sumanā-kalā*) on the back of the right neck;
(4) *Īṃ* Oṃ, obeisance to the digit of passion (*ratikalā*) in the right ear; (4) *Uṃ* Oṃ, obeisance to the digit of affection (*prīti-kalā*) in the right eye;
(4) *Ūṃ* Oṃ, obeisance to the digit of fortitude (*dhṛti-kalā*) in the right nostril; (4) *Ṛṃ* Oṃ, [obeisance to the digit of memory] on the right forehead.
(4) *Namaḥ* to the *Siddhi-kalā*, on the right head; (4) *namaḥ* to the *Saumya-kalā*, on the left head;
(4) *namaḥ* to the *Marīci-kalā*, on the left forehead; (4) *namaḥ* to the *Aṃśumālinī-kalā*, on the left nostril;
(4) *namaḥ* to the *Aṅgirā-kalā*, on the left eye; (4) *namaḥ* to the *Śaśinī-kalā*.

(4) *Oṃ* *namaḥ* to the digit *Ākalā*, on the left ear; (4) *Oṃ* *namaḥ* to the digit *Saṃpūrṇamaṇḍalākalā*, on the back of the left neck; (4) *Oṃ* *namaḥ* to the digit *Tuṣṭikalā*, on the back of the left shoulder;
(4) *Oṃ* *namaḥ* to the digit *Amṛtākalā*, on the left back. This is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the lunar digits (*somakalā*). Now, [the solar digits].

The placement (*nyāsa*) of the goddesses of speech, beginning with Vaśinī: On the head: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ (16) vlūṃ*—salutation to Vaśinī, the goddess of speech. On the forehead: *(4) ṃ kaṃ (4) ṃ kala hrīṃ*—salutation to Kāmeśvarī, the goddess of speech. Between the eyebrows: *(4) ṃ caṃ (4) ṃ navalīṃ*—salutation to Modinī, the goddess of speech. In the throat: *(4) ṃ ṭaṃ (4) ṃ hlyūṃ*... [the mantra continues].

Salutation to the goddess Vimalā-vāgdevatā in the heart. (4) ṃ taṃ (4) ṃ jmrīṃ, salutation to the goddess Aruṇā-vāgdevatā in the navel. (4) ṃ paṃ (4) ṃ hasalavayūṃ, salutation to the goddess Jayinī-vāgdevatā in the *mūlādhāra*.
(4) ṃ yaṃ (3) ṃ jhamarayuṃ, salutation to the goddess Sarveśvarī-vāgdevatā from the *mūlādhāra* down to the tips of the feet.
(4)ṃ Śaṃ (5)ṃ Kṣmrīṃ, obeisance to Kaulinī Vāgdevatā—thus is the *nyāsa* of the goddesses of speech, beginning with Vaśinī.

Now follows the *nyāsa* of the four seats (*catuṣpīṭha*): at the *mūlādhāra*, (4)ṃ, the first *kūṭa*; in the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*), on the seat of Kāmagiri, whose nature is that of Mitrīśanātha, the presiding deity over the state of waking, [and] by means of the power of will (*icchāśakti*).

Salutation to the goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī, the power of the self of Tamarudra, in the heart. (4) Salutation to the goddess Śrī Vajeśvarī, the power of Viṣṇu who is of the nature of the power of knowledge, the presiding deity of the dream state, whose essence is the Lord Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha at the Jālandhara seat in the solar wheel, [and who is] the second *kūṭa*, between the eyebrows.

(4)ṃ To the third peak (kūṭa), in the lunar wheel (somacakra), at the seat (pīṭha) of Pūrṇagiri, whose essence is Uḍḍīśanātha, presiding over the state of deep sleep (suṣupti-daśā), consisting of the power of action (kriyā-śakti), and whose nature is the Brahman— salutation to the Goddess Śrī Bhagamālinī. In the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), to the fourth Vidyā, in the wheel of Brahmā (brahmacakra), at the seat (pīṭha) of Uḍḍiyāna, Śrī...

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who is the essence of the Supreme Brahman, the power (*śakti*) presiding over the state beyond the fourth (*turyātīta-daśā*), and the banner of the nature of the *caryā* [tradition]. Thus ends the *catuṣpīṭha-nyāsa*. Now follows the *prakaṭādi-nyāsa*:
at the *mūlādhāra*, [recite] (4) *ṃaṃ āṃḥ sauṃḥ* to those residing in the *trailokyamohana-cakra*, the *prakaṭa* [deities].

Salutation to the Yoginīs in the Svādhiṣṭhāna: *ṃaiṃ klīṃ sauṃḥ*, salutation to the most secret Yoginīs residing in the Sarvāśāpūraka-cakra. In the Anāhata: *ṃhaiṃ hakalīṃ hsauṃḥ*, salutation to the Saṃpradāya Yoginīs residing in the Sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka-cakra. In the Viśuddha...

(4) *ṃ hsaṃ hasakalīṃ hsauṃḥ*—salutation to the Kula-kaula Yoginīs residing in the Sarvārthasādhaka-cakra at the Ājñā [center]. (4) *ṃ hrīṃ klīṃ blīṃ*—salutation to the Nigarbha Yoginīs residing in the Sarvarakṣākara-cakra at the forehead (*lalāṭa*). (4) *ṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sauṃḥ*—[salutation] to those residing in the Sarvarogahara-cakra... at the forehead.

Salutation to the Hasyayoginīs on the head: 4) ṃ hsaḥ haṃ sa ka la rīṃ hsauṃḥ, salutation to the Parāpararahasyayoginīs residing in the wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradacakra*) in the *brahmarandhra*: 4) ṃ, salutation to the Parāparātirahasyayoginīs residing in the wheel consisting of universal bliss (*sarvānandamayacakra*), who are the fifteenth [verse] of the root [mantra].

Having placed *maḥ*, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) on all limbs with the mantra: "Obeisance to the sandals of the Śrīcakra Yoginīs of the manifest, the more secret, the most secret, the Kula, the Kaula, the Nigarbha, the Secret, the Higher-Secret, the Higher-Higher-Secret, and the Supreme-Supreme-Secret. Next is the placement of the Manifest and others (*prakaṭādi-nyāsa*). Now, the six...
The *saṃhāranyāsa* with the letters of the Daśārṇa mantra is as follows: On the two feet: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, first seed-syllable, *namaḥ*.

On the two shanks: second seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the two knees: third seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the waist: fourth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the penis: fifth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the back: sixth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the navel... [and so on].

(4) *Bhauṃ*, the seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the two sides; (4) *Ṃaṃ*, the eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the two breasts; (4) *Ṃnaṃ*, the ninth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the two shoulders; (4) *Ṃdaṃ*, the tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the two ears; (4) *Ṃeṃ*, the eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*);
(4) *Ṃvaṃ*, the twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* to the face; (4) *Ṃtraṃ*, the thirteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* [to the head].

The fourteenth seed-syllable, *ṃ*, with *namaḥ* at the vicinity of the two ear-cavities; the fifteenth seed-syllable, *ṃ*, with *namaḥ* at the two ear-lobes; the sixteenth seed-syllable, *ṃ*, with *namaḥ*. This is the Saṃhāra-nyāsa. Now, the Sṛṣṭi-nyāsa: the first seed-syllable, *ṃ*, with *namaḥ* at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); the second seed-syllable, *ṃ*, with *namaḥ* at the forehead.

The third seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two eyes; the fourth seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two ears; the fifth seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two nostrils; the sixth seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two cheeks; the seventh seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two teeth; the eighth seed-syllable, *namas*, on the two lips; the ninth seed-syllable, *namas*, on the tongue.

*Namaḥ* on the face—(4) the tenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the back—(4) the eleventh seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on all limbs—(4) the twelfth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the breasts—(4) the thirteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the heart—(4) the fourteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the belly—(4) the fifteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the *liṅga*—(4) the sixteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the... Sa.
One should place [the mantra] pervading the *mastavidyā*. This is the *sṛṣṭinyāsa*. Now, the *sthitinyāsa*:

on the two thumbs (4) the first seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the two index fingers (4) the second seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the two middle fingers (4) the third seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the two ring fingers (4) the fourth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*.
(4) *ṃ* the fifth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the *brahmarandhra*; (4) *ṃ* the sixth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the mouth;
(4) *ṃ* the seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the heart; (4) *ṃ* the eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, from the navel to the ends of the feet;
(4) *ṃ* the ninth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, from the throat to the navel; (4) *ṃ* the tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, from the *brahmarandhra* to the throat.

(4)ṃ the eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, to the two big toes; (4)ṃ the twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, to the two index fingers; (4)ṃ the thirteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, to the two middle fingers; (4)ṃ the fourteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, to the two ring fingers;
(4)ṃ the fifteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, to the two little fingers; (4)ṃ the sixteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*—thus [the sixteen].
The placement of the syllables according to their colors (*śīvarṇaiḥ sthitinyāsa*). Now, the fivefold syllable-placement (*pañcavidhavarṇanyāsa*) of the sixteen-syllable mantra:

[4] *ṃ* the first seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the head; [4] *ṃ* the second seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the mouth; [4] *ṃ* the third seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the right eye; [4] *ṃ* the fourth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the left [eye]; [4] *ṃ* the fifth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the right ear.
(4) *ṃ* the sixth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the left nostril; (4) *ṃ* the seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the right nostril;
(4) *ṃ* the eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the left [nostril]; (4) *ṃ* the ninth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the right cheek;
(4) *ṃ* the tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the left [cheek]; (4) *ṃ* the eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the back; (4) *ṃ* the twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the lower lip.

*Namaḥ* to the face, the thirteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* to the upper teeth, the fourteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* to the lower teeth, the fifteenth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* to the two mouths, the sixteenth seed-syllable—this is one method. *Namaḥ* to the head, the first seed-syllable; *namaḥ* to the hairline (*sīmanta*), the second seed-syllable.

*Namaḥ* on the forehead, the third seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the two eyebrows, the fourth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the nose, the fifth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* on the face, the sixth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* at the base of the right arm, the seventh seed-syllable; *namaḥ* at the joint of its middle, the eighth seed-syllable; *namaḥ* at its wrist, the ninth...

The seed-syllable *maṃ*, *namaḥ* at the base of that finger; (4) the tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at its tip; (4) the eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the base of the left arm; (4) the twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* in its middle; (4) the thirteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the wrist; (4) the fourteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; (4) the fifteenth...
The tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the beginning; (4) the sixteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*—this is the second method.

(2) On the head: (4) the first seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the forehead: (4) the second seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the right eye: (4) the third seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the left: (4) the fourth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*; on the mouth: (4) the fifth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*.

Maḥ, the sixth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the tip of the tongue; (4) ṃ, the seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the base of the right thigh; (4) ṇi, the eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the knee; (4) ṃ, the ninth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the ankle; (4) ṃ, the tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the base of the fingers; (4) ṃ, the eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ* at the tips of the fingers;
(4) ṃ, [the twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*] at the base of the left thigh. (4) ṃ, the second...

The tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the knees; (4) the thirteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the ankles; (4) the fourteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the bases of the toes; (4) the fifteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the tips of the toes; (4) the sixteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*—this is the third method. (3) The first seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the head; [the second] on the face...
On the forehead: (4) *Ṃ* second seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the right eye: (4) *Ṃ* third seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the left [eye]: (4) *Ṃ* fourth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*.

On the right ear: (4) *Ṃ* fifth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the left [ear]: (4) *Ṃ* sixth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the right nostril: (4) *Ṃ* seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the left [nostril]: (4) *Ṃ* eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*. On the right cheek: (4) *Ṃ* ninth seed-syllable...
(4) *ṃ* the tenth seed-syllable, obeisance to the left [eye]; (4) *ṃ* the eleventh seed-syllable, obeisance to the upper lip;
(4) *ṃ* the twelfth seed-syllable, obeisance to the lower lip; (4) *ṃ* the thirteenth seed-syllable, obeisance to the upper teeth;
(4) *ṃ* the fourteenth seed-syllable, obeisance to the lower [teeth]; (4) *ṃ* the fifteenth seed-syllable, obeisance to the head; (4) *ṃ* the sixteenth [seed-syllable], obeisance to the tongue.

The fourth method is as follows: (4) the first seed-syllable *namaḥ* on the forehead; (4) the second seed-syllable *namaḥ* on the throat; (4) the third seed-syllable *namaḥ* at the heart; (4) the fourth seed-syllable *namaḥ* at the navel;
(4) the fifth seed-syllable *namaḥ* at the *mūlādhāra*; (4) the sixth seed-syllable *namaḥ* at the *brahmarandhra*; (4) the [seventh] seed-syllable *namaḥ* on the mouth.
(4)ṃ Seventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, at the *mūlādhāra*. (4)ṃ Eighth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, again at the *mūlādhāra*.

(4)ṃ Ninth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, in the heart. (4)ṃ Tenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, in the *brahmarandhra*. (4)ṃ Eleventh seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the palm of the right hand. (4)ṃ Twelfth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the left [hand]. (4)ṃ Thirteenth seed-syllable...
(4) *Namaḥ* to the fourteenth seed-syllable on the right foot; (4) *Namaḥ* to the fifteenth seed-syllable on the left [foot];
(4) *Namaḥ* to the sixteenth seed-syllable in the heart. This is the fifth method. Now, the placement of the weapons (*āyudha-nyāsa*):
there, on one's own right hand, [place] (4) *Eṃ drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ klūṃ saḥ yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ sāṃ*.
To the yawns, the arrows of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, salutation; on the lower left hand: (4) *ṛṃ ṛṃ*, to the two enchanters, the bows of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, salutation; on the upper left hand:
(4) *āṃ hrīṃ*, to the two subduers, the nooses of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, salutation; on the right...

*Ṛdhvakare* (4) *ṃ kroṃ kroṃ staṃbhanābhyāṃ kāmeśvara-kāmeśvarī-aṅkuśābhyāṃ namaḥ*. This [mantra] should be performed with its corresponding mudrā; such is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the weapons. Now follows the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Kāmeśvarī and the others:
from the big toe of the left foot up to the navel, [one recites] (4) *ṃ aiṃ*, the first peak-syllable (*kūṭa*), followed by *kāmeśvaryai namaḥ*.

Having performed the placement on the left side— namely, from the navel to the throat *klīṃ*, the second peak-syllable (*kūṭa*), "salutation to Vajreśvarī," and from the throat to the head *sauṃḥ*, the third peak-syllable, "salutation to Bhagamālinī"—
one should then place [the syllables] from the big toe of the right foot to the navel: *hsraiṃ*, "salutation to Brahmā, the lord of the principle of the self (*ātmatattva*)."
From the navel up to the throat: *hsklrīṃ* to Viṣṇu, the Lord of the *Vidyā-tattva*, *namaḥ*.

From the throat up to the head: *hsrauṃ* to Śiva, the Lord of the *Śiva-tattva*, *namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) on the right side, this is the *Kāmeśvarī-nyāsa*. Now follows the *Tattva-tattva-nyāsa*: from the navel... [etc.]

(4) *ṃ* ending with the feet, the first *kūṭa*, to the Self of the Ātma-tattva, obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī; (4) *ṃ* from the throat to the navel, the second *kūṭa*, to the Self of the Vidya-tattva, obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī; (4) *ṃ* from the head to the throat, the third *kūṭa*, to the Self of the Śiva-tattva, to Śrī...

*Mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ* on all limbs. (4) *Āṃ Turīyavidyā-sarvatattvātmane Śrī-Mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ*. This is the Nyāsa of the four principles (*catustattva*). Now, the Nyāsa of the Root Mantra (*mūlavidyā*):
(4) *Āṃ* First Kūṭa, *namaḥ* at the Mūlādhāra; (4) *Īṃ* Second Kūṭa, *namaḥ* at the heart; [Third Kūṭa, *namaḥ*] between the eyebrows.

In the middle [of the forehead], one should place the third *kūṭa* with "namaḥ sarvāṅge" [and the seed-syllable] (4)ṃ; then, having placed the three *vidyās* as the fourth, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) of the entire *vidyā* as before. This is the placement of the Root *Vidyā* (*mūlāvidyā-nyāsa*). Now, the placement of the Nine Yonis (*navayoni-nyāsa*): On the left ear: (4)ṃ aiṃ namaḥ. On the right ear: (4)ṃ klīṃ namaḥ. On the chin: (4)ṃ sauṃḥ na...

(4) *Aiṃ* Namaḥ to the left temple; (4) *Klīṃ* Namaḥ to the right temple; (4) *Sauṃḥ* Namaḥ to the mouth; (4) *Aiṃ* Namaḥ to the left eye; (4) *Klīṃ* Namaḥ to the right eye; (4) *Sauṃḥ* Namaḥ to the nose; (4) *Aiṃ* Namaḥ to the left shoulder;
(4) *Klīṃ* Namaḥ to the right shoulder; (4) *Sauṃḥ* Namaḥ to the heart; (4) *Aiṃ* Namaḥ to the left elbow.
(4) *Namaḥ* to the right upper arm; (4) *ṃ klīṃ namaḥ* to the navel; (4) *ṃ sauṃḥ namaḥ* to the left knee;

(4) *ṃ aiṃ namaḥ* to the right knee; (4) *ṃ klīṃ namaḥ* to the *liṅga*; (4) *ṃ sauṃḥ namaḥ* to the left foot; (4) *ṃ aiṃ namaḥ* to the right foot; (4) *ṃ klīṃ namaḥ* to the secret place (*guhya*); (4) *ṃ sauṃḥ namaḥ* to the left side; (4) *ṃ aiṃ*.

*Namaḥ* to the right side; *(4) ̐klīṃ namaḥ* to the heart; *(4) ̐sauṃ namaḥ* to the left breast; *(4) ̐aiṃ namaḥ* to the right breast; *(4) ̐klīṃ namaḥ* to the throat; *(4) ̐sauṃ namaḥ*. This is the *navayoninyāsa*. Now follows the internal *navayoninyāsa*: from the *mūlādhāra* up to the six *cakras*, the forehead, and the *sīmanta*.
Having conceived nine *yonis* enclosed within squares at the nine locations, including the *brahmarandhra*,

one should perform the internal *navayoni-nyāsa* by mentally meditating upon and placing the three previously mentioned seed-syllables (*bījas*) in those [squares], starting from the front and proceeding in a clockwise direction. Now follows the *śṛṅkhalā-nyāsa*.

On the crest-lock (śikhā): (4) *ṃ* First Peak, *namaḥ*. On the chin (cibuka): (4) *ṃ* Second Peak, *namaḥ*. On the mouth (mukha): (4) *ṃ* Third Peak, *namaḥ*. (1) On the mouth: (4) *ṃ* First Peak, *namaḥ*. On the throat (kaṇṭha): (4) *ṃ* Second Peak, *namaḥ*. On the chin: (4) *ṃ* Third Peak, *namaḥ*. (2) On the chin: (4) *ṃ* First Peak, *namaḥ*. On the heart (hṛdaya): (4) *ṃ* Second [Peak, *namaḥ*].

(4) *Ūṃ* Third Peak, salutation to the throat; (3) *Ūṃ* Third Peak, salutation to the throat; (4) *Ūṃ* First Peak, salutation to the navel; (4) *Ūṃ* Second Peak, salutation to the heart; (4) *Ūṃ* Third Peak, salutation to the heart; (4) *Ūṃ* First Peak, salutation to the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; (4) *Ūṃ* Second Peak, salutation to the navel; (4) *Ūṃ* Third [Peak].

Kūṭaṃ namaḥ (5) at the navel; (4) ṃ prathamakūṭaṃ namaḥ at the mūlādhāra; (4) ṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ at the svādhiṣṭhāna; (4) ṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ (6) at the svādhiṣṭhāna; (4) ṃ prathamakūṭaṃ namaḥ at the thighs; (4) ṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ at the mūlādhāra; (4) ṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ (7).
At the *mūlādhāra*: (4) *ṃ prathamakūṭaṃ namaḥ*; at the knees: (4) *ṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ*;

at the thighs: (4) *ṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ*. At the thighs: (4) *ṃ prathamakūṭaṃ namaḥ*; at the feet: (4) *ṃ dvitīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ*; at the knees: (4) *ṃ tṛtīyakūṭaṃ namaḥ*. This is the *śṛṅkhalā-nyāsa* (chain placement).
Now, the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the hermitage: on the head, *oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*; on the forehead, *hrīṃ pārvatyai namaḥ*;
in the right eye, *aṃ savitre namaḥ*; in the left [eye], *maṃ agnaye namaḥ*; around the mouth, *ṭhaṃ candramase namaḥ*; on the tongue, *śrīṃ śriyai namaḥ*; on the right cheek, *svāṃ dantine*.

"Obeisance to Vāma; obeisance to Hāṃ Dantin"—thus is the *amaṭha*-nyāsa. Having performed the nyāsas in this manner, one should place the sixteen-syllable Śrī-mantra, encapsulated by the *praṇava* (Oṃ), as a pervasive covering over the entire body.
Then, one should again place that same sixteen-syllable Śrī-mantra, likewise encapsulated by the *praṇava*, upon the heart. Now...

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) beginning with the *ṛṣi*, and contemplating "I am Śiva," one should bind the nine mudrās beginning with Saṃkṣobhiṇī and the four mudrās beginning with Pāśa as they are about to be described; then, meditating upon one's own self as the form of Kāmakalā through its presence in all limbs, [one performs] the Śaktyutthāpana mudrā.
Having performed the *vṛddhi* [of mantras] and having raised the Kuṇḍalinī from the Mūlādhāra according to the method described in the *Prātaḥsmaraṇa*,
and having likewise performed the worship of the six *cakras*, one should contemplate the Śrī Paradevatā, who is the transformation of those splendors,
seated upon the lion-throne within the heart-lotus, resting on the lap of Kāmeśvara in the King of Mandalas (*Śrīcakra*), adorned with all ornaments.

With hands sealed in the *trikhaṇḍa-mudrā*, one should meditate as follows: "Oṃ! [I am] my own self, exceedingly serene, joined with youthful radiance, mature, and possessing an internal luster through the form of non-difference from That.
Oṃ! In the midst of the ocean of red nectar overflowing at the rising of the moon, there is a golden ground."
In the center of that [city], one should remember the great Nandana garden,
which intoxicates even the God of Love and is resplendent with the mass of moonlight from the ever-risen full moon;
it is brilliant with the flowers of all seasons, including kadamba, mango, punnāga, nāgakeśara, campaka, bakula, and pārijāta trees.
It was frequented by bees resonant with the sound of "hum," by cuckoos, parrots, and various other multicolored flocks of birds;
it was surrounded by peacocks, ducks, swans, and many other species of winged creatures,
and adorned with clusters of trees strewn with various flowering creepers and ponds blooming along its banks.

Having meditated upon the Nandana garden as grey with the pollen produced from the *lolpa* flowers and perfectly served by the Malaya breezes, one should then contemplate its courtyard. Having thus reflected on the courtyard, which is adorned with grounds resembling pure gold and frequented by gods and Siddhas, one should visualize a pavilion in its center.

One should meditate upon the sphere of the Brahmāṇḍa-pavilion, which pervades the entire universe, resembling a thousand suns, four-cornered and most beautiful; its quarters made tawny by masses of radiance from the luster of jewels, free of pillars in the center yet provided with pillars at the corners, and adorned with great rubies, lapis lazuli, gems, and gold.

Richly adorned with canopies of pearl necklaces, beautified by stairways of jewels, fanned by gentle breezes, rippled by fragrant incense, and graced by celestial palanquins such as jeweled chowries and bells;
[it was further embellished] with jasmine, campaka, punnāga, ketakī, mallikā, and other flowers, as well as red lotuses and white water-lilies.
Adorned with *dhava* flowers and beautiful blossoms, and decorated with variegated garlands, it is embellished by the pure splendor of all seasons.

Adorned with millions of jeweled figures shimmering upwards and across, and fashioned by Viśvakarman from various divine jewels, one should meditate upon a vast altar (*vedikā*) measuring a hundred *yojanas* in its center.
Resembling ten thousand suns, adorned with ten million rubies, provided with four gates, featuring ruby door-arches,
decorated on all sides with lamps and full water-jars,
embellished with golden banners bearing sprouts, and [furnished] with divine [images] seated upon jeweled pedestals.
It was adorned with golden pillars at intervals, crowded with rising jewel-mirrors,

and amplified by the sweet and sublime hymns of various Gandharvas; it was filled with throngs of celestial nymphs, endowed with the sentiment of love (*śṛṅgāra-rasa*), graced with fresh youth, adorned with ornaments of various jewels, and engaged in playing the lute, flute, drum, and other instruments.

One should always meditate upon the auspicious jeweled lion-throne situated in the center of the altar, surrounded on all sides by those who delight the Great Goddess with dances; [one should meditate] upon that throne as Sadāśiva himself, consisting of the four feet of Brahmā, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Īśa, which is essentially Paraśiva, and thereupon the sovereignty of the flower-couch.

One should meditate upon her, seated in the Śrīcakra, situated in the center of the *yoni* within the venerable Uḍḍiyāna-pīṭha, graced by the *svastika* posture while reclining in the *paryaṅka-bandha*, resting on the lap of Paraśiva, with a form blazing in the center of a lotus. Thereafter, I shall describe the meditation that is to be practiced by the gods, beginning from the lotus.
I salute Goddess Bhāṃ, who is as red as the rays of the rising sun, resembling the *japā* flower, comparable to the *dāḍima* blossom,
radiant like a ruby, and similar to saffron-water;
she is adorned with a shimmering crown-gem and a network of tiny bells, and her sprout-like, curling locks of hair resemble a swarm of black bees.
The Supreme Goddess, whose lotus-face is like the orb of the newly risen sun, whose soft forehead-ribbon is slightly curved like the crescent moon,
whose creeper-like eyebrows have the form of the Pināka bow,
whose eyes roll with playful movement as she rejoices in bliss, and whose golden earrings shine with clusters of flickering rays.
Her full cheeks surpass the orb of the moon; her nose is perfectly defined as if by the measuring line of Viśvakarman and other celestial architects;

her lips are red like coral and the bimba fruit, resembling nectar; she is adorned with a row of teeth shining like pomegranate seeds and diamonds; her tongue flickers like a jewel upon an island of gems; and she speaks pure words with a gentle smile.

The Great Queen, whose neck was graced by a chin endowed with incomparable qualities that surpassed the ocean of the essence of sweetness; who was adorned with arms as graceful as lotus stalks, beautified by the weight of jeweled bracelets and armlets;
and whose delicate lotus-hands resembled the petals of a red lotus.
Her surface of the sky was illuminated by the light from the nails of her lotus-like hands; she possessed uplifted breasts adorned with strings of pearl necklaces;

she was beautifully graced by a waist marked with the curvature of the three folds; she was embellished by a navel shaped like the eddy of a river of loveliness; and her hips were endowed with a girdle fashioned from priceless gems.
Her hips were like the frontal globes of an elephant, and the line of hair upon them was like a sprout; she was as delicate as the graceful trunk of a plantain tree, O Queen.
Her knees were beautiful, curved, and like blossoms of loveliness, and she was adorned with a pair of shanks resembling the stalks of that very beauty.
With her two feet, their ankles hidden and toes well-formed, she surpassed even the tortoise, and her body was slender.

Her fingers were long and graced with moon-like shining nails; her lotus feet were rubbed by the crest-jewels upon the heads of Brahmā and Viṣṇu; she laughed with a continuous stream of splendor resembling a hundred moons; her feet possessed the crimson hue of sindūra, the japā flower, and the pomegranate, surpassing even the redness of the Lauhitya river; she was clothed in red garments, and her hands were raised, holding a noose and a goad.
Seated upon a red lotus, adorned with red ornaments, four-armed and three-eyed, holding five arrows and a bow,
her mouth filled with betel-leaf mixed with camphor fragments,
her body crimson with the intense fragrance of musk and saffron, richly arrayed in all erotic finery, and decorated with every ornament.

One should thus meditate upon the Great Goddess Mahātripurasundarī— the mother who generates joy for the world, who brings delight to the world, who effects the attraction of the world, whose form is the cause of the world; the Goddess who consists of all mantras, who is beautiful with all auspiciousness, who embodies all Lakṣmī, who is eternal, and who is beautiful with supreme bliss.

Having meditated on the cave as one with oneself and offered a handful of flowers upon one's own head with the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*), one should again meditate upon the Goddess in her aforementioned form, together with Her limbs (*aṅga*) and retinues (*āvaraṇa*), within the lotus of the heart. Then,

preceded by the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) and so forth in the manner to be described, one should worship Her, along with Her limbs and retinues, through mental offerings (*mānasa-upacāra*).

Having offered the *naivedya*, at the conclusion of the meal, one should perform the *vaiśvadeva* rite. Therein, one should visualize within the *mūlādhāra* a square sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) consisting of the nature of the *ātman*, *antarātman*, *jñānātman*, and *paramātman*, blazing with the fire of the *kuṇḍalinī* and provided with the girdle of bliss (*ānanda-mekhalā*). In its center, within the fire of consciousness, bliss, and knowledge (*cid-ānanda-jñānāgni*), [one should offer the oblation].

One should offer oblations as follows: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mūlam ahaṃtāṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice egoism, svāhā); *mūlam asatyaṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice untruth, svāhā); *mūlam paiśunyaṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice backbiting, svāhā); *mūlam kāmaṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice desire, svāhā); *mūlam krodhaṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice anger, svāhā); *mūlam lobhaṃ juhomi svāhā* (I sacrifice greed, svāhā). *Mūlam...* [and so forth].

"I offer delusion, svāhā! I offer the root of pride, svāhā! I offer the root of envy, svāhā! Having thus offered, one should give three full oblations (*pūrṇāhuti*) as follows: with the root mantra, in the root-fire, using the navel-consciousness as the sacrificial offering, the mind as the ladle, and kindled by the lamp of knowledge, one should constantly offer the functions of the senses.

"I offer myself, svāhā!"—with this, one should offer the first oblation. (1) "Oblation! O radiant fire of Dharma and Adharma, with the ladle of the mind, I constantly offer my sensory functions into the fire of the Self through the path of the *suṣumṇā*; svāhā!"—with this, one should offer the second oblation. (2) Root-mantra: *prakā...*

"Supporting with the hands of space and consciousness the sacrificial ladle of *unmanī*, filled with the oil of the portions of merit and demerit, I offer it into the fire—*svāhā*. With this, one should give the third oblation. "In the internal, continuous, and fuel-less fire, which blazes forth as the adversary of the darkness of *māyā*, within the kindled consciousness..."

"Obeisance, Svāhā! I offer the universe, beginning with the earth and ending in auspiciousness, as if into the ground of the expansion of wondrous rays. Having thus offered three full oblations (*pūrṇāhuti*), while meditating upon one's own self as a mass of consciousness and bliss, [one recites]:
"I am full; I am non-dual; I am Śiva; I am the practitioner; I am the Supreme Brahman."

With a mind intent on the desire for reintegration (*nusaṃdhāna*), possessing mature and surging joy, and having shaken off all impurities; with a body of consciousness that has become the three cities (*tripurībhūta*) filled with the essence of consciousness-bliss;
and with a mind engaged in the closing of the white and red lotuses of the Guru, there arises the desire to sever the *prāṇa* and *apāna* breaths.
Having thus contemplated the true nature of the practitioner, who is the progenitor of the entire fulfilled universe, one should begin the worship.

Then, having meditated upon the Goddess within the lotus of the heart and having propitiated her with all the services beginning with the *uttarāpośāna*, one should recite the root mantra according to one's capacity. Having offered the recitation through breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and other means, [one should offer it to] Śrī...

Having prostrated before the Guru and adorned one's own body with perfumes and other substances—namely saffron (*kuṅkuma*), agallochum (*aguru*), musk (*kastūrī*), camphor (*karpūra*), and sandalwood (*candana*)—one should then decorate the maṇḍala for the Lord of Devas with these fragrances. One should perform the installation of the water-jar (*kalaśa*); there, on one's left side, within a six-cornered figure, is a triangle.

Having fashioned a square with two circles and two external perimeters, and having constructed on the ground a triangle, a circle, and a mandala in one's own right, [one should worship] with "Aiṃ Kei Hrīṃ Namaḥ" in the southeast (Agni), "Klīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Namaḥ" in the south,
"Sauṃḥ Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Namaḥ" in the left (north), "Hrīṃ" in the northwest (Vāyu), and "Namaḥ to the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti)" in the center. I.

Having worshipped there, [one should recite]: *śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauṃḥ hṛdayāya namaḥ*; *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śirase svāhā*; *ke ī la hrīṃ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ*; *ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ kavacāya huṃ*; *sa ka la hrīṃ netratrayāya vaṣaṭ*; *sauṃḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*. Thus.
Having worshipped the six-cornered [diagram] with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should place the support (*ādhāra*) thereon. Upon that, having established a vessel such as a conch,

which has been purified with the mantra "Astrāya Phaṭ" and filled with water using the mantra "Namaḥ," one should offer the general *arghya* consisting of sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, barley, tips of *kuśa* grass, sesame seeds, mustard seeds, and *dūrvā* grass.

Regarding the substances for the vessel: having invoked the sacred ford (*tīrtha*) there with the mantra *oṃ gaṅge ca yamune ca* using the goad-mudrā (*aṅkuśamudrā*), one should place perfumes, unbroken rice, flowers, and so forth into the general offering vessel (*sāmānyārghyapātra*) while reciting the *praṇava*.
Having worshipped [the water] with the digits (*kalā*) of Fire, Sun, and Moon, and having displayed the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*), [one worships] the self eight times...

The meaning is "with the *kṣara-mantra*," namely: *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ so 'haṃ svāhā*. One should worship with one's own mantra as well. Having sprinkled the maṇḍala made on one's left with the water of the general *arghya* prepared according to the prescribed rule, [one should offer] "Salutation to Ādhāra-śakti" there, and in the center, upon that, "to Kālāgni-rudra."
Salutations to Maṇḍūka; salutations to Kūrma; salutations to Ananta; salutations to Mūlaprakṛti; salutations to Pṛthivī; salutations to the Ocean of Nectar; salutations to the Ocean of Nectar;
salutations to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice; salutations to the Ocean of Wine; salutations to the Ocean of Milk.

Salutation to the Ocean of Curd; salutation to the Ocean of Clarified Butter; salutation to the Ocean of Salt Water; salutation to the Isle of Jewels; salutation to the Abode of the Wish-Fulfilling Gem; salutation to the Jewel Altar-platform adorned with nine sections; salutation to the Seat of the Wish-Fulfilling Gem; salutation to the Jewel Lion-throne.
Homage to the thousand-petaled lotus; homage to the ruby gem; homage to the golden mountain; homage to the Nandana grove; homage to the various multitudes of jewels;
homage to the various deities; homage to Dharma; homage to Jñāna; homage to Vairāgya; homage to Aiśvarya.

Salutations to Sovereignty; salutations to Unrighteousness; salutations to Ignorance; salutations to Lack of Dispassion; salutations to Lack of Sovereignty; salutations to Śeṣa; salutations to Padmā; salutations to the petals consisting of Prakṛti;
salutations to the filaments consisting of the transformations (vikāra); salutations to the fifty seed-syllables.
Obeisance to the white pericarp; obeisance to the solar orb; obeisance to the lunar orb; obeisance to the fire orb;
obeisance to the aggregate of beings (*saṃsattva*); obeisance to *raṃ* as passion (*rajas*); obeisance to *taṃ* as darkness (*tamas*);
obeisance to *taṃ* as darkness (*tamas*); obeisance to *āṃ* as the Self (*ātman*); obeisance to *aṃ* as the inner Self (*antarātman*).

Salutation to the Supreme Self (Paramātman). Salutation to the Self of Knowledge (Jñānātman). Salutation to Vāmā. Salutation to Jyeṣṭhā. Salutation to Raudrī. Salutation to Ambikā. Salutation to Icchā. Salutation to Jñānā.
Salutation to Kriyā. Salutation to Kuvjikā. Salutation to Citrā. Salutation to Viṣaghnikā.

*Maḥ* obeisance to the Messenger; *namaḥ* obeisance to Ānandā; *namaḥ* obeisance to Manonmanī; *aiṃ* obeisance to Parā; *aiṃ* obeisance to Aparā; *aiṃ* obeisance to Virūpā; *hsauṃḥ* obeisance to Sadāśiva, the Great Corpse, whose seat is the lotus. Having thus worshipped the mandala and rinsed [the vessel] with "namas," one should place the support (*ādhāra*) there.

*Pya oṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ yaṃ*: May the vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) of the ten digits (*kalāḥ*) beginning with Dhūmra and bestowing righteousness (*dharmapradāḥ*) be established here; may the life-force (*jīvaḥ*) be established here; may all the sense-faculties (*sarvendriyāṇi*) be established here; may speech, mind, hearing, and breath (*vāṅ-manas-śrotra-prāṇāḥ*), having come here, remain happily—*svāhā*. Thus, one should establish the vital breaths with the *lelihāna-mudrā*.

One should perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) with: "O you who bestow the qualities of fire, beginning with smoke-colored [flames], come here! (2) Be present! (2) Remain near! (2) Establish yourselves! (2) Accept the worship! Having thus performed the invocation, one should worship with: *oṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ raṃ vahnimaṇḍalāya dharmaprada-daśakalātmane aiṃ*.

Salutation to Kalaśādhārā; salutation to Dhūmrā (Yaṃ); salutation to Nīlavarṇā (Raṃ); salutation to Kapilā (Laṃ); salutation to Visphuliṅginī (Vaṃ); salutation to Jvālā (Śaṃ); salutation to Haimavatī (Ṣaṃ);
salutation to Kavyavāhinī (Saṃ); salutation to Havivāhinī (Haṃ); salutation to Raudrī (Laṃ).

Having worshipped with "Oṃ Kṣaṃ Saṃkarṣiṇyai Namaḥ," and having rinsed the pitcher with "Phaṭ," the practitioner, regarding it as the Goddess herself, should with devotion place it there— filled to its source (the base) with the mantra "Hsauṃḥ Shauṃḥ Namaḥ"— and adorned with a red cloth and red garlands.

Then one should gaze upon that vessel and consecrate it with the root mantra: "O Goddess, just as by Śambhu, just as by Viṣṇu in the past, and just as by Brahmā in former times, so do I establish you.
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, I establish the pitcher of the Great Goddess Tripurā; obeisance. Thus [he should say].

Standing [there], [one recites]: *Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haṃ ma la va ra yūṃ, obeisance to the solar disc (*arka-maṇḍala*), which consists of twelve parts (*kalā*) and bestows the eightfold wealth (*vasu-prada*).* *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ aṃ.
May the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) of the twelve solar parts that bestow the eightfold wealth enter here; may the life-force (*jīva*) remain here; may all the sense organs (*indriya*) remain here.*
"May those [energies] of speech, mind, hearing, and smell come here and remain for a long time in happiness, svāhā.

Having thus established the vital breaths (*prāṇas*) with the *lelihāna-mudrā*, one should invoke: "O twelve digits beginning with *Vasu*, *Prada*, and *Tapinī*, come here! Remain! Be present! Face me! (4) *ṃvasu-prada-tapiny-ādyā dvādaśakalā ihāgacchata saṃtiṣṭhata sannidadhata saṃmukhībhavata*.

Saying "Be present," one should invoke and worship [the deity]. Having worshipped with "Oṃ *klīṃ* obeisance to the special arghya vessel" (*klīṃ viśeṣārghyapātrāya namaḥ*), one should worship the twelve kalās as follows:
*kaṃ bhaṃ obeisance to Tapinī*, *khaṃ vaṃ obeisance to Tāpinī*, *gaṃ phaṃ obeisance to Bodhinī*, *ghaṃ paṃ obeisance to Rodhinī*, *ṅaṃ naṃ obeisance to Kālinī*.
*Caṃ* to the one who dries up the moon, *namaḥ*; *chaṃ* to the most excellent one, *namaḥ*; *jaṃ* to the attractor, *namaḥ*;

*jhaṃ* to the illusory power (*māyā*), *namaḥ*; *ñaṃ* to the one possessing all things, *namaḥ*; *ṭaṃ* to the one with golden luster, *namaḥ*; *ḍhaṃ* to the earth (*kṣamā*), *namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped the pitcher, [one recites]: *kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ maṃ*.

Reciting "bhaṃ vaṃ phaṃ paṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ chaṃ caṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ aṃḥ aṃ auṃ oṃ aiṃ eṃ ḹṃ ḷṃ ṛṃ ṛṃ ūṃ uṃ īṃ iṃ āṃ aṃ," one should fill that flask with water by means of the *nyāsa* (ritual placement).
Then, having visualized that nectar as being in the form of the moon, [one recites]: "Oṃ sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ sa-mala-va-ra-yūṃ, from the lunar maṇḍala..."
"Obeisance to the one whose nature consists of the sixteen digits that grant all desires"—having thus worshipped, [one should recite]: "Māṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ!
O life-breaths of the sixteen digits of the nectar-bestowing moon beginning with Kāmapradā, your life-breaths are here;
your life is established here; all your senses are established here—speech, mind, hearing, touch, smell, and breath."
Having offered the vital breaths (*prāṇas*) with the *lelihāna-mudrā* while reciting, "Come here and remain happily, svāhā," one should perform the invocation:
"O Amṛtā and the other sixteen digits (*kalās*), who grant all desires, come here! Remain here! Be present! Be well-disposed! Having thus performed the invocation, one should worship.
One should worship the sixteen digits (*kalās*) as follows: *Aṃ* obeisance to Amṛtā; *Āṃ* obeisance to Mānadā;
*Iṃ* obeisance to Tuṣṭi; *Īṃ* obeisance to Puṣṭi; *Uṃ* obeisance to Prīti; *Ūṃ* obeisance to Rati;
*Ṛṃ* obeisance to Śrī; *Ṝṃ* obeisance to Hī; *Ḷṃ* obeisance to Svadhā; *Ḹṃ* obeisance to Rātri; *Aiṃ* obeisance to Jyotsnā.
*Namaḥ aiṃ haimavatyai namaḥ; oṃ chāyāyai namaḥ; oṃ pūrṇimāyai namaḥ; aṃ nityāyai namaḥ;

aṃḥ amāvāsyāyai namaḥ.* Having worshipped these digits (*kalā*) with the ritual substance, one should protect it with *phaṭ*, veil it with *huṃ*, gaze upon it with the root mantra (*mūla*), sprinkle it with water while saying *namaḥ*, and [finally] with the root mantra.

Having smelled the fragrance of cardamom, cloves, musk, sandalwood, uśīra, and flowers, and having placed them into a jar, O Goddess, one should release the fifth initiation. Having adorned that jar with red garments, garlands, and so forth, [one should recite] the root mantra: *hasakhaphreṃ pathikadevatābhyo huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Ha*.

Sakhaphreṃ āsphālinī grāmacāṇḍālinī huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Hasakhaphreṃ kro dhacāṇḍālinī huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Hasakhaphreṃ dṛṣṭicāṇḍālinī huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Hasakhaphreṃ sṛṣṭicāṇḍālinī huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Hasakhaphreṃ ghaṭacāṇḍālinī huṃ phaṭ svāhā!

HASAKHAPHREṂ TAPANA-VEDHACĀṆḌĀLINĪ HŪṂ (0) HASAKHAPHREṂ NIRDAIVACĀṆḌĀLINĪ HŪṂ (0) HASAKHAPHREṂ TANADṚṢṬISPARŚADOṢACĀṆḌĀLINĪ HŪṂ (0) HASAKHAPHREṂ PAŚUPĀŚACĀṆḌĀLINĪ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ. Thus [is the mantra for] the nectar of the jar, with perfumes and unbroken rice grains.

Having worshipped with flowers there, while reciting the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) over the water-pot (*kalaśa*), one should meditate upon the Supreme Goddess (*parā*) within the circle of the drop (*bindu*) in the center of the triangle—marked with *aṃ āṃ* and so forth, and *haṃ laṃ kṣaṃḥ*—and worship the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
Then: *Oṃ hrīṃ, O Supreme Mistress (*parasvāminī*), who flows through the void of the supreme ether (*paramākāśaśūnya*), O Moon-like One...*
Having held the jar while reciting "rkāgnibhakṣiṇipātreviśaviśasvāhā," one should recite [the mantra] ten times.

Then, one should recite three times: "aṃ āṃ" and so on, up to "kṣaṃ; obeisance to the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogins; may *svadhā* and *svāhā* always be present here. Thus one should recite.
"Moving with black dust, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the god Savitṛ goes on his golden chariot, beholding all beings"—one should also recite this ṛc ten times.
"The winds blow sweet for the one who follows the Truth; the rivers flow with sweetness; may they be sweet for us."

May the plants be sweet at night and also at dawn; may the earthly realm be sweet; may the sky, our father, be sweet; may the tree be full of sweetness; may the sun be full of sweetness; may the cows be sweet for us. *Oṃ Madhu*. Thus one should recite ten times. *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ānandeśvara*.

Having recited the Gāyatrī mantra ten times— *rāyavidmahe śrīsurādevyaidhīmahi tannordhanārīśvaraḥ pracodayāt*— [one recites]: *haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasat hotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat | nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||*
One should recite "gojā ṛtajādrijā ṛtam" three times. (3) One should also recite "agnim īḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devam ṛtvijaṃ hotāraṃ ratnadhātamaṃ" three times.
(3) Vāṃ vīṃ vūṃ vaiṃ vauṃ vaṃḥ, salutation to the Goddess Surā, who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā.

Having thus recited ten times: *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ saiṃ sauṃ saṃḥ śukra-śāpaṃ mocaya surā-devyai namaḥ*, one should worship the jar three times with the mantra: *iṣetvorjetvā vāyava stha pāyava stha devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatu śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇe*. Thus [the verse].
One should recite this once: (1) *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ sure kṛṣṇa śāpaṃ mocaya* (2) *amṛtaṃ srāvaya* (2) *svāhā*. This should be muttered three times.
(3) *ā yāhi vītaye gṛhṇāno havyadātaye | ni hotā satsi barhiṣe ||*

One should recite [the mantra] ten times (10). One should recite the vidyā that removes the curse of Śukra as follows: oṃ sūryamaṇḍalasaṃbhūte varuṇālayasaṃbhave | amāvījamaye devi śukraśāpād vimucyatām || vedānāṃ praṇavo bījaṃ brahmānandamayo yadi | tena satyena...

May the Lord of Gods dispel the sin of Brahman-slaughter: *Oṃ juṃ saḥ*. The one supreme Brahman alone consists of both the gross and the subtle; by that [Brahman], I destroy the Brahman-slaughter born of my hair. Released from the curse of Brahmā, released from the curse of Viṣṇu, may you be liberated from the curse of Rudra.

Having recited "napavitrābhavasāṃpratam" three times, one should mutter ten times: "śannodevīrabhiṣṭaye āpobhavantu pītaye śaṃyyorabhisravantunaḥ. Then [one should recite]: "hrīṃ śrīṃ chāṃ chīṃ chūṃ chaiṃ chauṃ chaḥ churikākāriṇi śobhiṇi vikārān..."
"May there be the destruction of the enemy's substance, svāhā!"—having thus recited ten times over the water-pot (10), [one recites]:
"He who is all-seeing and whose face is on every side, whose hands are on every side and whose arms are on every side;
he, generating heaven and earth, embraces them with his arms and his wings."

One should recite "Veka" ten times. Then, having meditated upon the Guru on the thousand-spoked [lotus], and having bowed to one's chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) in the heart-lotus, [one should contemplate] the Śrī Guru Daśikānanda,

who has filled the entire maṇḍala, who is exultant with bliss, who is filled by all [the gods] beginning with Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and who [bears] the gesture of knowledge (*jñānamudrā*) and the gesture of fearlessness (*abhayamudrā*).
One should worship the Lord of Gurus (Gurudeva), who holds excellent books with his arms, who embodies all deities, and who is the immutable causal self, by means of the *pādukā* sequences. Then,
one should meditate upon the Supreme Deity in the midst of the Goddess’s substances— she who is red, whose nature is causal bliss, and who abides in the state beyond the mind (*unmanas*).

The wise practitioner should perform meditation upon her who resides within the divine Śiva Kāmeśāna, whose body is the glorious identity with one’s own self (*śrīsvātmaikya*), whose form is the void of Great Joy (*mahāmudita*), and who holds a noose, a goad, a bow, and arrows in the midst of her [four] hands. Having meditated upon the glorious Tiraskariṇī, he should recite: *Oṃ nīlatoyadasaṃkāśāṃ*.
The Goddess, adorned with dark-blue locks of hair, wearing blue garments, with eyes like blue lotuses, enriched with ornaments of blue flowers, decorated with blue jewelry, covered in blue unguents,
wearing a necklace of blue lapis lazuli, and possessing highly precious gem-ornaments set with sapphires.

Mounted upon a blue horse, armed with a blue sword, that supreme Mahāmāyā deludes the fourteen worlds with her blue veil of sleep; she devours those who revile the sacrificial substances and protects on all sides the heroes devoted to the drinking of *vīrapāna*, as she pervades the divine circle of the secret convention (*saṃketamaṇḍala*).

"I bow to the Supreme Goddess, the Mother of Supreme Bliss, the Paramānandabhairavī, whose body is supreme bliss, who bestows [grace] with a beautiful garment. Having thus meditated upon the *tiraskariṇī* (the veil), one should mutter the mantra:
*aiṃ klīṃ glauṃ hrīṃ śrī tiraskariṇi sakalapaśujanavāk-stambhini*.
"Overcome the eyes, ears, tongues, noses, and other [senses] of the entire multitude of deluded people!
*ṭhaḥ* (3) *svāhā*. Having recited this mantra ten times, his ancestors approach that supreme Brahman, the supreme state, the pure light free from disease—the purifying [Vedic hymn].

"To him who approaches the *sāmidhenī* verses, whose essence has been gathered by the seers—for him Sarasvatī pours forth milk, clarified butter, honey, and water. The *pāvamāna* is the supreme Brahman; the *pāvamāna* is the supreme essence;
the *pāvamāna* is the supreme knowledge. With that, I purify you. Having recited this three times, [one should worship] Śrī...

Having meditated upon the Guru and reciting "Vaṃ," and reciting the solar mantra "Haṃsaḥ," one should pour nectar from the tip of the left nostril into the vessel by means of the Kuṇḍalinī practice. Then, having rendered it immortal with the Amṛta-mudrā, [one should recite]:
"Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, O Amṛta, born of nectar, showerer of nectar, amṛ..."

Having recited "Taṃstrāvaya (2) aṃ āṃ amṛteśvaryai namaḥ" three times (3), and having meditated upon the nectar-filled jar, having prepared it with camphor, cardamom, cloves, musk, sandalwood, and vetiver, one should invoke the sacred waters (*tīrthas*) with the *mūlamantra* and the verse "Gaṅge ca... (0) using the *aṅkuśamudrā*. [Then] all the [sacred waters...]

One should meditate upon that divine [liṅga] consisting of the *artha* (essence). Then, in the midst of the substance, one should visualize a triangle joined with a *bindu* as before, and having formed the *yonimudrā*, one should meditate upon Ānandabhairava and the Goddess Surā within the *bindu*, as follows:
"Oṃ, resembling ten million suns and as cool as ten million moons, possessing eighteen arms..."

One should meditate upon the Lord who has five faces and three eyes, situated in the midst of an ocean of nectar, seated upon a Brahma-lotus, mounted on a bull, blue-throated, and adorned with all ornaments; holding a skull-cup and a *khaṭvāṅga*,
sounding a bell and a *ḍamaru* drum, bearing a noose and a goad, and wielding a mace, a shield, a sword, and a *kheṭaka*.

The best of practitioners should meditate upon the Lord of the Gods, who is red in color and holds in his hands a silken cloth, a mallet, a trident, a spear, a variegated shield, a skull, a loincloth, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. Having offered a handful of flowers into the pitcher, he should recite the mantra of Ānandabhairava. Having thus meditated and offered a handful of flowers into the pitcher, [he should worship] Ānanda...

One should recite the Bhairava mantra ten times: *ha sa ra kṣa ma la va yūṃ ānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ*. Having thus recited it ten times (10), one should meditate upon the Goddess Surā seated on the lap of Ānandabhairava, as follows: *Oṃ, while the ocean was being churned, in the milk-ocean, the best of seas...*
One should meditate upon the goddess Surā, who has arisen in the form of a maiden,

possessing the radiance of ten million times ten thousand moons, white as snow, kunda flowers, and the moon; she has five faces, three eyes, and is endowed with eighteen arms, intent on bestowing all bliss, smiling, and large-eyed, O Lord.
Having offered a handful of flowers facing the deity, one should recite the mantra of Ānandabhairavī over the jar. Having thus meditated upon her with the mantra:
*sahakṣamalavarayūṃ surādevyai vauṣaṭ*, and having recited it ten times, one should display the Mahāmudrā, Yonimudrā, Dhenumudrā, and Matsyamudrā. Then, [the Lelihānā...]*

Having bound the *khyāṃ-mudrā*, the *kuṇḍalinī* rises again from the *mūlādhāra*, ascends by way of the *suṣumṇā* to the end of the twelve (*dvādaśānta*), and while recollecting "I am He" (*so'haṃ haṃsaḥ*),
unites with Śiva; becoming filled with supreme bliss, one [receives] through the mind the rain of nectar arising therefrom.

Meditating on the *praṇava* with the *sāpuṭa* [method], one should apply it to the substance of another and meditate upon the *kalaśa* as being directly filled with nectar. Then, having uttered the seed-syllable of Varuṇa,
*vaṃ*, and having recited the root mantra ten times while uttering it, [one should perform the rite] preceded by the ringing of a bell and various kinds of flowers.

Having worshipped the jar with garlands, ornaments, incense, lamps, medicinal herbs, prostrations, and hymns, one should meditate upon it as containing all the gods. Thus, having drawn the wheel of powers (*śakticakra*) within the jar, and having written *haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ* in its center, one should hold the jar eight times while reciting the root mantra (*mūlamantra*) *vaṃ*, and then recite the ritual for the installation of the jar (*ghaṭasthāpanavidhi*).

One should offer this special *arghya* (offering water) and place it according to one's own purpose; having set aside the twelfth [portion] for oneself, one should set aside the twelfth for the Deity. One should place the special *arghya* situated in the middle of twelve finger-breadths before Śivā. Thus ends the worship of the jar (*ghaṭapūjā*). Now follows the worship of the venerable vessel (*śrīpātrapūjā*): there, between the Self and the *Śrīcakra*, is a triangle.
Having drawn a hexagon, a circle, and a square, one should worship within the square with the mantras: "Oṃ, salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha;
salutation to Uḍḍiyāna-pīṭha; salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha; salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha.
Then, having worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the six corners, [one should worship] at the tip of the triangle with the three *kuṭas*.

Having worshipped [the deities] in the outer [circles], and having worshipped the *ādhāra-śaktis* in the center, one should install the *yantra*—which contains a triangle and is adorned with six corners—within the womb of the [central] triangle. Having sprinkled it with water from the general *arghya* vessel while uttering "Namaḥ," [one recites]:
"Oṃ rāṃ rīṃ rūṃraiṃ rauṃ raḥ ramala-varayūṃ! To the fire-maṇḍala, the bestower of dharma, consisting of ten lotuses..."

Having worshipped the special *arghya* seat with "Oṃ aiṃ, obeisance to the special *arghya* seat," [one worships the fires]: "Yaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrārciḥ; Raṃ, obeisance to Ūṣmā; Laṃ, obeisance to Jvalinī; Vaṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī; Śaṃ, obeisance to Vi..."
